title: Topology of a Smile: Persistent Homology in Dental Imaging
summary: CBCT (Cone Beam Computed Tomography) scans provide detailed three-dimensional images, widely used in dentistry for diagnostic and treatment planning tasks. While invaluable, analyzing and documenting these scans is labor-intensive, prompting efforts to automate key steps like the classification and segmentation of anatomical structures to identify tooth types and associated pathologies. In this article, we propose an approach to automation that leverages persistent homology, a framework from topological data analysis that studies the shape of data by identifying features like connected components, holes, and voids across multiple scales. Persistent homology, together with a support vector machine, allows us to classify teeth in a CBCT scan and to perform diagnostics. Our method advances the state of the art, reaching average accuracy scores of 97.67% for tooth-labeling and 96.77% for diagnostic tasks, outperforming a CNN trained on the same data with accuracy of 70.27% and 86.67%, respectively.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a topological data analysis approach using persistent homology combined with a support vector machine to automate tooth classification and pathology diagnosis in CBCT dental scans, achieving 97.67% accuracy for tooth-labeling and 96.77% for diagnostics, outperforming a CNN baseline (70.27% and 86.67%).
AI.motivation: Analyzing and documenting CBCT scans is labor-intensive, and automating key steps like classification and segmentation of anatomical structures would reduce manual burden in dental diagnostic and treatment planning workflows.
AI.method: The approach leverages persistent homology from topological data analysis to extract multi-scale shape features (connected components, holes, voids) from CBCT scans, then feeds these topological signatures into a support vector machine for tooth type classification and pathology diagnosis.
AI.result: Average accuracy of 97.67% for tooth-labeling and 96.77% for diagnostic tasks, outperforming a CNN trained on the same data which achieved 70.27% and 86.67% accuracy respectively.
AI.conclusion: Persistent homology combined with SVM advances the state of the art in automated CBCT tooth classification and diagnostics, significantly surpassing CNN-based approaches on the same dataset.

title: EditStream: A Unified Autoregressive Framework for Interactive Video Generation and Editing
summary: Interactive video generation and editing are becoming increasingly important for creative design. In this report, we introduce EditStream: a unified framework for interactive video generation and editing. EditStream unifies multiple video creation and manipulation tasks within a single DiT-based model through flexible task-specific conditioning, and further transforms it into a fast, few-step autoregressive model for efficient streaming. It supports Text-to-Video, Image-to-Video, Video-to-Video, Editing Propagation, Reference-guided Video Editing, and Camera Pose Change, enabling flexible control over video generation, transformation, and editing within one system. To make the unified model practical for interactive use, we develop a two-stage distillation approach that combines Velocity Moment Matching (VMM) with autoregressive unrolling. VMM matches conditional velocity moments at student-reached intermediate states to preserve generation quality and motion, while unrolling exposes the student to its own autoregressive predictions to improve temporal stability. Together, they alleviate common challenges in few-step autoregressive video generation, including over-saturation, degraded motion, temporal instability, and complex training. EditStream provides a practical and scalable solution that bridges high-quality diffusion-based video models with interactive creative workflows.

AI.tldr: EditStream is a unified DiT-based framework for interactive video generation and editing, supporting six tasks (Text-to-Video, Image-to-Video, Video-to-Video, Editing Propagation, Reference-guided Video Editing, Camera Pose Change) via flexible task-specific conditioning, and is transformed into a fast few-step autoregressive model through a two-stage distillation combining Velocity Moment Matching (VMM) with autoregressive unrolling.
AI.motivation: Interactive video generation and editing are becoming increasingly important for creative design, yet existing methods are fragmented across separate tasks and diffusion models are too slow for interactive use. There is a need for a unified, efficient framework that can handle multiple video creation and manipulation tasks in real-time.
AI.method: The framework unifies multiple video tasks within a single DiT-based model using flexible task-specific conditioning. It employs a two-stage distillation approach: (1) Velocity Moment Matching (VMM) matches conditional velocity moments at student-reached intermediate states to preserve generation quality and motion; (2) autoregressive unrolling exposes the student to its own predictions to improve temporal stability. Together these address challenges in few-step autoregressive video generation such as over-saturation, degraded motion, temporal instability, and complex training.
AI.result: EditStream produces a practical and scalable solution that bridges high-quality diffusion-based video models with interactive creative workflows, alleviating common challenges in few-step autoregressive video generation including over-saturation, degraded motion, temporal instability, and training complexity.
AI.conclusion: EditStream provides a unified, efficient, and scalable framework for interactive video generation and editing, enabling flexible control over video generation, transformation, and editing within a single system while maintaining quality through a well-designed distillation strategy.

title: Aligning Human Sense: Calibrated Distributional Reward Learning for Video Generation
summary: Video generation is central to AI-powered content creation. Aligning generated videos with human preferences is a key criterion for evaluating generation quality. Despite significant progress in visual quality, three key challenges remain. First, the reliability of reward signals is constrained by the quality of human preference data, which is often affected by subjective noise and bias. Second, standard scalar reward models collapse multi-aspect human preferences into a single value, leading to the loss of dynamic trade-offs across multiple preference dimensions. Third, in policy optimization, the widely adopted KL divergence imposes primarily local constraints and may fail to capture the global structure of human preferences. To address these challenges, we propose a unified preference-aware learning framework for video generation. First, we introduce elite-guided filtering to calibrate preference data and construct reliable supervision for reward model training. We then model video quality as a multidimensional reward distribution to capture the uncertainty inherent in human preferences, and use the Wasserstein distance to align the learned reward distribution with the empirical human preference distribution. Finally, we introduce Wasserstein-based distributional alignment into GRPO, guiding policy optimization to better match the global structure of human preferences over videos. Experiments on reward modeling and video generation demonstrate that our approach improves the reliability of reward signals and the perceptual consistency of generated videos. Our code is available at https://github.com/alignhs26/ahs.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a unified preference-aware learning framework for video generation that addresses three key challenges: noisy human preference data, scalar reward models that collapse multi-dimensional preferences, and KL divergence's local constraints in policy optimization. The framework introduces elite-guided filtering to calibrate preference data, a multidimensional reward distribution modeled with Wasserstein distance for alignment, and Wasserstein-based distributional alignment integrated into GRPO for global preference matching.
AI.motivation: Aligning generated videos with human preferences is crucial for evaluating generation quality, but three challenges remain: (1) reward signals are unreliable due to noisy/biased human preference data, (2) scalar reward models lose dynamic trade-offs across multiple preference dimensions, and (3) KL divergence in policy optimization imposes only local constraints that fail to capture global preference structure.
AI.method: The framework has three components: (1) elite-guided filtering to calibrate preference data and build reliable supervision for reward model training; (2) modeling video quality as a multidimensional reward distribution capturing uncertainty in human preferences, using Wasserstein distance to align learned reward distribution with empirical human preference distribution; (3) integrating Wasserstein-based distributional alignment into GRPO to guide policy optimization toward matching the global structure of human preferences.
AI.result: Experiments on reward modeling and video generation show the approach improves the reliability of reward signals and the perceptual consistency of generated videos compared to baselines.
AI.conclusion: A unified preference-aware learning framework using elite-guided filtering, multidimensional reward distributions with Wasserstein alignment, and distributional GRPO can effectively address reliability, multi-aspect trade-offs, and global structure challenges in preference-aligned video generation.

title: AI Visual Inspection for Garment Production
summary:
The garment manufacturing industry is under increasing pressure to improve product quality, reduce costs, and accelerate digital transformation toward Industry 4.0. One of the most challenging quality-control activities is sewing-line inspection, where defects such as broken stitches and skipped stitches are difficult to detect consistently through manual inspection. Human-based inspection is often affected by fatigue, subjective judgement, and inconsistent performance, resulting in defect leakage, rework, and reduced production efficiency.
  This study presents the development and validation of an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based visual inspection system for garment sewing-line quality control. The system utilizes Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to detect sewing defects and was initially trained using black fabric and black sewing thread samples. Experimental testing was conducted on black, red, dark green, light blue, silver, and fluorescent yellow fabrics. The results demonstrated successful detection of jump sewing-line defects on black, red, and dark green materials, while performance limitations were observed for broken sewing-line defects and fabrics with significantly different visual characteristics, including light blue, silver, and fluorescent yellow colours. These findings indicate that model accuracy is strongly influenced by the diversity of training data and the ability to generalize across different fabric and thread colours.

AI.tldr: This study develops and validates a CNN-based AI visual inspection system for garment sewing-line defect detection, trained on black fabric/thread samples. Experimental testing shows successful detection on black, red, and dark green fabrics but performance limitations on broken-seam defects and fabrics with significantly different visual characteristics (light blue, silver, fluorescent yellow), highlighting that model accuracy depends on training data diversity and generalization capability.
AI.motivation: The garment manufacturing industry faces pressure to improve quality and digitalize toward Industry 4.0. Manual sewing-line inspection is unreliable due to fatigue, subjective judgment, and inconsistent performance, leading to defect leakage, rework, and reduced production efficiency. An automated AI-based inspection system is needed to overcome these limitations.
AI.method: The system uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) trained on black fabric and black sewing thread samples for visual inspection of sewing defects, specifically targeting broken stitches and skipped stitches. Experimental validation was conducted across six fabric colors: black, red, dark green, light blue, silver, and fluorescent yellow.
AI.result: The system successfully detected jump sewing-line defects on black, red, and dark green fabrics. However, performance limitations were observed for broken sewing-line defects and for fabrics with substantially different visual characteristics (light blue, silver, fluorescent yellow). Model accuracy was strongly influenced by training data diversity and generalization across colors.
AI.conclusion: The AI-based visual inspection system shows promise for garment sewing-line quality control but requires more diverse training data to improve generalization across different fabric and thread colors and different defect types. The findings emphasize that training data diversity is critical for robust performance in real-world manufacturing settings.

title: RoboShape: Information-Theoretic Point Cloud Representations for Privacy-Aware Robot Perception
summary: With the increased adoption of robotic agents operating in human environments by scanning and sharing 3D representations (e.g., for fleet learning, cloud-based planning, or collaborative mapping), collected point clouds reveal not just the objects in a scene but also sensitive spatial context, such as room function or information that occupants never consented to disclose. Traditional point cloud encoders offer no principled control over this: either all is preserved, or none. Hence, we introduce RoboShape, an information theory guided compression head following the frozen {\tt Sonata} encoder. We project voxel-level embeddings using the Donsker-Varadhan formulation of mutual information (MI). Specifically, we maximize the MI between embeddings and object-level understanding while minimizing it for private attributes. RoboShape leads to 87.5\% smaller embeddings that retain 98.7\% of object classification utility while collapsing sensitive attribute predictions by 39.3\% across the three real-world indoor LiDAR datasets. Its privacy-preserving embeddings are cheaper to transmit over the network or to train a model for any downstream tasks. We release the RoboShape codebase to give the robotics community a practical, encoder-agnostic tool for building perception pipelines that are compact, privacy-aware, and deployment-ready.

AI.tldr: RoboShape is an information-theoretic compression head for point cloud encoders that reduces embedding size by 87.5% while retaining 98.7% of object classification utility and collapsing sensitive attribute predictions by 39.3%, enabling privacy-preserving and compact robotic perception.
AI.motivation: Collected point clouds in robotic environments reveal sensitive spatial context (e.g., room function, unconsented occupant information) beyond the intended objects. Traditional point cloud encoders provide no principled control over what information is preserved versus suppressed.
AI.method: RoboShape uses a Donsker-Varadhan formulation of mutual information to guide a compression head placed after a frozen Sonata encoder. It projects voxel-level embeddings by maximizing MI with object-level understanding while minimizing MI with private attributes.
AI.result: 87.5% smaller embeddings, 98.7% retained object classification utility, 39.3% collapse in sensitive attribute predictions across three real-world indoor LiDAR datasets. Privacy-preserving embeddings are also cheaper to transmit and train downstream models on.
AI.conclusion: RoboShape provides a practical, encoder-agnostic tool for building perception pipelines that are compact, privacy-aware, and deployment-ready, with the codebase released to the robotics community.

title: Distinguishing Revision and Delayed Elaboration in Incremental Narrative Interpretation
comment: Accepted as a full paper for presentation at the 2026 Workshop on Computational Models of Narrative (CMN 2026). This preprint corresponds to the workshop version
summary:
Both human and AI systems that process narrative or long-form content operate incrementally: input is received over time, and internal representations must be updated accordingly. Incremental interpretation, therefore, depends not only on what is represented but also on how the representational state evolves under new evidence.
  We distinguish two structurally different update operators that arise in narrative interpretation: revision-driven update and delayed elaboration. Revision-driven updates retract or replace previously committed structure in response to a contradiction and are therefore non-monotonic. Delayed elaboration, by contrast, refines initially underspecified elements through constraint addition without retracting prior commitments, yielding monotonic extension of the interpretive state. Although both operators may alter how earlier material is understood, they impose fundamentally different structural requirements on state transitions.
  Using visual narratives as a diagnostic domain, we demonstrate how a structured narrative representation can explicitly separate committed from underspecified content and support both update operators during incremental construction. Through a worked example, we show how delayed elaboration enables monotonic refinement of interpretive state, while revision requires non-monotonic correction. We discuss the broader relevance of this structural distinction for incremental reasoning and hybrid symbolic-neural systems.

AI.tldr: This paper distinguishes two structurally different update operators in incremental narrative interpretation—revision-driven update (non-monotonic, retracts prior commitments) and delayed elaboration (monotonic, refines underspecified elements via constraint addition)—and demonstrates, using visual narratives, how a structured representation can explicitly separate committed from underspecified content to support both operators.
AI.motivation: Incremental interpretation of narrative content (in both humans and AI systems) depends not just on what is represented but on how representational states evolve under new evidence. The authors aim to articulate and empirically ground the structural distinction between two fundamentally different kinds of update operators required for incremental processing.
AI.method: The paper uses visual narratives as a diagnostic domain to demonstrate how a structured narrative representation can separate committed from underspecified content, and supports both update operators during incremental construction. A worked example shows delayed elaboration achieving monotonic refinement while revision requires non-monotonic correction.
AI.result: The paper demonstrates that delayed elaboration permits monotonic extension of the interpretive state by refining underspecified elements without retracting prior commitments, whereas revision-driven updates require non-monotonic retraction or replacement of committed structure in response to contradictions. These impose different structural requirements on state transitions.
AI.conclusion: The structural distinction between revision-driven updates and delayed elaboration has broader relevance for incremental reasoning and hybrid symbolic-neural systems, as it highlights the need for representations that explicitly track commitment status during incremental processing.

title: KVBoost: Chunk-Level Key-Value Cache Reuse with Deviation-Guided Recomputation for Efficient Large Language Model Inference
summary: Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) incur high prefill latency because key-value (KV) tensors must be recomputed for each request. Existing prefix-caching systems reduce this cost but require prompts to share a leading contiguous prefix, limiting effectiveness when shared content appears at arbitrary positions. We present KVBoost, a chunk-level KV cache reuse system for HuggingFace-compatible decoder models that enables reuse regardless of content position. KVBoost introduces a dual-hash keying scheme that separates positional identity (prefix hash) from content identity (content hash), supporting both exact and approximate cache matches. To address attention boundary errors from independently cached chunks, KVBoost employs two repair strategies: SelectiveRecompute, which re-encodes boundary regions, and CacheBlendRecompute, which identifies and recomputes high-deviation tokens after a probe pass. The system further incorporates asymmetric KV quantization (int8/int4), adaptive chunk boundary splitting, and importance-weighted eviction under a fixed memory budget. Evaluated on Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B over 1,000 bug-localization samples, KVBoost achieves a 4.49x reduction in time-to-first-token (142.4 ms vs.\ 639.1 ms) and outperforms prefix caching by 16%, with no loss in accuracy (99.2% vs.\ 99.1%). KVBoost provides a practical, memory-bounded inference acceleration layer compatible with RoPE-based models without architectural modification.

AI.tldr: KVBoost is a chunk-level KV cache reuse system for HuggingFace-compatible decoder models that enables prefix-cache reuse regardless of content position. It uses a dual-hash keying scheme (prefix hash + content hash), two boundary repair strategies (SelectiveRecompute and CacheBlendRecompute), asymmetric KV quantization, adaptive chunk boundary splitting, and importance-weighted eviction. Evaluated on Qwen2.5-3B over 1,000 bug-localization samples, it achieves a 4.49x reduction in time-to-first-token with no accuracy loss.
AI.motivation: Transformer-based LLMs incur high prefill latency because KV tensors must be recomputed per request. Existing prefix-caching systems are limited because they require prompts to share a leading contiguous prefix, which restricts cache reuse when shared content appears at arbitrary positions in the prompt.
AI.method: KVBoost introduces: (1) a dual-hash keying scheme separating positional identity (prefix hash) from content identity (content hash) for both exact and approximate cache matches; (2) two attention boundary repair strategies—SelectiveRecompute (re-encoding boundary regions) and CacheBlendRecompute (identifying and recomputing high-deviation tokens after a probe pass); (3) asymmetric KV quantization (int8/int4); (4) adaptive chunk boundary splitting; and (5) importance-weighted eviction under a fixed memory budget.
AI.result: Evaluated on Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B over 1,000 bug-localization samples, KVBoost achieves a 4.49x reduction in time-to-first-token (142.4 ms vs 639.1 ms) and outperforms prefix caching by 16%, while maintaining accuracy (99.2% vs 99.1%).
AI.conclusion: KVBoost provides a practical, memory-bounded inference acceleration layer compatible with RoPE-based models that enables KV cache reuse at arbitrary content positions without requiring architectural modifications.

title: Few-Shot Cross-Dataset Adaptation for Tuberculosis Detection Using DenseNet
summary: Tuberculosis (TB) is one of the most common and dangerous bacterial ailments. Every year, it causes a large number of deaths worldwide. Although many deep learning models can detect tuberculosis from chest X-rays quite accurately, severe domain shift across datasets makes the task challenging. Different imaging protocols, patient demographics, and equipment across domains make the task of generalization difficult. In real-world settings, a model may perform well on one dataset but show a noticeable drop in performance when tested on another. In this work, we address this domain adaptation challenge through a few-shot scaling study. A controlled cross-dataset evaluation is presented in this paper using TBX11K as the source domain and the Mendeley TB dataset as the target domain. It is investigated how varying the number of target samples affects model performance under three training regimes: frozen backbone adaptation, full fine-tuning of a source-pretrained DenseNet121 model, and training from scratch. The results indicate that the model can perform well even with limited data and can achieve 98.36\% accuracy with just 75 labeled samples per class. The adaptation curves demonstrate how fine-tuning effectively mitigates domain shift. These findings establish full fine-tuning of pretrained models as a highly effective and practical strategy for mitigating domain shift in low-resource clinical deployment scenarios.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses domain shift in tuberculosis detection from chest X-rays through a few-shot scaling study, showing that full fine-tuning of a source-pretrained DenseNet121 model can achieve 98.36% accuracy with just 75 labeled target samples per class when adapting from TBX11K to the Mendeley TB dataset.
AI.motivation: TB is a major global health threat, and while deep learning models detect it well from chest X-rays, severe domain shift across datasets (caused by differing imaging protocols, patient demographics, and equipment) leads to significant performance drops when models generalize to new clinical settings.
AI.method: The authors conduct a controlled cross-dataset few-shot scaling study using TBX11K as the source domain and Mendeley TB as the target domain. They systematically vary the number of target samples and compare three training regimes: frozen backbone adaptation, full fine-tuning of a source-pretrained DenseNet121, and training from scratch.
AI.result: The model achieved 98.36% accuracy with only 75 labeled samples per class. The adaptation curves demonstrate that fine-tuning effectively mitigates domain shift, with full fine-tuning performing best even under extreme data scarcity.
AI.conclusion: Full fine-tuning of pretrained models is established as a highly effective and practical strategy for mitigating domain shift in low-resource clinical deployment scenarios, enabling strong performance with minimal labeled target data.

title: Multimodal-Language-Model-Driven Interaction and Companionship for Service Robots in Elderly-Care Facilities
comment: Accepted to the 2026 IEEE/ASME International Conference on Advanced Intelligent Mechatronics (AIM)
summary: Service robots are increasingly deployed in elderly-care facilities to alleviate caregiver workload and enhance the quality of daily care. However, most existing studies focus on isolated service functions and lack integrated capabilities for continuous companionship, natural interaction, and safety monitoring. In this paper, we present an intelligent companion robot system that unifies active visual human-following, real-time LLM-driven speech interaction for intent understanding and task execution, and VLM-based safety monitoring for fall detection and abnormal posture assessment. The perception layer ensures robust human tracking and uses an active gimbal to maintain the user in view during occlusions or abrupt movements. At the interaction layer, a Large Language Model interprets spoken requests and maps them to robot actions, enabling escorting and semantic navigation. Simultaneously, a VLM-based safety agent continuously analyzes visual observations to detect fall-related or abnormal postures and triggers emergency responses when necessary. Experimental results demonstrate the system's ability to reliably follow and interact with humans, while effectively detecting potential falls to ensure user safety.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an intelligent companion robot system for elderly-care facilities that unifies active visual human-following, LLM-driven speech interaction, and VLM-based safety monitoring for fall detection and abnormal posture assessment.
AI.motivation: Existing service robots in elderly care focus on isolated service functions and lack integrated capabilities for continuous companionship, natural interaction, and safety monitoring.
AI.method: The system comprises: (1) a perception layer using active visual human-following with a gimbal to maintain user tracking during occlusions or abrupt movements; (2) an interaction layer where a Large Language Model interprets spoken requests and maps them to robot actions for escorting and semantic navigation; and (3) a safety agent using a VLM that continuously analyzes visual observations to detect fall-related or abnormal postures and triggers emergency responses.
AI.result: Experimental results demonstrate the system's ability to reliably follow and interact with humans while effectively detecting potential falls to ensure user safety.
AI.conclusion: The system successfully integrates companionship, natural interaction, and safety monitoring into a unified robot platform, addressing the gap in multi-functional elderly-care service robots.

title: KSE-Web: An Analysis of Hybrid Retrieval and LLM-Assisted Query Expansion for Low-Resource Khmer Semantic Search
summary: As a low-resource language, Khmer presents several retrieval challenges, including limited annotated data, ambiguous word boundaries, weak support in multilingual embedding models, and frequent mixed Khmer-English usage. This paper presents KSE-Web, an analysis of hybrid retrieval and LLM-assisted query expansion for Khmer semantic search. We construct the dataset from approximately 17K candidate Khmer titles and retain 3K cleaned full-text Khmer documents after filtering, normalization, deduplication, and document-length control. The dataset includes 300 manually reviewed user-style Khmer search queries and silver relevance labels with partial human verification. We evaluate character n-gram BM25, multilingual dense retrieval, hybrid BM25+dense retrieval, and LLM-assisted query expansion using Qwen2.5 models. Experimental results show that BM25 achieves the strongest overall performance, reaching 0.943 Recall and 0.876 nDCG. Hybrid BM25+dense retrieval performs comparably, achieving 0.929 Recall and 0.871 nDCG, while dense retrieval alone performs lower. LLM-assisted query expansion does not outperform non-expanded retrieval; however, Qwen2.5-3B produces substantially stronger expanded-query results than Qwen2.5-0.5B, suggesting that LLM size and expansion quality matter for low-resource Khmer retrieval. Our analysis further shows that direct LLM expansion can introduce topic drift, generic terms, and noisy reformulations, while simple filtering may remove useful semantic cues. These findings highlight both the potential and limitations of LLM-assisted retrieval for Khmer semantic search and provide a foundation for future Khmer retrieval datasets with stronger human-verified annotations and Khmer-aware retrieval models. The dataset and documentation will be made available at github.com/back-kh/KhmerSemantic-Search.

AI.tldr: KSE-Web is a new Khmer semantic search dataset (3K cleaned documents, 300 manually reviewed queries) evaluating BM25, dense, hybrid retrieval, and LLM-assisted query expansion. BM25 performs best (0.943 Recall, 0.876 nDCG), hybrid is comparable, and LLM query expansion underperforms—though larger LLMs (Qwen2.5-3B) produce better expansions than smaller ones.
AI.motivation: Khmer, as a low-resource language, suffers from limited annotated data, ambiguous word boundaries, weak multilingual embedding support, and frequent code-mixing with English. There is a need for dedicated analysis and datasets for Khmer semantic search, particularly regarding hybrid retrieval and LLM-assisted techniques.
AI.method: The authors construct a dataset from ~17K candidate Khmer titles, filtering down to 3K cleaned full-text documents via deduplication, normalization, and length control. They create 300 manual user-style queries with silver relevance labels partially human-verified. They evaluate character n-gram BM25, multilingual dense retrieval, hybrid BM25+dense, and LLM-assisted query expansion using Qwen2.5-0.5B and Qwen2.5-3B.
AI.result: BM25 achieves the best overall performance (0.943 Recall, 0.876 nDCG). Hybrid BM25+dense performs comparably (0.929 Recall, 0.871 nDCG). Dense retrieval alone performs lower. LLM-assisted query expansion does not outperform non-expanded retrieval; however, Qwen2.5-3B significantly outperforms Qwen2.5-0.5B for expanded queries. LLM expansion risks topic drift, generic terms, and noisy reformulations.
AI.conclusion: The findings demonstrate that traditional lexical retrieval remains highly competitive for low-resource Khmer, while LLM-assisted expansion has potential but needs better control to avoid semantic degradation. The work establishes a foundation for future Khmer retrieval datasets with stronger human verification and Khmer-aware models. The dataset is publicly released.

title: AIREP: A Protocol for Per-Decision Evidence in AI Runtime Governance
comment: 8 pages. Reference implementation and two-verifier conformance kit: https://github.com/halvrenofviryel/ai-runtime-evidence-protocol
summary: A protocol is presented for recording the governance decisions of automated AI runtimes. When a runtime releases, blocks, defers, redacts, or escalates an individual output, AIREP records that decision as a single signed object that any party can check offline, independent of the runtime that produced it. A record carries the decision as one of a closed set of verbs under a stated policy basis, references its input, output, and evidence by hash rather than by value, and declares both what its evidence covers and what it does not. Records form a SHA-256 hash chain that binds each record to its position, so that tampering and gaps are detectable by recomputation. Vendor-, model-, and domain-specific content is confined to a single optional namespace, and a mechanical neutrality test keeps the shared format free of it. A reference implementation and a two-language conformance kit are described. Some implementation issues are considered, and problems such as alignment of the canonical form across implementations, freshness witnesses, and multi-runtime chains are exposed. The format is offered for adoption by any AI runtime that records governance decisions.

AI.tldr: This paper presents AIREP, a protocol for recording governance decisions of automated AI runtimes. It defines a standardized, signed record format capturing actions (release, block, defer, redact, escalate) under policy bases, using hash references instead of values, and links records into a SHA-256 hash chain for tamper/gap detection. The format stays vendor/domain-neutral via an optional namespace and a mechanical neutrality test, with a reference implementation and two-language conformance kit provided.
AI.motivation: As AI runtimes increasingly make automated governance decisions about outputs, there is a need for a standard, auditable, and offline-verifiable record format so that any party can independently check these decisions without depending on the runtime that produced them.
AI.method: The protocol defines signed records with a closed set of governance verbs under a stated policy basis. It stores inputs, outputs, and evidence by hash rather than value, declares evidence coverage (and gaps), and chains records via SHA-256 hashes to bind positions and enable detection of tampering and gaps. Vendor/model/domain specifics are confined to a single optional namespace with a mechanical neutrality test. A reference implementation and two-language conformance kit validate the format.
AI.result: A reference implementation and a two-language conformance kit were produced. Implementation issues were identified, including alignment of canonical form across implementations, freshness witnesses, and multi-runtime chains. The format is offered for adoption by any AI runtime recording governance decisions.
AI.conclusion: AIREP provides a workable, open, and neutral standard for recording and auditing AI governance decisions offline. Despite remaining implementation challenges (canonical form alignment, freshness witnesses, multi-runtime chains), the protocol is presented as ready for adoption by AI runtimes.

title: Measuring Gender Representation in Animated Films
summary: Animated films--often developed with an audience of children in mind--are an important vector for enculturation, and empirical work that has examined the representation of gender at scale in these films has largely focused on counting the gender composition of the cast rather than deploying a more fine-grained instrument (such as assessing the visibility of those characters in overall screentime). In this work, we develop a computational pipeline for recognizing animated characters in these films, and use it to test several hypotheses about gender representation in a corpus of 224 popular animated movies. We find that while the overall representation of female characters in animated films largely tracks with those of live-action films (over the period 1980-2025), we see stark differences between the representation of human characters (much greater representation among women and girls) and non-humans (largely male). Contrary to past work on Disney, we do not see female characters declining in antagonist roles in animated films, and characters who are women and girls are much more likely to share scenes together than their live action contemporaneous counterparts.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a computational pipeline to recognize animated characters in films and analyzes gender representation in 224 popular animated movies (1980-2025), finding that while overall female representation tracks live-action trends, stark differences exist between human characters (more female representation) and non-human characters (largely male), contrary to past Disney-focused work, female characters do not decline in antagonist roles, and female characters are more likely to share scenes together than in live-action films.
AI.motivation: Animated films are important vectors for enculturation, especially for children, yet prior empirical work on gender representation in these films has relied primarily on basic counts of cast gender composition rather than more fine-grained measures such as character visibility in overall screentime.
AI.method: The authors develop a computational pipeline for recognizing animated characters in films and apply it to test hypotheses about gender representation across a corpus of 224 popular animated movies.
AI.result: Overall female representation in animated films largely tracks live-action films (1980-2025), but there are stark differences between human characters (much greater female representation) and non-human characters (largely male). Contrary to past Disney-focused work, female characters do not decline in antagonist roles, and women/girls are much more likely to share scenes together than their live-action counterparts.
AI.conclusion: Gender representation in animated films is more nuanced than previously understood; using fine-grained screentime-based measures reveals distinct patterns based on character type (human vs. non-human) and role, challenging prior findings from Disney-focused studies.

title: Gimbal-Based Human Tracking for Companion Robots Using Continual Learning
comment: Accepted to the 2026 IEEE/ASME International Conference on Advanced Intelligent Mechatronics (AIM)
summary: Reliable and continuous human tracking is essential for natural human-robot interaction, particularly for companion robots. However, many existing approaches rely on wearable tags or fixed cameras with limited fields of view, which reduces system flexibility and often causes tracking failures when the target moves outside the sensing range. In this paper, we present a human tracking approach based on a gimbal-mounted camera integrated into a mobile robot. By actively controlling the gimbal mechanism, the camera can dynamically adjust its viewing direction to maintain the target within the field of view, even under substantial relative motion between the robot and the human. Furthermore, a continual learning strategy is applied to the person re-identification (ReID) task to adapt to changes in appearance and environmental conditions during long-term tracking. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system significantly improves the stability and continuity of human tracking, enables real-time re-identification, and provides responsive feedback for reliable tracking of human motion from walking to running. User studies further indicate that the proposed approach enhances user comfort by eliminating the need for wearable tags.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a human tracking system for companion robots that uses a gimbal-mounted camera on a mobile robot to dynamically adjust its viewing angle, keeping the target within the field of view even during significant relative motion. A continual learning strategy is applied to person re-identification for adapting to appearance and environmental changes. Results show improved tracking stability and continuity, real-time re-identification from walking to running speeds, and enhanced user comfort without wearable tags.
AI.motivation: Existing human tracking approaches rely on wearable tags or fixed cameras with limited fields of view, which reduces flexibility and causes tracking failures when the target moves outside the sensing range. Companion robots require more reliable and continuous tracking for natural human-robot interaction.
AI.method: The approach uses a gimbal-mounted camera integrated into a mobile robot. The gimbal mechanism is actively controlled to adjust the camera's viewing direction, maintaining the target within the field of view under substantial relative motion. Additionally, a continual learning strategy is applied to person re-identification (ReID) to adapt to appearance and environmental changes during long-term tracking.
AI.result: Experimental results show significant improvement in tracking stability and continuity, real-time re-identification capability, and responsive feedback for tracking human motion from walking to running. User studies demonstrate that the approach enhances user comfort by eliminating the need for wearable tags.
AI.conclusion: The proposed gimbal-based active camera tracking system with continual learning for ReID provides a reliable, tag-free, and flexible human tracking solution for companion robots, effectively addressing the limitations of fixed cameras and wearable-tag-based approaches.

title: Wazobia Eval: A Benchmark for Nigerian Pidgin Emotion Understanding, Sarcasm Detection, and Cultural Reasoning
summary: Nigerian Pidgin is one of Africa's most widely spoken languages, yet remains severely underrepresented in language model evaluation. Existing benchmarks primarily focus on translation, transcription, or generic sentiment analysis, leaving critical aspects of culturally grounded language understanding unmeasured. We introduce Wazobia Eval, a benchmark for evaluating Nigerian Pidgin emotion understanding, sarcasm detection, and cultural reasoning. The benchmark is built on a manually annotated dataset containing over 550 examples and a 16-category emotion taxonomy designed to capture culturally specific emotional registers that are not represented in conventional sentiment frameworks. Wazobia Eval provides standardized evaluation protocols and benchmark tasks for assessing model performance on nuanced Nigerian language understanding. We present the benchmark design, annotation methodology, taxonomy development process, and preliminary pilot evaluation results. Our goal is to provide foundational evaluation infrastructure for Nigerian language AI and establish a reproducible benchmark for future research. The dataset is publicly available at https://huggingface.co/WAZOBIALABS.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Wazobia Eval, a benchmark for evaluating Nigerian Pidgin language models on emotion understanding, sarcasm detection, and cultural reasoning, built on a manually annotated dataset of over 550 examples with a 16-category culturally specific emotion taxonomy.
AI.motivation: Nigerian Pidgin is among Africa's most widely spoken languages but is severely underrepresented in language model evaluation. Existing benchmarks only cover translation, transcription, or generic sentiment analysis, leaving culturally grounded language understanding unmeasured.
AI.method: The authors construct a manually annotated dataset of over 550 examples, develop a 16-category emotion taxonomy designed to capture culturally specific emotional registers not represented in conventional sentiment frameworks, and provide standardized evaluation protocols and benchmark tasks for emotion understanding, sarcasm detection, and cultural reasoning.
AI.result: The paper presents the benchmark design, annotation methodology, taxonomy development process, and preliminary pilot evaluation results, along with a publicly available dataset at Hugging Face.
AI.conclusion: The goal is to provide foundational evaluation infrastructure for Nigerian language AI and establish a reproducible benchmark for future research on nuanced Nigerian language understanding.

title: Reviewing Model Collapse and Countermeasures
comment: 11 pages, 1 figure, Accepted and published in Proceedings of IEEE AAIML 2026
summary: Driven by massive amounts of web-scale data, generative AI (GenAI) has achieved remarkable progress, enabling various applications in diverse sectors. The advances of GenAI have actuated practitioners to use AI-synthesized data for training next-generation AI models. Undeniably, using synthetic data has alleviated the increasing stringent demand for data supply. Unfortunately, it also introduces a new critical issue: in a self-consuming cycle between model and data, the model ultimately collapse, raising more trustworthiness concerns to GenAI. In recent years, increasingly more studies have investigated the phenomenon of model collapse (MC) and explored potential solutions to mitigate it. However, the review of the phenomenon of MC still remains blank. To fill this gap, this paper provides an up-to-date overview of these studies for consolidating and reviewing the progress of MC in different application scenarios and countermeasures for mitigating MC. We also highlight challenges and future research opportunities.

AI.tldr: This paper provides an up-to-date overview of the model collapse (MC) phenomenon in generative AI, where models trained on AI-synthesized data in a self-consuming cycle become degenerate. It consolidates and reviews progress on MC across different application scenarios, explores countermeasures for mitigation, and highlights challenges and future research opportunities.
AI.motivation: While generative AI has achieved remarkable progress driven by web-scale data, the use of AI-synthesized data for training next-generation models introduces a critical issue: in a self-consuming cycle between model and data, the model ultimately collapses, raising trustworthiness concerns. Despite increasing studies investigating model collapse, no comprehensive review of the phenomenon exists.
AI.method: The paper conducts an up-to-date literature review that consolidates and reviews the progress of model collapse research across different application scenarios, alongside countermeasures for mitigating MC.
AI.result: The paper presents a consolidated overview of model collapse phenomena in various application scenarios, summarizes existing mitigation strategies, and identifies open challenges and future research directions.
AI.conclusion: The review fills the gap left by the absence of a consolidated review of model collapse, providing researchers with a structured understanding of MC across scenarios, mitigation approaches, and future opportunities.

title: Boosting Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering with Structured Context Reasoning
comment: Accepted by ICME 2026. Source code is available at https://github.com/WISLab-GDUT/SCoRe
summary: Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering aims to answer questions about an image by integrating external knowledge with visual and textual information. Recent approaches often rely on in-context learning to prompt Large Language Models (LLMs) with multimodal context in a zero-shot or few-shot manner. However, we observe that directly concatenating heterogeneous visual descriptions and retrieved knowledge into long, unstructured prompts often degrades reasoning performance, due to both excessive irrelevant context and the lack of explicit relational structure. In this paper, we propose an LLM-based Structured Context Reasoning (SCoRe) framework that infers both explicit and implicit relationships for prediction. SCoRe consists of three stages: Context Acquisition, which generates diverse visual notes and retrieves explicit knowledge via an efficient two-stage multimodal retrieval strategy; Context Selection, which filters relevant visual, explicit, and implicit knowledge using LLM-guided selection; and Context Compression, which performs Relational Logic Distillation (RLD) to transform raw text into explicit entity-relation triplets. These relational triplets serve as a concise and structured prompt for final answer prediction. Extensive experiments on the OK-VQA and A-OKVQA benchmarks demonstrate that SCoRe consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: SCoRe is an LLM-based framework for Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering that acquires, selects, and compresses multimodal context into structured entity-relation triplets, outperforming state-of-the-art methods on OK-VQA and A-OKVQA benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Directly concatenating heterogeneous visual descriptions and retrieved knowledge into long, unstructured prompts degrades reasoning performance due to excessive irrelevant context and the lack of explicit relational structure, motivating a structured approach.
AI.method: SCoRe consists of three stages: (1) Context Acquisition - generates diverse visual notes and retrieves explicit knowledge via a two-stage multimodal retrieval strategy; (2) Context Selection - filters relevant visual, explicit, and implicit knowledge using LLM-guided selection; (3) Context Compression - performs Relational Logic Distillation (RLD) to transform raw text into explicit entity-relation triplets used as concise structured prompts for final prediction.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on OK-VQA and A-OKVQA benchmarks demonstrate that SCoRe consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: Structured relational triplets from context acquisition, selection, and compression reduce prompt noise and enhance reasoning performance for knowledge-based VQA, surpassing existing approaches on standard benchmarks.

title: On the Optimized Use of Non-Orthonormality Constraints for the Quasi-Static INS Alignment of Autonomous Underwater and Surface Vehicles
summary: Inertial navigation systems are specialized navigation apparatuses that equip almost all autonomous underwater and surface vehicles. They require precise initial alignment, i.e., determination of their initial attitude, which is typically achieved: (a) in quasi-static conditions (whenever possible); and (b) in two stages: Coarse Alignment (CA), using methods like TRI-axis Attitude Determination (TRIAD), and Fine Alignment (FA), via Zero Velocity Update (ZVU)-based Extended Kalman Filtering (EKF). However, conventional methods suffer from slow convergence and limited bias estimability. In response, this paper introduces: (a) an optimized version of a recently proposed CA method, namely, TRIAD with Coarse Bias Estimation (TRIAD-CBE); and (b) a novel FA EKF observation model that incorporates Non-Orthonormality (NON) error constraints derived from TRIAD, directly linking these errors to the inertial sensor biases. As validated through extensive Monte Carlo (MC) simulations, as well as real-world experiments using two Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) of different grades, our approaches substantially accelerate the convergence of misalignment and bias estimates (from minutes to seconds), while maintaining accuracy/precision comparable to traditional techniques.

AI.tldr: This paper improves inertial navigation system initial alignment by optimizing TRIAD-based coarse alignment with coarse bias estimation and introducing a novel fine alignment EKF observation model with non-orthonormality error constraints.
AI.motivation: Conventional two-stage inertial navigation alignment methods (TRIAD coarse alignment plus ZVU-based EKF fine alignment) suffer from slow convergence and limited bias estimability.
AI.method: (a) An optimized TRIAD with Coarse Bias Estimation (TRIAD-CBE) for coarse alignment; (b) a novel fine alignment EKF observation model incorporating Non-Orthonormality (NON) error constraints derived from TRIAD, directly linking these errors to inertial sensor biases.
AI.result: Extensive Monte Carlo simulations and real-world experiments with two IMUs of different grades show convergence of misalignment and bias estimates accelerated from minutes to seconds with accuracy/precision comparable to traditional techniques.
AI.conclusion: The proposed coarse and fine alignment approaches substantially accelerate inertial alignment convergence while maintaining comparable accuracy to conventional methods.

title: On the Role of Citations in Preference Data
summary: Many NLP tasks require systems to provide attribution in their outputs--i.e. citations to grounding sources. Attribution serves as a bulwark against model hallucination and as a means for users to verify the credibility of model outputs. Yet, it is unclear how humans and LLMs evaluate citations when comparing outputs, a process central to reward modeling and modern LLM post-training. This paper studies the role of citations in the preferences of human judges and four open-source LLMs within the context of scientific question answering, leveraging mixed effects models to investigate the influence of citations on pairwise judgments. Among our key findings are (1) that humans prefer more diverse citations but fewer overall, and (2) that LLMs show some citation-related preferences compared to humans, despite lacking access to the sources, but these preferences depend on the data and specific models. We further discuss the implications of our findings for preference data collection.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how human judges and four open-source LLMs evaluate citations in pairwise comparisons for scientific question answering, using mixed effects models. Key findings show humans prefer fewer but more diverse citations, while LLMs exhibit citation-related preferences even without accessing sources, though these depend on data and model specifics.
AI.motivation: Attribution/citations are critical for combating hallucinations and enabling verification, but it is unclear how judges (humans and LLMs) actually evaluate citations when comparing outputs—a process central to reward modeling and LLM post-training.
AI.method: The study examines preferences of human judges and four open-source LLMs in pairwise comparisons within scientific question answering, using mixed effects models to isolate the influence of citations on judgments.
AI.result: (1) Humans prefer more diverse citations but fewer overall; (2) LLMs show some citation-related preferences compared to humans despite lacking access to the sources, though these preferences are dependent on the data and specific models.
AI.conclusion: The findings have implications for how preference data should be collected in NLP evaluation and reward modeling, particularly regarding the role of citation formatting and diversity in human and model judgments.

title: AI Learning and Conceptual Transfer in the Game of Hidden Rules
summary: This report summarizes the work conducted on the Game of Hidden Rules (GOHR), focusing on reinforcement learning agents trained to infer hidden rules from trial-and-error feedback, representation design, rule difficulty analysis, transfer learning, generalization, and pseudo-bot-assisted human learning analysis. The report focuses on the Transformer-based A2C framework, Feature-Centric and Object-Centric representations, experimental findings, and classification of human learning data.

AI.tldr: This report investigates Reinforcement Learning agents trained on the Game of Hidden Rules (GOHR), covering representation design (Transformer-based A2C with Feature-Centric and Object-Centric encodings), rule difficulty, transfer learning, generalization, and pseudo-bot-assisted human learning analysis.
AI.motivation: To understand how reinforcement learning agents can infer hidden rules through trial-and-error feedback, and to analyze rule difficulty, transfer learning, and generalization in this context.
AI.method: Transformer-based A2C framework with Feature-Centric and Object-Centric representations, experiments on rule difficulty, transfer learning, generalization, and classification of human learning data with pseudo-bot assistance.
AI.result: Experimental findings on representation effectiveness, rule difficulty analysis, transfer and generalization performance, and classification of human learning data.
AI.conclusion: The work provides insights into the effectiveness of different representation designs and frameworks for hidden rule inference in RL agents, with implications for human learning analysis.

title: DesignAgent3D: Interactive 3D Scene Editing via Designer-like Multimodal Reasoning
summary: Text guided 3D scene editing provides an intuitive interface for modifying reconstructed environments, but remains difficult because natural language design requests are often semantically underspecified and must be grounded in cluttered 3D scenes. Existing methods typically formulate the task as one-shot conditional generation from a single prompt, failing to resolve ambiguous user intents or achieve precise spatial grounding. Consequently, they suffer from severe object localization drift, tracking failure under occlusions, and the notorious multi-view "sticker effect." To overcome these limitations, we present DesignAgent3D, an interactive multimodal agentic framework that reformulates 3D scene editing as a designer-like Plan-Perceive-Act paradigm. The agent first plans by interacting with the user to clarify underspecified design goals, then perceives by grounding the intended edit to specific objects or regions in the 3D scene, and finally acts by applying controlled visual modifications while preserving scene consistency. The edits are further integrated into the underlying 3D representation, supporting persistent and multi-view consistent novel-view rendering. Extensive experiments across both NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting backbones demonstrate that DesignAgent3D significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, delivering superior semantic intent alignment, impeccable spatial localization accuracy, and high-fidelity multi-view consistency.

AI.tldr: DesignAgent3D is an interactive multimodal agentic framework that reformulates text-guided 3D scene editing as a Plan-Perceive-Act paradigm, addressing issues of semantic underspecification, object localization drift, occlusion tracking failure, and multi-view "sticker effect" in existing one-shot conditional generation methods.
AI.motivation: Existing text-guided 3D scene editing methods formulate the task as one-shot conditional generation from a single prompt, which fails to resolve ambiguous user intents and achieve precise spatial grounding in cluttered 3D scenes, leading to object localization drift, tracking failures under occlusions, and multi-view inconsistency.
AI.method: The framework employs a designer-like Plan-Perceive-Act paradigm: (1) Plan—interacts with the user to clarify underspecified design goals; (2) Perceive—grounds the intended edit to specific objects or regions in the 3D scene; (3) Act—applies controlled visual modifications while preserving scene consistency, with edits integrated into the underlying 3D representation for persistent, multi-view consistent rendering.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across both NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting backbones demonstrate that DesignAgent3D significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in semantic intent alignment, spatial localization accuracy, and multi-view consistency.
AI.conclusion: DesignAgent3D effectively overcomes the limitations of one-shot conditional editing by introducing interactive user clarification and explicit spatial grounding, achieving robust and consistent 3D scene editing across modern 3D representations.

title: ODG-NoMaD: Overhead-Camera Direction-Guided NoMaD
summary: NoMaD [31] is a learned vision-navigation policy that unifies goal-conditioned navigation and exploration in a single goal-masked diffusion policy. In an unseen environment, however - where neither a goal image nor a topological map is available - it can only explore undirectedly, wandering without global awareness. We present ODG-NoMaD, which gives NoMaD's exploration mode a global sense of where to proceed, without retraining the policy. An overhead depth camera is used once on deployment to build an occupancy map and plan a global path, which is segmented to yield a desired heading; a per-frame traversability map from the robot's onboard depth then refines this into a collision-free direction. The gradient of a cosine direction cost is injected into the final denoising steps, rotating sampled trajectories toward this direction while preserving the multimodality of exploration. In simulated office environments with and without random obstacles, ODG-NoMaD reduces the residual distance to the target by up to an order of magnitude over unguided exploration, outperforms the point-goal cost guidance of NaviDiffusor [37], and is the only configuration that remains collision-free on every trial.

AI.tldr: ODG-NoMaD enhances NoMaD's exploration mode with global direction guidance using an overhead depth camera for occupancy mapping and global path planning, plus onboard depth for local traversability, injecting a direction cost gradient during denoising—without retraining the policy.
AI.motivation: NoMaD unifies goal-conditioned navigation and exploration but in unseen environments without goals or maps, it explores undirectedly and lacks global awareness, wasting effort wandering without a sense of where to go.
AI.method: An overhead depth camera builds an occupancy map and plans a global path once at deployment; the path is segmented into a desired heading. A per-frame traversability map from onboard depth refines this into a collision-free direction. The gradient of a cosine direction cost is injected into the final denoising steps of the diffusion policy to rotate sampled trajectories toward the desired heading while preserving exploration multimodality. No retraining of NoMaD is required.
AI.result: In simulated office environments with and without random obstacles, ODG-NoMaD reduces residual distance to target by up to an order of magnitude over unguided exploration, outperforms NaviDiffusor's point-goal cost guidance, and is the only configuration that remains collision-free on every trial.
AI.conclusion: Providing global direction guidance via cost-guidance injection at inference time significantly improves the efficiency and safety of learned exploration policies without any retraining, offering a practical deployment-time enhancement.

title: Agentic Scaffolding Amplifies Sycophantic Behavior in Large Language Models
comment: 13 pages, 4 figures. Accepted to the UAI 2026 Workshop on Safe AI
summary: Sycophancy in large language models, the tendency to prioritize user agreement over truthful responses, has been documented extensively but studied primarily in single-turn settings. This paper investigates a critical question: does subjecting LLMs to greater interaction scaffolding make sycophancy better or worse? Across 4,800 veracity judgments (200 statements $\times$ 6 models $\times$ 4 conditions), we find that the interaction scaffolding characteristic of agentic systems (feedback loops, reconsideration checkpoints, and iterative refinement) systematically amplifies sycophantic behavior. Multi-turn interaction, user pressure, and iterative self-refinement each provide additional opportunities for models to drift toward agreement, and this drift coincides with a mean accuracy drop of $-6.3$ percentage points, establishing the capitulation as harmful rather than corrective. More capable models show larger amplification effects, a troubling inversion of expectations. We introduce the concept of agentic sycophancy amplification (ASA) and two novel metrics: capitulation rate and sycophantic capitulation rate. Our results indicate that as AI systems acquire greater autonomy, sycophancy becomes compounding rather than merely persistent. Systems designed with human oversight loops may inadvertently create the conditions for this drift.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether interaction scaffolding (multi-turn feedback loops, reconsideration checkpoints, and iterative refinement) in agentic LLM systems amplifies sycophancy. Across 4,800 veracity judgments (200 statements x 6 models x 4 conditions), scaffolding systematically increases sycophantic behavior, coinciding with a mean accuracy drop of -6.3 percentage points. The paper introduces agentic sycophancy amplification (ASA) and two new metrics (capitulation rate and sycophantic capitulation rate), showing that more capable models exhibit larger amplification effects.
AI.motivation: Sycophancy in LLMs has been documented extensively but studied primarily in single-turn settings. This paper asks whether the interaction scaffolding characteristic of agentic systems makes sycophancy better or worse—a critical question as AI systems gain greater autonomy and human oversight loops become common.
AI.method: The study uses 4,800 veracity judgments (200 statements × 6 models × 4 conditions) spanning multi-turn interaction, user pressure, and iterative self-refinement conditions. Two novel metrics—capitulation rate and sycophantic capitulation rate—are introduced to quantify drift toward agreement.
AI.result: Interaction scaffolding systematically amplifies sycophantic behavior. Mean accuracy drops by 6.3 percentage points, establishing the capitulation as harmful rather than corrective. Notably, more capable models show larger amplification effects, an inversion of expectations.
AI.conclusion: As AI systems acquire greater autonomy, sycophancy becomes compounding rather than merely persistent. Systems designed with human oversight loops may inadvertently create conditions for sycophantic drift, a critical concern for agentic system deployment.

title: LitReview Arena: Evaluating Literature Review Agents with Battle-Style Peer Review Platform
summary: Literature reviews are essential to scientific progress, but rigorously evaluating automatically generated reviews remains difficult because many aspects of research utility depend on expert judgment rather than reference-overlap metrics. We introduce LitReview Arena, a battle-style evaluation platform with a structured protocol tailored to literature review quality: domain experts with AI paper-writing experience compare anonymized drafts, are matched to topics within their expertise, and provide dimension-wise outcomes over five literature-review-specific criteria. From this protocol, we collect approximately 3k expert judgments, each containing five dimension-wise outcomes, and show that even the strongest current systems win only 23.0% of decisive matches against human drafts on overall utility, while agentic LLMs such as Sonar Deep Research substantially outperform base language models by over 60%. We further find that existing LLM-as-a-judge methods are substantially misaligned with human experts (Spearman's rho=0.467), especially on synthesis-heavy criteria such as paper structure and research suggestions. Using the collected preference data, we provide an expert-calibrated evaluator, LitJudge, which improves alignment to Spearman's rho=0.78, comparable to inter-expert consistency; code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/VanellopeAsher/LitReview-Arena.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces LitReview Arena, a battle-style evaluation platform for assessing automatically generated literature reviews using domain-expert judgments across five literature-review-specific criteria. From ~3k expert judgments, they find current systems win only 23.0% of decisive matches vs. human drafts on overall utility, and agentic LLMs outperform base models by over 60%. They also show LLM-as-a-judge methods misalign with experts (rho=0.467) and propose LitJudge, an expert-calibrated evaluator achieving rho=0.78, comparable to inter-expert consistency.
AI.motivation: Rigorously evaluating automatically generated literature reviews is difficult because reference-overlap metrics fail to capture research utility, which depends on expert judgment. Existing evaluation methods do not adequately reflect the nuanced, synthesis-heavy aspects of literature review quality.
AI.method: LitReview Arena uses a battle-style protocol where domain experts with AI paper-writing experience compare anonymized review drafts matched to their expertise, providing dimension-wise judgments across five literature-review-specific criteria. The paper collects ~3k such expert judgments and trains an expert-calibrated evaluator (LitJudge) on this preference data.
AI.result: Strongest current systems win only 23.0% of decisive matches against human drafts on overall utility; agentic LLMs (e.g., Sonar Deep Research) outperform base models by over 60%. LLM-as-a-judge shows poor alignment with human experts (rho=0.467), especially on synthesis-heavy criteria; LitJudge improves alignment to rho=0.78, comparable to inter-expert consistency.
AI.conclusion: The LitReview Arena provides a rigorous, expert-based evaluation benchmark for literature review generation, revealing significant gaps between current systems and human performance, and demonstrating that expert-calibrated evaluators can substantially improve alignment over generic LLM-as-a-judge approaches.

title: WorldMind: Decoupled Game World Model for State-Aware NPC Behavior
summary: Game world models have recently demonstrated promising capabilities in generating visually coherent and action-controllable gameplay videos. However, non-player character (NPC) behavior in existing models is either implicitly entangled with video generation or explicitly prescribed through external control signals. Consequently, a game world model has to jointly understand the state, plan the NPC's response and render its visual outcome, limiting its ability to produce responsive and state-aware NPC behavior. The challenge lies in the lack of an explicit interface for state-grounded decision-making. To this end, we introduce WorldMind, to our knowledge the first decoupled framework for state-aware NPC behavior in game world models. WorldMind separates interactive world modeling into four layers: an Understanding Layer that constructs a compact state from generated frames; a Decision Layer that reasons over the compact state to plan the NPC's next action; a Control Layer that translates the actions into temporally aligned conditions; and a Generation Layer that synthesizes their visual outcomes. By reconnecting layers in a closed interaction loop, WorldMind grounds NPC behavior in the evolving game state. We further introduce BOSS-140K, a dataset of gameplay videos paired with rich internal game states, together with an agent that automates the collection at scale. Experiments on BOSS-140K demonstrate reliable compact state reconstruction and mechanics-grounded planning, with WorldMind preferred over the baselines in approximately 70% of pairwise comparisons for its more tactically appropriate and coherent NPC behavior. Project page: https://teawhite.cn/worldmind_projectpage/

AI.tldr: WorldMind is a decoupled framework for state-aware NPC behavior in game world models, separating interactive world modeling into four layers (Understanding, Decision, Control, Generation) to explicitly ground NPC's actions in evolving game state. The authors also introduce BOSS-140K, a large-scale gameplay dataset with rich internal game states, demonstrating reliable state reconstruction and mechanics-grounded planning, with WorldMind preferred over baselines ~70% of the time.
AI.motivation: Existing game world models either implicitly entangle NPC behavior with video generation or explicitly prescribe it via external signals, forcing a single model to jointly understand state, plan NPC responses, and render outcomes. This limits responsiveness and state-awareness due to the lack of an explicit interface for state-grounded decision-making.
AI.method: WorldMind decouples interactive world modeling into four layers: an Understanding Layer constructing a compact state from generated frames, a Decision Layer reasoning over that state to plan NPC actions, a Control Layer translating actions into temporally aligned conditions, and a Generation Layer synthesizing visual outcomes. These layers are reconnected in a closed interaction loop. Additionally, BOSS-140K dataset and an automated collection agent are introduced.
AI.result: Experiments on BOSS-140K demonstrate reliable compact state reconstruction and mechanics-grounded planning. WorldMind was preferred over baselines in approximately 70% of pairwise comparisons for more tactically appropriate and coherent NPC behavior.
AI.conclusion: WorldMind provides the first decoupled framework for state-aware NPC behavior in game world models, demonstrating that separating state understanding, decision-making, action control, and generation improves NPC behavioral coherence and tactical appropriateness, supported by a large-scale dataset and automated collection pipeline.

title: Active Interaction-Aware Model Predictive Path Integral via Ego-Conditioned Generative Predictions
summary: Dense traffic is inherently interactive. The ego vehicle and surrounding agents continuously influence each other's reactions, making "what-if" reasoning essential for safe and efficient driving. To enable such an active interaction-aware behavior, we propose a planning framework that integrates an ego-conditioned generative autoregressive prediction model within Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control. The generative prediction model outputs stochastic, multi-modal predictions of surrounding agents conditioned on each of the ego's considered future actions. A nested sampling scheme enables tractable evaluation of expected cost and collision risk under the induced distribution. This formulation allows the ego to actively probe how different candidate actions shape the interaction outcomes and to identify actions that reduce ambiguity in uncertain interactions. Closed-loop simulations demonstrate improved safety and efficiency compared to conventional predict-then-plan and passive interaction-aware approaches.

AI.tldr: A planning framework combining an ego-conditioned generative autoregressive prediction model with MPPI control for dense traffic, enabling active interaction-aware "what-if" reasoning through nested sampling to evaluate expected costs and collision risks across candidate ego actions.
AI.motivation: Dense traffic is highly interactive, where ego and surrounding agents mutually influence each other's behavior. Conventional predict-then-plan and passive interaction-aware approaches are insufficient because they do not actively reason about how ego actions shape the reactions of other agents.
AI.method: The framework integrates an ego-conditioned generative autoregressive prediction model within Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control. The prediction model produces stochastic, multi-modal future trajectories of surrounding agents conditioned on each candidate ego action. A nested sampling scheme is used to tractably evaluate the expected cost and collision risk under the induced distribution over future outcomes.
AI.result: Closed-loop simulations show improved safety and efficiency compared to conventional predict-then-plan and passive interaction-aware baselines.
AI.conclusion: The ego-conditioned generative approach enables the planner to actively probe how candidate actions influence interaction outcomes and to identify actions that reduce ambiguity in uncertain traffic interactions, leading to safer and more efficient driving in dense, interactive scenarios.

title: Beyond Two Bytes per Letter: Tokenization Overhead in Cyrillic AI Systems
summary: Modern multilingual tokenizers often fragment Ukrainian and other underrepresented Cyrillic-script languages more heavily than English, creating disparities in cost and context capacity. We quantify this overhead across nine production tokenizers and five languages with standardized Cyrillic and Latin representations, covering 8.37 million word forms. On a corpus benchmark, Ukrainian shows 68-121% token overhead on modern tokenizers and 220% on the older cl100k, measured through full-text fertility on the BrUK and Brown corpora. Overhead is negatively associated with Cyrillic vocabulary allocation in the subset with independently verified English baselines, although the association is not statistically significant (Spearman rho = -0.536, p = 0.215, n = 7). We evaluate two mitigation strategies. LLMLingua-2 reduces Ukrainian input length by 47-49% on an e-commerce RAG benchmark of 1,536 products and 145 queries, with no compression-induced value losses among 80 retrievable cases. A balanced byte-level BPE tokenizer trained with a 200K vocabulary cap, converging at 158,184 actual entries, reduces the held-out UK/EN ratio from 2.22x to 1.30x. Romanization increases Ukrainian token counts by 2-19% on most tokenizers. Across the five languages, tokenization efficiency favors the script more prevalent in web data. These findings indicate that training data allocation contributes to Cyrillic tokenization overhead and that mitigation is possible at both inference and tokenizer-design stages.

AI.tldr: This paper quantifies tokenization overhead for Ukrainian and other Cyrillic-script languages across nine production tokenizers, finding 68-121% token overhead on modern tokenizers and 220% on cl100k compared to English. It evaluates two mitigation strategies: LLMLingua-2 for inference-time prompt compression (47-49% length reduction) and a balanced byte-level BPE tokenizer with a 200K vocab cap (reducing UK/EN ratio from 2.22x to 1.30x), attributing overhead primarily to training data allocation.
AI.motivation: Multilingual tokenizers disproportionately fragment underrepresented Cyrillic-script languages like Ukrainian compared to English, creating disparities in token cost, latency, and effective context capacity. The authors seek to quantify this overhead systematically and explore practical mitigation strategies at both inference and tokenizer-design levels.
AI.method: The study measures tokenization overhead (full-text fertility) across nine production tokenizers and five languages with standardized Cyrillic and Latin scripts, using the BrUK and Brown corpora covering 8.37 million word forms. It examines the correlation between overhead and Cyrillic vocabulary allocation (Spearman rho = -0.536), and evaluates two mitigation approaches: LLMLingua-2 for inference-time compression on an e-commerce RAG benchmark (1,536 products, 145 queries), and a balanced byte-level BPE tokenizer trained with a 200K vocabulary cap converging at 158,184 entries. Romanization effects on token counts are also assessed.
