AI.motivation: Existing world models typically handle single modalities (e.g., video only) and limited interaction paradigms, lacking the ability to enter generative media with synchronized audio-visual output and flexible trajectory control across both first- and third-person perspectives.
AI.method: EchoWM organizes interaction around camera intent, learning camera-character dynamics for third-person scenes from data. It maps discrete commands and continuous poses to a shared metric-scale relative 6-DoF trajectory with dataset-level calibration, and uses a complementary data engine plus progressive training followed by autoregressive post-training for joint audio-visual generation and trajectory control.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations demonstrate strong trajectory following and high visual quality on public world-model benchmarks, supporting both first- and third-person interaction across varied subjects while maintaining synchronized environmental sound and speech over long-horizon generation.
AI.conclusion: EchoWM establishes that an omnimodal, navigable world model is feasible and effective, unifying visual, audio, and movement control into a single enterable generative media framework.

title: Apodex 1.1: Scaling Agentic Intelligence for Complex Work
summary: General-purpose language models can reason and synthesize knowledge, but complex work also requires sustained interaction with files, information sources, and executable code, together with state maintenance, failure recovery, and verifiable delivery. We call this \emph{working capability}: sustained, verifiable progress toward a real-world objective. Apodex 1.1 develops this capability along two complementary dimensions. \emph{Environment Scaling} expands the diversity and verifiability of executable file, search, and code environments, while \emph{Agentic Coordination Scaling} trains agents to decompose long-horizon tasks, delegate parallel work, integrate asynchronous results, and replan. A shared execution harness and AgentOS maintain task state and provenance across tools and agents, and training turns environment trajectories and coordination traces into reliable behavior. Across complex professional work, finance, scientific research, mathematics, coding, and search, Apodex 1.1 reaches the leading performance band despite using a substantially smaller model than many frontier systems. The 35B-parameter Apodex 1.1 Mini further retains strong working capability in a locally deployable form. These results ground agentic intelligence in useful, verifiable work completed over time and advance our goal of building a \emph{Heavy-Duty Solver} for ambitious, long-running tasks.

AI.tldr: Apodex 1.1 is a language model system developed for "working capability"—sustained, verifiable progress on complex real-world objectives—via Environment Scaling (more diverse and verifiable file/search/code environments) and Agentic Coordination Scaling (training agents to decompose tasks, delegate, integrate results, and replan). Despite being substantially smaller, it reaches leading performance across professional work, finance, science, math, coding, and search, with a 35B Mini variant retaining strong capability in a locally deployable form.
AI.motivation: General-purpose language models can reason and synthesize knowledge, but they lack the ability to sustain long-horizon work involving interaction with files, information sources, and executable code, along with state maintenance, failure recovery, and verifiable delivery—capabilities collectively termed "working capability" that are essential for real-world tasks.
AI.method: The paper introduces two complementary scaling dimensions: Environment Scaling expands the diversity and verifiability of executable file, search, and code environments; Agentic Coordination Scaling trains agents to decompose long-horizon tasks, delegate parallel work, integrate asynchronous results, and replan. A shared execution harness and AgentOS maintain task state and provenance across tools and agents, and training converts environment trajectories and coordination traces into reliable behavior.
AI.result: Apodex 1.1 reaches the leading performance band across complex professional work, finance, scientific research, mathematics, coding, and search, despite using a substantially smaller model than many frontier systems. The 35B-parameter Apodex 1.1 Mini also retains strong working capability in a locally deployable form.
AI.conclusion: The results ground agentic intelligence in useful, verifiable work completed over time and advance the goal of building a "Heavy-Duty Solver" for ambitious, long-running tasks.

title: Toward a Foundation Plug-and-Play Prior for Computed Tomography Reconstruction via a Multimodal Diffusion Model
summary: Computed tomography (CT) throughput is limited by scan time, which grows with both the number of projections acquired and the detector integration time for each. Reconstructing high-quality volumes from sparse-view or low-dose measurements therefore depends on an informative prior, typically a neural network trained for one specific scan setting and retrained whenever the modality, geometry, or material changes. We investigate whether a single diffusion model trained across several imaging domains can instead serve as a prior for many CT problems simultaneously. We evaluate the proposed method using the same frozen model on three datasets that differ in modality, beam geometry, material, and degradation type, spanning flaw analysis in additively manufactured metal parts imaged with cone-beam X-ray CT and concrete microstructure imaged with parallel-beam neutron CT. Our proposed method out-performs analytic reconstructions in all three cases, providing a step toward a reusable foundation prior for heterogeneous CT reconstruction problems.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates using a single diffusion model trained across multiple imaging domains as a universal prior for heterogeneous CT reconstruction problems, demonstrating that a frozen model can serve diverse scenarios (cone-beam X-ray CT for metal flaw analysis, parallel-beam neutron CT for concrete microstructure) and outperform analytic reconstructions.
AI.motivation: CT reconstruction quality depends on informative priors, typically neural networks trained for one specific scan setting that must be retrained for every new modality, geometry, or material. This limits scalability and reuse. The authors ask whether a single diffusion model trained across several imaging domains can serve as a reusable prior for many CT problems simultaneously.
AI.method: A single diffusion model is trained across multiple imaging domains and then used as a frozen prior for reconstructing CT volumes from sparse-view or low-dose measurements. The method is evaluated on three datasets differing in modality (X-ray vs. neutron CT), beam geometry (cone-beam vs. parallel-beam), material (additively manufactured metal vs. concrete), and degradation type.
AI.result: The proposed method outperforms analytic reconstructions in all three evaluated cases, spanning flaw analysis in additively manufactured metal parts (cone-beam X-ray CT) and concrete microstructure imaging (parallel-beam neutron CT), all using the same frozen diffusion model.
AI.conclusion: A cross-domain frozen diffusion model can serve as an effective foundation prior for heterogeneous CT reconstruction problems, offering a step toward reusable priors that generalize across scan settings without retraining.

title: EviSafe: Evidence-Grounded Safety Evaluation for Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-language model safety benchmarks typically evaluate only final responses: whether a model refuses, warns, or complies. This outcome-level view cannot tell whether a model is safe for the right multimodal reason. Safelooking behavior may reflect keyword-triggered refusal, missed visual hazards, or over-refusal of benign-sensitive inputs. We introduce EviSafe, an evidence-grounded framework for VLM safety that jointly evaluates natural user-facing behavior, explicit grounding in textual and visual evidence, and behavioral sensitivity to counterfactual changes in safety-critical evidence. EviSafeBench instantiates the framework as a controlled benchmark with 1,181 gold image-text scenarios and 2,452 targeted counterfactual variants across eight safety domains and eight risk-source types. Each scenario includes a gold safety decision, evidence annotations, a safe-response policy, and counterfactual interventions. The three-probe protocol queries models with natural-response, evidencereporting, and counterfactual-response prompts, then scores them using an evidence-aware judge. Across eleven evaluated VLMs, natural severity accuracy ranges from 27.6% to 52.8%, relaxed diagnostic consistency from 6.1% to 29.3%, and unsafe-to-safe counterfactual transition success from 30.4% to 58.4%. These gaps show that the evaluated VLMs are not reliably safe for the right multimodal reason and motivate evaluation beyond refusal counts.

AI.tldr: EviSafe is an evidence-grounded framework for evaluating vision-language model (VLM) safety that goes beyond final-response outcomes to jointly assess natural user-facing behavior, explicit textual/visual evidence grounding, and behavioral sensitivity to counterfactual changes in safety-critical evidence. EviSafeBench provides 1,181 gold scenarios and 2,452 counterfactual variants across eight safety domains. Evaluations of eleven VLMs reveal significant gaps (natural severity accuracy 27.6–52.8%, diagnostic consistency 6.1–29.3%, counterfactual transition success 30.4–58.4%), showing models are not reliably safe for the right multimodal reasons.
AI.motivation: Existing VLM safety benchmarks only evaluate final responses (refuse, warn, comply), which cannot determine whether a model is safe for the correct multimodal reason. Safe-looking behavior may stem from keyword-triggered refusals, missed visual hazards, or over-refusal of benign-sensitive inputs.
AI.method: Introduces EviSafe, a framework jointly evaluating (1) natural user-facing behavior, (2) explicit grounding in textual and visual evidence, and (3) behavioral sensitivity to counterfactual changes in safety-critical evidence. EviSafeBench instantiates the framework with 1,181 gold image-text scenarios and 2,452 counterfactual variants across eight safety domains and eight risk-source types, using a three-probe protocol (natural-response, evidence-reporting, counterfactual-response prompts) scored by an evidence-aware judge.
AI.result: Across eleven evaluated VLMs: natural severity accuracy ranges 27.6%–52.8%, relaxed diagnostic consistency 6.1%–29.3%, and unsafe-to-safe counterfactual transition success 30.4%–58.4%, indicating substantial gaps in evidence-grounded safety reasoning.
AI.conclusion: The evaluated VLMs are not reliably safe for the right multimodal reasons, and evaluation must extend beyond simple refusal counts to evidence-grounded, counterfactual-aware assessment.

title: Learning Spherical Occupancy Profiles for Multi-View 3D Reconstruction and Generation
comment: 12 pages,5 figures,5 tables. Code and data will be released
summary: We study spherical occupancy profiles-the ray-wise occupancy probability profiles P(r) = T(r) o(r) distilled from multi-view 3D Gaussian reconstructions-as a unified intermediate representation for both discriminative and generative 3D reconstruction from images. On a 999-object subset of Google Scanned Objects with 48 turntable views each, we train (i) a discriminative per-ray decoder that injects global view-averaged and ray-specific image evidence into a FiLM-conditioned profile head, reaching median soft depth error 0.035 (normalized) on an independent 90-object test split, and (ii) a generative pipeline built on a profile VAE and a latent diffusion model, which supports unconditional sampling that matches the reconstruction manifold and image-conditioned multi-solution reconstruction whose per-object solution spread is quantifiable and tunable via classifier-free guidance. We further analyze the morphology of predicted profiles: post-hoc power sharpening and a learned sharpening target both recover ground-truth profile width without degrading depth, exposing a monotonic width-peak frontier in the L1-per-ray loss family and motivating a principled redefinition of morphology gates. Real-photo validation on two DTU scenes confirms the pipeline transfers to non-synthetic input. Our results suggest that ray-wise occupancy profiles offer a compact, learned, and uncertainty-aware interface between multi-view reconstruction and generative priors.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes spherical occupancy profiles—ray-wise occupancy probability distributions distilled from multi-view 3D Gaussian reconstructions—as a unified intermediate representation for both discriminative and generative 3D reconstruction from images. On a 999-object Google Scanned Objects subset, a discriminative FiLM-conditioned ray decoder achieves 0.035 median normalized soft depth error, while a generative pipeline (profile VAE + latent diffusion) supports unconditional sampling and image-conditioned multi-solution reconstruction with quantifiable, tunable spread via classifier-free guidance. Profile morphology analysis reveals a monotonic width-peak frontier in the L1-per-ray loss family, motivating principled redefinition of morphology gates. Real-photo validation on DTU scenes confirms transferability.
AI.motivation: To unify discriminative and generative 3D reconstruction tasks under a single compact, learned, uncertainty-aware intermediate representation, using ray-wise occupancy profiles distilled from 3D Gaussian reconstructions.
AI.method: Distill spherical occupancy profiles P(r) = T(r)o(r) from multi-view 3D Gaussian reconstructions. Train (i) a per-ray discriminative decoder that injects global view-averaged and ray-specific image evidence into a FiLM-conditioned profile head, and (ii) a generative pipeline consisting of a profile VAE combined with a latent diffusion model, supporting both unconditional sampling and image-conditioned generation via classifier-free guidance. Analyze profile morphology via post-hoc power sharpening and a learned sharpening target.
AI.result: Discriminative decoder achieves 0.035 median normalized soft depth error on an independent 90-object test split. Generative pipeline produces samples matching the reconstruction manifold with quantifiable and tunable per-object solution spread. Sharpening methods recover ground-truth profile width without degrading depth, exposing a monotonic width-peak frontier in the L1-per-ray loss family. Real-photo validation on two DTU scenes confirms transfer to non-synthetic input.
AI.conclusion: Ray-wise occupancy profiles serve as a compact, learned, and uncertainty-aware interface between multi-view reconstruction and generative priors, offering a unified framework for both discriminative depth estimation and controllable generative multi-solution reconstruction.

title: Agent-G$^2$: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: Hint-based reinforcement learning addresses reward sparsity in long-horizon agentic tasks by retaining a prefix of an expert trajectory before each rollout, letting the policy explore from a state closer to success. Its effectiveness hinges on the guidance depth: how much of the trajectory to keep. Existing methods treat this depth as a deterministic scalar. Scheduled approaches share one value across samples and ignore per-task heterogeneity; per-sample probing estimates it separately at the cost of extra rollouts. We find that useful guidance occupies a band of depths whose informativeness profile is approximately Gaussian around the band center, rather than concentrating at a single optimal point. We propose Agent-G$^2$, a Gaussian guidance framework that draws the depth per task from a Gaussian whose center and spread are estimated online from rollouts already collected for policy optimization, requiring no probe rollouts or learned depth predictor. The center combines a global baseline with per-cluster difficulty, and the spread tracks within-cluster variance. We evaluate Agent-G$^2$ on ALFWorld and WebShop on Qwen2.5-1.5B / 7B-Instruct. Agent-G$^2$ outperforms the strongest hint-based, hint-free, and Aux-RL baselines on ALFWorld by 2.3 / 3.9 / 7.4 points at under one-third the rollout cost of per-sample probing.

AI.tldr: Agent-G² is a Gaussian guidance framework for hint-based reinforcement learning that models per-task guidance depth as a Gaussian distribution (center and spread estimated online from existing rollouts), eliminating the need for probe rollouts or learned predictors. It outperforms baselines on ALFWorld and WebShop using Qwen2.5 models while reducing rollout cost to under one-third of per-sample probing.
AI.motivation: Existing hint-based RL methods treat guidance depth as a deterministic scalar (shared across samples or probed per-sample), ignoring per-task heterogeneity. This is suboptimal because useful guidance spans a band of depths with an approximately Gaussian informativeness profile rather than a single optimal point.
AI.method: Agent-G² draws the guidance depth per task from a Gaussian distribution. The center combines a global baseline with per-cluster difficulty, and the spread tracks within-cluster variance. Both parameters are estimated online from rollouts already collected for policy optimization, requiring no extra probe rollouts or learned depth predictors.
AI.result: On ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct, Agent-G² outperforms the strongest hint-based, hint-free, and Aux-RL baselines on ALFWorld by 2.3/3.9/7.4 points respectively, while using under one-third the rollout cost of per-sample probing.
AI.conclusion: Modeling guidance depth as a Gaussian distribution—rather than a deterministic scalar—better captures the band-like nature of informative guidance and yields superior performance at significantly lower computational cost than per-sample probing approaches.

title: Bee Detection and Tracking at Hive Entrance using YOLO11 and ByteTrack
summary: This work presents an automatic bee entrance monitoring system based on YOLO11 transfer learning and the ByteTrack tracking algorithm. The study investigates the influence of data augmentation, backbone freezing, and tracker parameter optimization on the detection and counting of small, fast-moving bees. The detector with progressive backbone unfreezing strategy achieved about 97.0% precision and 98.7% mAP50, while providing more stable convergence than full fine-tuning. Experiments also showed that light augmentation outperformed heavy augmentation. For tracking, ByteTrack parameters were optimized to improve trajectory continuity under low-confidence detections. On an independent 25 FPS side-view video, the optimized YOLO11-ByteTrack system correctly counted 43 of 47 incoming bees (91.5%) and 7 of 30 outgoing bees (23.3%). Error analysis showed that most counting errors were caused by missed detections due to rapid bee motion and motion blur, while tracking failures became less frequent after parameter optimization. Overall, the results indicate that moderate augmentation, progressive backbone unfreezing, and ByteTrack tuning improve the reliability of automatic bee entrance monitoring under realistic recording conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an automatic bee entrance monitoring system using YOLO11 transfer learning and ByteTrack tracking. The optimized system achieved 97.0% precision, 98.7% mAP50 for detection, and correctly counted 91.5% of incoming bees on an independent 25 FPS video, though outgoing bee counting was significantly lower at 23.3%.
AI.motivation: To improve the reliability of automatic bee entrance monitoring under realistic conditions, particularly addressing challenges of detecting and counting small, fast-moving bees with motion blur.
AI.method: The system combines YOLO11 with transfer learning and the ByteTrack algorithm. Key methodological choices include investigating data augmentation strategies, progressive backbone unfreezing versus full fine-tuning, and ByteTrack parameter optimization for low-confidence detection scenarios.
AI.result: Progressive backbone unfreezing achieved ~97.0% precision and 98.7% mAP50 with more stable convergence. Light augmentation outperformed heavy augmentation. On an independent 25 FPS side-view video, the system counted 43/47 incoming bees (91.5%) and 7/30 outgoing bees (23.3%). Most errors stemmed from missed detections due to rapid motion and motion blur.
AI.conclusion: Moderate augmentation, progressive backbone unfreezing, and ByteTrack tuning collectively improve the reliability of automatic bee entrance monitoring under realistic recording conditions, though outgoing bee counting remains a significant limitation.

title: Walking on the DARKSIDE
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) recognise patterns but do not natively track the path of exclusions that a coherent discourse demands. When an input rests on a fabricated authority, a misapplied mechanism, or a surreptitious analogy, an unsteered LLM tends to engage with it as if it were grounded, and to reify the misstep into any structured output it generates. Logic-Augmented Generation (LAG) with POLANYI++, an LLM-steering method that uses heuristics, ontologies and problem solving methods for tacit knowledge extraction, produces an Extended Knowledge Graph (XKG) in OWL2, but inherits the same vulnerability: a sophisticated nonsensical input is reified into the graph alongside the legitimate triples, and is hardly detectable by automated reasoners since the XKG is generated jointly with the wrong assumptions. We introduce DARKSIDE, a coherence auditing method on top of POLANYI++. It formalises the trail as an explicit data structure of accumulated exclusions over discourse time, complemented by a warrant axis that classifies each named referent as Warranted, Unattested, Misattributed or Fabricated, with an escalation rule that pushes the DelegationRiskAssessment to UNSAFE when the fabricated rate is positive or the unsupported rate exceeds a threshold. We evaluate DARKSIDE as a steering layer over a Gemini 3 on BSBench, a 100-item adversarial corpus of sophisticated-sounding nonsense across software engineering, finance, healthcare, physics and law, with Claude Sonnet 4.6 as an independent judge. The empirical evidence supports an architectural claim: when an LLM forward pass is wrapped in an ontology-mediated negative-trail apparatus, the structural pattern-vs-path gap can be partially scaffolded. The XKG functions as the missing memory, and the warrant axis as an epistemic firewall.

AI.tldr: DARKSIDE is a coherence auditing method layered on top of POLANYII++'s Logic-Augmented Generation (LAG) pipeline. It formalizes the discourse trail as an explicit data structure of accumulated exclusions, classifies named referents along a warrant axis (Warranted, Unattested, Misattributed, Fabricated), and escalates delegation risk to UNSAFE when fabrication or unsupported rates exceed thresholds. Evaluated on BSBench (100 adversarial nonsense items across 5 domains) with Gemini 3 and judged by Claude Sonnet 4.6, it demonstrates that an ontology-mediated negative-trail apparatus can partially bridge the pattern-vs-path gap in LLMs.
AI.motivation: LLMs reify fabricated authority, misapplied mechanisms, or surreptitious analogies into structured outputs like Extended Knowledge Graphs (XKGs), and this vulnerability is inherited by Logic-Augmented Generation systems such as POLANYI++ since the XKG is generated jointly with the wrong assumptions, making such errors nearly undetectable by automated reasoners. There is a need for a coherence auditing mechanism that explicitly tracks the path of exclusions in discourse.
AI.method: DARKSIDE formalizes the trail of accumulated exclusions over discourse time as an explicit data structure, and adds a warrant axis classifying each named referent into one of four categories: Warranted, Unattested, Misattributed, or Fabricated. An escalation rule raises DelegationRiskAssessment to UNSAFE when the fabricated rate is positive or the unsupported rate exceeds a threshold. It operates as a steering layer over a Gemini 3 LLM, evaluated on the BSBench adversarial corpus with Claude Sonnet 4.6 as an independent judge.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on BSBench (100 sophisticated-sounding nonsense items across software engineering, finance, healthcare, physics, and law) shows that wrapping an LLM forward pass in an ontology-mediated negative-trail apparatus can partially scaffold the structural pattern-vs-path gap. The XKG serves as the missing memory, and the warrant axis acts as an epistemic firewall.
AI.conclusion: The paper supports an architectural claim: representing the exclusion trail explicitly and layering a warrant-based epistemic assessment over an LLM can partially mitigate the reification of sophisticated nonsense into structured outputs, though the scaffolding is only partial rather than a complete solution.

title: BenthicDINO: Physics-Informed Self-Distillation for View-Invariant Side-Scan Sonar Representations
summary: Automated perception in side-scan sonar (SSS) imagery is severely hindered by physical acoustic artifacts, resulting in representations that inextricably mix intrinsic seabed reflectivity with transient viewing geometries. Existing self-supervised learning (SSL) frameworks rely on augmentations designed for natural images, failing to account for acoustic degradation and explicitly enforce view-invariance. To address this gap, we introduce a physics-informed self-distillation framework built upon the DINOv3 architecture utilizing a ConvNeXt-v2-Tiny backbone to maximize data efficiency. The proposed methodology enforces view-invariance through two primary mechanisms: physically motivated augmentations that simulate speckle noise, range-dependent attenuation, and radiometric miscalibration; and a Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC) penalty that explicitly decouples learned dense patch features from physical viewing parameters. Furthermore, we propose a dense, hierarchical feature fusion strategy across all four network stages to preserve fine-grained sediment details alongside deep semantic abstractions. Extensive evaluation demonstrates that the framework natively groups complex benthic topographies into stable, noise-free semantic clusters without relying on manual annotations. During supervised downstream tasks on the S3Seg dataset, the fused representations exhibited exceptional data efficiency, achieving 96% of its absolute peak performance using only 10% of the available annotated data, ultimately reaching a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 71.4% and an overall accuracy of 86.5%.

AI.tldr: A physics-informed self-distillation framework for side-scan sonar imagery, built on DINOv3 with a ConvNeXt-v2-Tiny backbone, using physically motivated augmentations and an HSIC penalty to enforce view-invariance, achieving 71.4% mIoU and 86.5% accuracy on S3Seg while reaching 96% of peak performance with only 10% of labeled data.
AI.motivation: Existing SSL frameworks for SSS imagery use augmentations designed for natural images, failing to account for acoustic artifacts (speckle noise, range-dependent attenuation, radiometric miscalibration) that mix seabed reflectivity with transient viewing geometries. This undermines view-invariance learning needed for robust automated perception in underwater sonar.
AI.method: A physics-informed self-distillation framework built on DINOv3 with a ConvNeXt-v2-Tiny backbone. View-invariance is enforced via (1) physically motivated augmentations simulating speckle noise, range-dependent attenuation, and radiometric miscalibration; and (2) an HSIC penalty that explicitly decouples dense patch features from physical viewing parameters. Additionally, a dense hierarchical feature fusion strategy across all four network stages preserves fine-grained sediment details alongside deep semantic abstractions.
AI.result: The framework natively groups complex benthic topographies into stable, noise-free semantic clusters without manual annotations. On the S3Seg dataset, fused representations achieved 96% of peak performance using only 10% of annotated data, with a final mIoU of 71.4% and overall accuracy of 86.5%.
AI.conclusion: Physics-informed self-distillation with explicit view-invariance constraints offers exceptional data efficiency and semantic clustering quality for SSS imagery, significantly outperforming natural-image-oriented SSL approaches in underwater acoustic perception tasks.

title: Measuring Stability and Failure Behavior in Language Models Under Structured Perturbations
summary: Language models are usually judged by a single accuracy score, which does not reveal how their performance degrades as inputs are perturbed. We present a graded, multi-family, failure-aware framework for stress-testing reasoning models. It perturbs each problem along a multi-level severity ladder across seven families: six that preserve the answer, paraphrase, input noise, formatting, irrelevant context, context load, and conflicting instructions, and a Knowledge Boundary family that removes answerability so that refusal becomes the correct response. Every test is validity-gated and labeled by its measured severity, and each model is summarized by per-level Accuracy, a magnitude-weighted Stability, and a per-family Collapse Point defined relative to the model's own baseline. Instantiated on the same 100 seed problems used by GSM-Symbolic, expanded into 4,473 gated tests and run on four models spanning capability tiers, the framework exposes structure that an aggregate score hides: the level at which a model fails is family-specific rather than global, and two stressors expose consistent weaknesses across all models: conflicting instructions and questions built on an impossible premise. Recognition of unanswerability is otherwise uneven, reliable on missing information and fabricated evidence but weak on impossible premises. These failure points are invisible to standard accuracy reporting.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a graded, multi-family, failure-aware stress-testing framework for reasoning models that systematically perturbs problems across seven families and multiple severity levels, revealing family-specific failure points that standard accuracy scores hide. Instantiating on 100 GSM-Symbolic seed problems expanded to 4,473 gated tests across four models, it shows conflicting instructions and impossible premises consistently break all models, while unanswerability recognition is uneven.
AI.motivation: Single accuracy scores do not reveal how language model performance degrades under input perturbations, masking critical failure points that are invisible to aggregate reporting.
AI.method: A graded, multi-family stress-testing framework that perturbs each problem along a multi-level severity ladder across seven families: six answer-preserving (paraphrase, input noise, formatting, irrelevant context, context load, conflicting instructions) and one Knowledge Boundary family that removes answerability. Tests are validity-gated and severity-labeled. Models are summarized by per-level Accuracy, magnitude-weighted Stability, and per-family Collapse Point relative to baseline.
AI.result: Applied to 100 seed problems (expanded to 4,473 gated tests) on four models across capability tiers, the framework shows failure levels are family-specific rather than global. Conflicting instructions and impossible-premise questions consistently break all models, while unanswerability recognition is reliable for missing information and fabricated evidence but weak on impossible premises.
AI.conclusion: Standard accuracy reporting hides critical failure structure; the proposed framework reveals that reasoning model degradation is family-specific, and identifies universal weak points (conflicting instructions and impossible premises) that require targeted attention.

title: Modalities Should Talk to Each Other: Dual-Stream Multimodal Learning for Long-Horizon Influenza Forecasting
summary: Forecasting long-range influenza-like illness (ILI) matters for public health readiness. Publicly available surveillance datasets typically pair numeric epidemiological signals with textual information that is noisy, loosely structured, only indirectly related to near-term trends, and often lagged relative to the numeric signal. Fusing the two therefore requires careful design. We propose Dual-Stream Attention (DSA), a multimodal deep learning framework that forecasts 12-week-ahead ILI activity from a 36-week multimodal history by letting the numerical and textual streams condition each other. Using the Time-MMD health-domain dataset, DSA separately encodes the two modalities with a Transformer-based numerical encoder and a domain-adapted headline encoder, then couples them through a bidirectional Cross-Modal Attention (CMA) mechanism: the text (news headlines) conditions the interpretation of the numeric signal and vice versa. The CMA output then passes to a causal temporal model for forecasting. Evaluated across ten random seeds, DSA achieves a median test MSE of 0.416, versus 0.668, 0.607, and 0.851 for iTransformer, TaTS, and GPT4MTS, corresponding to mean-error reductions of 54.95%, 37.29%, and 67.23%, with paired Cohen's d of 0.555, 0.337, and 0.345, respectively, and ranks first in 100% of bootstrap draws. It also has substantially lower worst-window error than all baselines. On an external-geography dataset, DSA again ranks first among nine evaluated baselines. Ablations show the advantage does not depend on text-encoder choice or language-model fine-tuning, and that bidirectional attention outperforms either direction alone. Finally, perturbation-based faithfulness analysis shows the learned CMA is functionally informative under targeted masking, with a stronger effect in the text-to-numerical direction.

AI.tldr: DSA is a multimodal deep learning framework that forecasts 12-week-ahead influenza-like illness (ILI) activity by fusing numeric epidemiological signals with noisy, lagged textual news headlines through bidirectional Cross-Modal Attention. It outperforms all baselines across internal and external datasets, with median test MSE of 0.416 versus 0.607-0.851 for strong baselines.
AI.motivation: Long-range ILI forecasting is important for public health readiness, but surveillance datasets pair numeric signals with noisy, loosely structured, indirectly related, and lagged textual information. Fusing these modalities requires careful design since naive integration fails to leverage their complementary value.
AI.method: DSA uses a Transformer-based numerical encoder and a domain-adapted headline encoder to separately encode the two modalities from a 36-week history, couples them through a bidirectional Cross-Modal Attention (CMA) mechanism where text conditions the interpretation of the numeric signal and vice versa, then passes the CMA output to a causal temporal model for 12-week-ahead forecasting.
AI.result: DSA achieves median test MSE of 0.416 versus 0.668, 0.607, and 0.851 for iTransformer, TaTS, and GPT4MTS (reductions of 54.95%, 37.29%, 67.23%), ranks first in 100% of bootstrap draws, has substantially lower worst-window error, and ranks first on an external-geography dataset. Ablations show robustness to text-encoder choice and fine-tuning, bidirectional attention superiority over unidirectional, and faithfulness via perturbation analysis.
AI.conclusion: Bidirectional cross-modal conditioning is an effective design for fusing noisy textual information with numeric epidemiological signals for long-horizon ILI forecasting, and the learned cross-modal attention is functionally informative rather than superficial.

title: MLLM-Assisted Audio VOS: A 3rd Place Report for the MeViS-Audio Track, 8th LSVOS Challenge
summary: In this technical report, we present a training-free framework for audio-guided video object segmentation, which integrates Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) with SAM-based segmentation models. We decompose the task into several stages and identify suitable foundation models for each stage. Without introducing additional model training or task-specific fine-tuning, our approach leverages the strong multimodal reasoning capabilities of MLLMs to model text-visual correspondence and employs SAM-based models for accurate object mask generation. The proposed framework demonstrates the effectiveness of leveraging foundation models for audio-guided video segmentation and achieves competitive performance in the MeViS-Audio Track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge.

AI.tldr: A training-free framework for audio-guided video object segmentation that combines Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) with SAM-based segmentation models, achieving competitive performance in the MeViS-Audio Track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge.
AI.motivation: To develop an audio-guided video object segmentation approach without requiring additional model training or task-specific fine-tuning, leveraging existing foundation models' capabilities.
AI.method: The task is decomposed into multiple stages, with suitable pre-trained foundation models selected for each stage. MLLMs handle text-visual correspondence for multimodal reasoning, while SAM-based models generate accurate object masks. The pipeline is training-free, relying entirely on off-the-shelf foundation models.
AI.result: The framework achieves competitive performance on the MeViS-Audio Track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge, demonstrating the effectiveness of leveraging foundation models for audio-guided video segmentation without fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: The proposed training-free approach successfully demonstrates that combining MLLMs with SAM-based segmentation models can effectively address audio-guided video object segmentation, providing a viable alternative to task-specific trained models.

title: Aggregation-Aware Synthetic Text Generation Against Authorship Re-Identification
comment: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
summary: Online users often release multiple texts under the same identity, giving attackers an author profile that can reveal more than any single text. Existing authorship obfuscation methods optimize privacy independently for each document, leaving them blind to cross-document correlations that make aggregation dangerous. We propose Aggregation-Aware Synthetic Text Generation (AAST), a framework that addresses this gap by jointly selecting synthetic texts at the bundle level rather than optimizing each text in isolation. AAST targets attribution and verification attacks, including cross-genre settings where attacker references come from a genre not observed during generation or selection. Experiments across same-genre, cross-genre, neural, and independent non-neural stylometric attacks show that AAST lowers account-level linkability as bundle size grows, while preserving semantic quality, linguistic acceptability, and sentiment alignment.

AI.tldr: AAST is a framework for aggregation-aware synthetic text generation that jointly optimizes bundles of texts to defend against authorship attribution and verification attacks, including cross-genre settings, outperforming existing single-document obfuscation methods.
AI.motivation: Online users publish multiple texts under the same identity, and attackers can aggregate these texts into an author profile that reveals more than any single document. Existing authorship obfuscation methods optimize privacy independently per document, failing to account for cross-document correlations that make aggregation dangerous.
AI.method: AAST jointly selects synthetic texts at the bundle level (rather than optimizing each text in isolation), targeting both attribution and verification attacks, including cross-genre scenarios where attacker references come from a genre not observed during generation or selection.
AI.result: Experiments across same-genre, cross-genre, neural, and independent non-neural stylometric attacks show that AAST lowers account-level linkability as bundle size grows, while preserving semantic quality, linguistic acceptability, and sentiment alignment.
AI.conclusion: Bundle-level or aggregation-aware optimization is essential for effective authorship obfuscation in multi-text settings, as it mitigates cross-document correlation risks without sacrificing text quality.

title: MediSkill-Evo: Process-Constrained Self-Evolution for Evidence-Grounded Clinical Interaction
summary: Interactive clinical agents operate under partial observability, so reliable care depends on reaching the correct diagnosis through evidence-grounded, safe interactions. Yet existing agents struggle to convert experience into reusable process knowledge with explicit provenance and authority. To address this gap, we introduce MediSkill-Evo, which self-evolves governed process knowledge without fine-tuning the backbone. It realizes this self-evolution by updating clinical, process, symbolic, and visual knowledge in four typed banks under type-specific validation and scope rules. The Process-Constrained Preference Harness then turns validated knowledge into action by grounding candidates in evidence and prioritizing safer decisions. We evaluate on 300 MIMIC-IV-derived FullChain encounters, 180 hard-isolation conditions covering six process obligations, and 100 multimodal NEJM image-diagnosis cases. On Qwen FullChain, MediSkill-Evo improves diagnosis accuracy by 7.81% and treatment-intent coverage by 70.67% over the best-performing prior agent, while reducing critical failures by 43.04%. Under stress, it improves the stress-process composite by 7.77% and required-action completion by 12.41% over the best-performing agent for each metric, with stronger patient-fact, temporal-evidence, and triage-red-flag recovery and no controller-scored errors in unavailable-evidence, treatment, and triage safety checks. On multimodal NEJM diagnosis, MediSkill-Evo with optional MedSAM localization improves diagnosis accuracy by 2.56% and core score by 18.96% over the best-performing memory agent. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/mediskill-evo_anonymous-68E7.

AI.tldr: MediSkill-Evo is a self-evolving interactive clinical agent that improves diagnosis and treatment safety by maintaining four typed knowledge banks (clinical, process, symbolic, visual) with type-specific validation and scope rules, plus a Process-Constrained Preference Harness for evidence-grounded action selection. It achieves significant gains over prior agents across FullChain, hard-isolation stress, and multimodal NEJM benchmarks without fine-tuning the backbone model.
AI.motivation: Interactive clinical agents operate under partial observability and must reach correct diagnoses through evidence-grounded, safe interactions; however, existing agents struggle to convert experience into reusable process knowledge that carries explicit provenance and authority.
AI.method: MediSkill-Evo self-evolves governed process knowledge without backbone fine-tuning by updating four typed knowledge banks (clinical, process, symbolic, visual) under type-specific validation and scope rules. A Process-Constrained Preference Harness grounds candidates in evidence and prioritizes safer decisions, converting validated knowledge into actionable behavior.
AI.result: On 300 MIMIC-IV FullChain encounters: +7.81% diagnosis accuracy and +70.67% treatment-intent coverage over best prior agent, with -43.04% critical failures. On 180 hard-isolation stress conditions: +7.77% stress-process composite and +12.41% required-action completion, with stronger recovery on patient-fact, temporal-evidence, and triage red flags, and zero controller-scored safety errors. On 100 multimodal NEJM cases: +2.56% diagnosis accuracy and +18.96% core score over best memory agent (optionally with MedSAM localization).
AI.conclusion: Self-evolving governed process knowledge with typed knowledge banks and evidence-constrained preference optimization enables safer, more accurate interactive clinical diagnosis without model fine-tuning, reducing critical failures while improving treatment coverage and multimodal performance.

title: Mover360: Controllable Object Manipulation in 360° Panoramic Images
summary: We present Mover360, a controllable object manipulation framework for 360° images. Unlike perspective images, 360° images in equirectangular projection (ERP) exhibit horizontal wrap-around, latitude-dependent distortion, and global scene continuity, which makes object-level edits difficult for existing perspective editors to produce and for users to specify. To address this, Mover360 centers on object Translation (relocating a specified object within an existing panorama) while supporting reference-guided Insert and Remove as auxiliary tasks. Its interface unifies point-, bbox-, and mask-guided control by encoding each task into a fixed prompt and a compact, ERP-aligned instruction map. In the default point mode, a single click relocates an object, allowing the model to infer a plausible size, support, and illumination using panoramic context and an auxiliary depth condition. Structurally, Mover360 is a lightweight adaptation of a pretrained diffusion transformer. To generate paired supervision, we construct a UE5 data-generation pipeline with surface-aware object placement and randomized illumination, yielding large-scale paired data and a dual-domain benchmark of synthetic and real panoramas with ground truth for all three tasks. Across both test domains and two evaluation protocols, Mover360 outperforms strong baselines for perspective editing, insertion, and inpainting in reconstruction fidelity, semantic consistency, and distributional quality. Code and our benchmark dataset are available at https://zhonghaoyi.github.io/Mover360/.

AI.tldr: Mover360 is a controllable object manipulation framework for 360° equirectangular images, focusing on object translation with reference-guided insert and remove as auxiliary tasks, built as a lightweight adaptation of a pretrained diffusion transformer with a UE5-based data pipeline.
AI.motivation: 360° images in equirectangular projection present unique challenges—horizontal wrap-around, latitude-dependent distortion, and global scene continuity—that make object-level editing difficult for existing perspective-based editors and hard for users to specify edits.
AI.method: Mover360 centers on object translation with auxiliary insert and remove tasks. Its interface unifies point-, bbox-, and mask-guided control through a fixed prompt and a compact, ERP-aligned instruction map. In default point mode, a single click relocates an object while inferring plausible size, support, and illumination from panoramic context and an auxiliary depth condition. The model is a lightweight adaptation of a pretrained diffusion transformer, trained on paired data generated by a UE5 pipeline with surface-aware placement and randomized illumination, yielding a dual-domain benchmark of synthetic and real panoramas with ground truth.
AI.result: Across both synthetic and real test domains and two evaluation protocols, Mover360 outperforms strong baselines for perspective editing, insertion, and inpainting in reconstruction fidelity, semantic consistency, and distributional quality.
AI.conclusion: Mover360 demonstrates that a lightweight adaptation of a pretrained diffusion transformer, coupled with a unified interface and UE5-generated paired training data, enables effective and controllable object manipulation in panoramic images, surpassing existing perspective-based approaches.

title: SkillAlchemy: Open-World Agent Skill Creation
summary: Agent skills are reusable procedural artifacts that extend language agents with specialized workflows, tool conventions, and domain behaviors at inference time. However, creating reliable skills still depends largely on human authorship, model priors, or execution traces. These sources are often unavailable for unfamiliar tasks, suggesting the need to create skills from open-world materials. In this paper, we study open-world skill creation: given an underspecified skill brief and a source-access specification, a creator must discover behavior-relevant requirements omitted by the brief and determine how broadly each source-derived procedure is justified. We propose SkillAlchemy, an admission-centered framework for source-grounded skill creation. SkillAlchemy identifies implicit requirements through contrastive evidence, admits candidate procedures based on evidence-supported scope, and compiles the admitted content into a grammar-guided skill package. Extensive experiments across 87 SkillsBench v1.1 tasks demonstrate that SkillAlchemy improves pass rate over no-skill execution by 19.9 percentage points and the strongest automated baseline by 8.6 percentage points, while achieving performance comparable to human-curated skills.

AI.tldr: SkillAlchemy is an admission-centered framework for creating reliable agent skills from open-world source materials, rather than relying on human authorship, model priors, or execution traces. It identifies implicit requirements via contrastive evidence, admits candidate procedures based on evidence-supported scope, and compiles them into grammar-guided skill packages, achieving a 19.9 percentage point pass rate improvement over no-skill execution and outperforming the strongest automated baseline by 8.6 percentage points on 87 SkillsBench v1.1 tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing methods for creating reliable agent skills depend on human authorship, model priors, or execution traces, which are often unavailable for unfamiliar tasks. This necessitates a method to create skills from open-world materials, addressing the open-world skill creation problem where underspecified skill briefs and source-access specifications require discovering behavior-relevant requirements omitted by the brief and determining the justified scope of each source-derived procedure.
AI.method: SkillAlchemy is an admission-centered framework with three key components: (1) identification of implicit requirements through contrastive evidence, (2) admission of candidate procedures based on evidence-supported scope to determine how broadly each source-derived procedure is justified, and (3) compilation of admitted content into a grammar-guided skill package for structured integration.
AI.result: On 87 SkillsBench v1.1 tasks, SkillAlchemy improves pass rate by 19.9 percentage points over no-skill execution and by 8.6 percentage points over the strongest automated baseline. It achieves performance comparable to human-curated skills.
AI.conclusion: Source-grounded skill creation from open-world materials is feasible and effective, with SkillAlchemy demonstrating that admission-centered frameworks can produce reliable skills rivaling human curation quality without requiring human authorship, model priors, or execution traces.

title: Semantic Reconstruction and 3-D Detection via Learned Multi-Pair Fusion in RF Imaging
summary: We consider a multistatic radio-frequency imaging problem with anisotropy, in which the reflection from a point depends on the positions of the transmit (Tx) and receive (Rx) arrays. The goal is to label the voxels of a field of view by a finite set of semantic classes and to group them into object instances. For the image formation of each Tx--Rx pair we apply a standard inverse-problem solver, and we feed the resulting per-pair reconstructions into a trained three-dimensional (3-D) U-Net that performs the fusion implicitly and the per-voxel classification explicitly. On a controlled, under-determined multistatic setup, we consider the following image formation methods: back-projection (BP) and the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) from a single deterministic snapshot, and incoherent BP and group-LASSO from multiple fading snapshots. For each imaging method we train a separate U-Net that fuses the six Tx--Rx pairs (its input channels) and assigns each voxel a probability vector over the classes. Taking the most probable class gives a labeled volume---the semantic reconstruction. Object instances and their oriented bounding boxes then follow by geometric post-processing (clustering and principal-component analysis). Across a wide range of signal-to-noise ratio, the semantic reconstruction (scored against ground truth by segmentation intersection-over-union) and the resulting 3-D detection degrade far more gracefully than the classical intensity reconstruction: the detection in particular stays reliable well into noise levels at which that reconstruction has dissolved. Because real scenes contain objects of classes the network was not trained on, we add an explicit unknown class trained by outlier exposure, which labels held-out novel objects as unknown instead of mislabeling them as a known class by reconstructed shape.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses multistatic radio-frequency imaging with anisotropy by combining per-pair inverse-problem reconstructions with a 3-D U-Net for semantic voxel classification and object instance detection. Different imaging methods (BP, LASSO, incoherent BP, group-LASSO) are fused across six Tx–Rx pairs via trained U-Nets, followed by geometric post-processing for instance-level bounding boxes. Semantic and detection performance degrades more gracefully with noise than classical intensity reconstruction, and an unknown class via outlier exposure handles novel object classes.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to go beyond classical intensity reconstruction in multistatic RF imaging, which degrades rapidly under noise in under-determined setups. They seek a semantic reconstruction approach that remains reliable at high noise levels and can handle anisotropy-induced pair-dependent reflections, while also addressing the practical issue of encountering object classes not seen during training.
AI.method: Per-pair images are formed using one of four methods: BP, LASSO (single deterministic snapshot), incoherent BP, or group-LASSO (multiple fading snapshots). Each trained 3-D U-Net fuses the six Tx–Rx pair inputs and assigns per-voxel probability vectors over semantic classes; the most probable class yields the labeled volume. Object instances and oriented bounding boxes are extracted via clustering and PCA. An explicit unknown class is trained using outlier exposure to label novel objects as unknown.
AI.result: Across a wide SNR range, semantic segmentation (measured by intersection-over-union) and 3-D detection degrade far more gracefully than classical intensity reconstruction. Detection remains reliable even at noise levels where intensity reconstruction has dissolved. The outlier-exposure-trained unknown class successfully labels held-out novel objects as unknown rather than misclassifying them as known classes based on reconstructed shape.
AI.conclusion: Semantic reconstruction via deep fusion of per-pair inverse-problem images provides robust, noise-resilient labeling and detection in multistatic anisotropic RF imaging, and outlier exposure enables handling of unseen object classes in real scenes.

title: Characterizing Necessary Losers to Explain Tournaments Losers
comment: This paper is the extended version of Contet, Grandi, Mengin. Characterizing Necessary Losers to Explain Tournaments Losers. In: Proceedings of the 9th International Conference on Algorithmic Decision Theory (ADT) (2026)
summary: We study the problem of formally explaining why a candidate was not selected by a given tournament rule, by identifying sub-tournaments in which the candidate loses independently of how the rest of the tournament is completed. We define destructive minimal supports as any minimal sub-tournaments satisfying this property, which in formal explainable artificial intelligence correspond to abductive explanations for the question "Why does the loser lose the tournament?". For six common tournament solutions (maximin, uncovered set and its weighted variant, top-cycle, Copeland, and Borda) we provide characterizations of when a candidate is either a necessary loser or a possible winner, we determine the size of the smallest destructive minimal supports, complemented by polynomial-time algorithms for their computation except for the case of the Borda rule which is suspected to be NP-complete.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the concept of destructive minimal supports—minimal sub-tournaments that explain why a candidate loses under a given tournament rule regardless of how the rest of the tournament is completed—and provides formal characterizations and algorithmic results for six common tournament solutions (maximin, uncovered set, weighted uncovered set, top-cycle, Copeland, and Borda).
AI.motivation: To provide formal explanations (in the sense of abductive explanations in explainable AI) for why a candidate lost a tournament, by identifying minimal sub-tournaments where the candidate's loss is unavoidable regardless of the remaining tournament structure.
AI.method: The paper formally defines destructive minimal supports as minimal sub-tournaments guaranteeing a candidate's loss for a given tournament rule. It characterizes when a candidate is a necessary loser or a possible winner for six tournament solutions, determines the smallest destructive minimal support sizes, and provides polynomial-time algorithms for computing them (except Borda, which is suspected to be NP-complete).
AI.result: For maximin, uncovered set, weighted uncovered set, top-cycle, and Copeland rules, polynomial-time algorithms are given for computing destructive minimal supports. For the Borda rule, the problem is suspected to be NP-complete. Complete characterizations of necessary losers and possible winners are provided for all six rules.
AI.conclusion: The paper bridges tournament theory and formal explainable AI by providing a principled framework for explaining tournament outcomes, with tractable algorithms for most common tournament solutions and a conjectured hardness result for the Borda rule.

title: E2S-Pruner: Progressive Two-Stage Evidence Fusion for Visual Token Pruning in Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-language models typically encode an image into hundreds of visual tokens, incurring substantial inference latency and GPU memory overhead. Existing pruning methods largely rely on attention scores and directly aggregate outputs across attention heads and network layers, making it difficult to characterize evidential uncertainty and conflict. We propose E2S-Pruner, a progressive two-stage evidence-fusion framework for visual token pruning that requires no auxiliary model, trainable parameters, or fine-tuning. In the first stage, E2S-Pruner treats each attention head as an independent evidence source, estimates its reliability from evidence clarity and inter-head consistency, and represents each visual token using three states: important, unimportant, and uncertain. In the second stage, Dempster--Shafer evidence theory is used to quantify inter-layer conflict and fuse complementary evidence from multiple network layers. We further introduce a spatial novelty constraint that promotes coverage of distinct image regions and prevents the retained tokens from concentrating in a few locally salient areas. On LLaVA-1.5-7B, E2S-Pruner retains 98.0%, 96.8%, and 90.6% of the aggregate performance when the average numbers of retained visual tokens are 192, 128, and 64, respectively, while improving throughput by 1.96x and 2.09x under the 128-token and 64-token settings. Experiments on Qwen2-VL-7B further demonstrate cross-model generalization. Code is available at https://github.com/taoyu-qian/E2S-Pruner.git.

AI.tldr: E2S-Pruner is a progressive two-stage evidence-fusion framework for visual token pruning in vision-language models. It uses Dempster-Shafer evidence theory to estimate evidential uncertainty across attention heads and network layers, eliminating the need for auxiliary models, trainable parameters, or fine-tuning. Pruning to 128 tokens retains 96.8% performance with 1.96x throughput improvement on LLaVA-1.5-7B, with cross-model generalization to Qwen2-VL-7B.
AI.motivation: Vision-language models encode images into hundreds of visual tokens, causing high inference latency and GPU memory overhead. Existing pruning methods rely on attention scores and aggregate outputs across heads and layers, failing to properly characterize evidential uncertainty and inter-source conflict during token importance assessment.
AI.method: E2S-Pruner consists of two stages. In stage one, each attention head is treated as an independent evidence source; reliability is estimated from evidence clarity and inter-head consistency, classifying each visual token as important, unimportant, or uncertain. In stage two, Dempster-Shafer evidence theory quantifies inter-layer conflict and fuses complementary evidence across layers. A spatial novelty constraint is added to ensure retained tokens cover distinct image regions rather than concentrating in locally salient areas. The method requires no auxiliary model, trainable parameters, or fine-tuning.
AI.result: On LLaVA-1.5-7B, E2S-Pruner retains 98.0%, 96.8%, and 90.6% of aggregate performance with 192, 128, and 64 retained visual tokens respectively, while achieving 1.96x and 2.09x throughput improvements at 128-token and 64-token settings. Experiments on Qwen2-VL-7B demonstrate cross-model generalization.
AI.conclusion: E2S-Pruner provides an effective, resource-efficient visual token pruning approach that models evidential uncertainty via Dempster-Shafer theory, preserves performance at high pruning ratios, and generalizes across different vision-language models without requiring training or fine-tuning.

title: StrategyBench: Evaluating Explicit Strategy Induction in Large Language Models
summary: As large language models are increasingly used in data-scarce and evolving task scenarios, few-shot in-context learning (ICL) has become a key paradigm for task adaptation. However, direct ICL often uses a small set of examples without explicitly abstracting task rules, making it sensitive to example construction. In contrast, human learners often reduce such sensitivity by first summarizing task rules from examples and then applying them to new instances. To evaluate this ability, we propose StrategyBench, which selects strategy-inducible tasks from BIG-Bench, constructs reference strategies, and defines evaluation metrics along two dimensions: strategy quality and downstream utility. We further analyze strategy induction from three perspectives: task variation, model configuration, and adaptation setting, covering category-wise differences, generator-executor choices, demonstration design, and SFT-based adaptation. Experiments show that explicit strategy utility differs substantially across task categories and depends on both strategy generation and execution conditions. The benchmark is released at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/StrategyBench-D53C.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces StrategyBench, a benchmark evaluating whether LLMs can explicitly induce task strategies (rules) from few-shot examples before applying them to new instances, mirroring human learning. It measures strategy quality and downstream utility across tasks from BIG-Bench, analyzing the effects of task variation, model configuration, and adaptation settings.
AI.motivation: Direct few-shot in-context learning lacks explicit task rule abstraction and is sensitive to example construction. The authors argue that humans reduce this sensitivity by first summarizing task rules from examples and then applying them, and propose to systematically evaluate whether LLMs can do the same.
AI.method: The authors build StrategyBench by selecting strategy-inducible tasks from BIG-Bench, constructing reference strategies, and defining evaluation metrics along two dimensions: strategy quality (how good is the induced strategy) and downstream utility (how well the strategy helps on new instances). They analyze strategy induction across three perspectives: task variation (category-wise differences), model configuration (generator-executor choices and demonstration design), and adaptation setting (SFT-based adaptation).
AI.result: Experiments show that explicit strategy utility differs substantially across task categories and depends on both strategy generation and execution conditions, indicating that neither strategy generation quality nor execution method alone determines overall utility.
AI.conclusion: StrategyBench provides a systematic evaluation framework for LLM strategy induction, revealing that explicit abstraction of task rules is a meaningful yet capability-dependent dimension of few-shot learning, varying by task type, model setup, and adaptation approach.

title: Progressively Learning Heterogeneous Skills in a Unified Latent Space
summary: We propose HetSkills, a novel framework designed to progressively learn heterogeneous skills within a unified latent space for physics-based character control. The core idea is to treat this latent space as a shared executable interface, enabling seamless integration of skills learned from diverse data sources, supervision forms, and tasks. HetSkills begins by learning a tracking skill that establishes a strong foundation in motion control and creates a shared motion decoder, which can be reused across tasks without the need for retraining or separate controllers. To prevent the text-to-motion skill from exploiting shortcut pathways instead of learning language semantics, we introduce motion intuition distillation to ground text-to-motion generation in language semantics and a task-guidance module that dynamically adjusts actions based on high-level language instructions. This enables HetSkills to preserve natural motion while continuously expanding its skill repertoire, making it highly adaptable for long-horizon tasks. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness in motion tracking, text-to-motion generation, motion completion, and downstream task adaptation, achieving impressive success rates even under challenging conditions.

AI.tldr: HetSkills is a framework for progressively learning heterogeneous skills in a unified latent space for physics-based character control. It uses a shared motion decoder from an initial tracking skill, then adds text-to-motion generation with motion intuition distillation and task-guidance modules. It achieves strong performance in motion tracking, text-to-motion generation, motion completion, and downstream task adaptation.
AI.motivation: Physics-based character control requires integrating skills from diverse data sources, supervision forms, and tasks, but existing approaches typically require separate controllers or retraining for each new skill. The paper aims to create a seamless, expandable system for heterogeneous skill learning in a single unified space.
AI.method: HetSkills builds a shared latent space as an executable interface. It first learns a tracking skill to establish a strong motion control foundation and create a reusable motion decoder. It then introduces motion intuition distillation to prevent text-to-motion skill from exploiting shortcuts rather than learning language semantics, and a task-guidance module that dynamically adjusts actions based on high-level language instructions.
AI.result: The framework demonstrates effectiveness across motion tracking, text-to-motion generation, motion completion, and downstream task adaptation, achieving impressive success rates even under challenging conditions.
AI.conclusion: HetSkills enables continuous skill expansion while preserving natural motion, making it highly adaptable for long-horizon tasks, without requiring retraining or separate controllers for each new skill.

title: Multi-Modal Semantic Expansion with Constrained LLM Reranking for Conversational Music Recommendation
summary: We present Team Semiintelligencn's solution for the ACM RecSys 2026 TalkPlayData Challenge, addressing conversational music recommendation through a multi-modal and personalized conversational recommender system. Our submitted system employs a three-stage pipeline: (1) multi-modal retrieval constructing decay-weighted centroids across seven dense embedding spaces - track- and user-level CF-BPR, Qwen3 (metadata, lyrics, attributes), CLAP audio, and SigLIP visual - supplemented by BM25 lexical retrieval and an artist substring-match signal, all fused via weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) with optimized signal weights; (2) lightweight reranking (history filtering, popularity smoothing, and catalog diversity penalization); and (3) persona-diversified response generation using GPT-4o-mini. Beyond this submitted configuration, we report development-time experiments with additional components - constrained LLM-guided artist injection, album continuation signals, XGBoost LambdaMART, and a superior GPT-4.1 response prompt - that were not deployed to Blind B due to cost and complexity constraints. We optimize RRF weights on a 500-session development split via differential evolution, improving MRR by +19.5%. On Blind A, we observe that unconstrained LLM-guided injection across 54 sessions causes catastrophic nDCG regression (-18.9%), while conservative injection on only 9 sessions yields the best observed Blind A nDCG - a finding we present as a Blind A observation warranting further validation. The submitted system achieves a Blind B composite score of 0.3213.

AI.tldr: The authors present their solution for the ACM RecSys 2026 TalkPlayData Challenge, a three-stage multi-modal conversational music recommender system combining decaying-centroid retrieval across seven dense embedding spaces (CF-BPR, Qwen3, CLAP, SigLIP) with BM25 and artist substring matching, fused via optimized weighted RRF, followed by lightweight reranking and persona-diversified GPT-4o-mini responses. The system achieves a Blind B composite score of 0.3213 and improves MRR by +19.5% on development via differential evolution.
AI.motivation: To address conversational music recommendation in the TalkPlayData Challenge by building a system that integrates multi-modal signals (text, audio, visual, collaborative filtering) and personalization to produce high-quality music recommendations in a conversational setting.
AI.method: A three-stage pipeline: (1) multi-modal retrieval using decay-weighted centroids across seven dense embedding spaces (track/user CF-BPR, Qwen3 metadata/lyrics/attributes, CLAP audio, SigLIP visual) plus BM25 lexical retrieval and artist substring-match, fused via weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion with signal weights optimized via differential evolution on a 500-session dev split; (2) lightweight reranking (history filtering, popularity smoothing, catalog diversity penalization); (3) persona-diversified response generation using GPT-4o-mini. Additional experiments included constrained LLM-guided artist injection, album continuation, XGBoost LambdaMART, and a GPT-4.1 prompt variant.
AI.result: Differential evolution RRF weight optimization improved MRR by +19.5%. Unconstrained LLM-guided injection across 54 sessions caused -18.9% nDCG regression on Blind A, while conservative injection on only 9 sessions yielded the best observed Blind A nDCG. The submitted system achieved a Blind B composite score of 0.3213.
AI.conclusion: The multi-modal fused retrieval approach with optimized fusion weights is effective for conversational music recommendation. While LLM-guided artist injection can be beneficial, unconstrained or broad application is harmful, suggesting a need for conservative, well-validated integration strategies. Cost and complexity constrained the deployment of otherwise promising components.

title: Dual-Grained Agent Memory and Shapley Context Attribution for Multimodal Agentic Learner
summary: Frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) deliver impressive perception yet still falter on scientific and mathematical reasoning. Parameter-level adaptation is unavailable for closed-weight or on-device backbones, and stateless prompting forfeits any compounding benefit from problems already solved. We propose \textbf{DG-Mem}, a dual-grained agentic memory framework that augments a frozen MLLM with a non-parametric, externally stored memory built once from training-time rollouts and consulted read-only at test time. Motivated by the Complementary Learning Systems (CLS) account of human memory, DG-Mem factors its store into an instance-grounded exemplar memory and a category-level schema memory of IF-THEN rules, with a transient reflection store mediating their construction so that schemas are synthesized only from abstract reflections, never from exemplar text. Two design choices distinguish DG-Mem: an online concept categorizer that grows the category space incrementally during training rather than committing to a predefined taxonomy, and a Shapley context attribution procedure that decomposes correctness across the entire retrieved rule set and yields a per-rule utility that re-weights retrieval at test time. The pipeline introduces no gradient updates and is deployable on closed-weight or on-device backbones. Across MathVista, MMMU, and MMMU-Pro on four open-weight and proprietary backbones (Qwen3.5-27B, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, GPT-5-Nano, Gemini-3-Flash), DG-Mem improves consistently over no-memory and competitive memory baselines.

AI.tldr: DG-Mem is a dual-grained agentic memory framework that augments frozen multimodal large language models with a non-parametric, externally stored memory built from training-time rollouts and consulted read-only at test time. It combines instance-grounded exemplar memory with category-level IF-THEN schema memory, uses an online concept categorizer and Shapley context attribution for retrieval weighting, and improves scientific/mathematical reasoning across MathVista, MMMU, and MMMU-Pro on both open-weight and proprietary backbones without any gradient updates.
AI.motivation: Frontier MLLMs deliver strong perception but still struggle with scientific and mathematical reasoning. Parameter-level adaptation is infeasible for closed-weight or on-device backbones, and stateless prompting cannot leverage compounding benefits from previously solved problems. A memory-augmentation approach is needed that works without fine-tuning and exploits past problem-solving experience.
AI.method: DG-Mem introduces a dual-grained memory with: (1) an instance-grounded exemplar memory storing full problem-solution traces from training rollouts, and (2) a category-level schema memory of IF-THEN rules synthesized only from abstract reflections (not exemplar text), mediated by a transient reflection store. Two key designs: an online concept categorizer that incrementally grows the category space during training without a predefined taxonomy, and a Shapley context attribution procedure that decomposes correctness across the retrieved rule set to produce per-rule utilities that re-weight retrieval at test time. The pipeline is entirely non-parametric, requiring no gradient updates.
AI.result: Across MathVista, MMMU, and MMMU-Pro on four backbones (Qwen3.5-27B, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, GPT-5-Nano, Gemini-3-Flash), DG-Mem consistently outperforms no-memory baselines and competitive memory baselines on scientific and mathematical reasoning tasks.
AI.conclusion: DG-Mem demonstrates that a frozen MLLM can be effectively augmented with non-parametric external memory inspired by Complementary Learning Systems theory, enabling improved reasoning without parameter adaptation. The dual-grained exemplar/schema memory, online taxonomy growth, and Shapley-based retrieval weighting collectively deliver consistent gains and are deployable on closed-weight and on-device backbones.

title: SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning
summary: Self-reflection is a powerful mechanism for credit assignment in human learning, converting sparse outcome feedback into actionable guidance. However, its potential for post-training Large Language Models (LLMs) remains underexplored. We propose Self-Reflective Policy Optimization (SRPO), a framework that internalizes this capability. SRPO enables LLMs to analyze their own completed trajectories, synthesize errors into concise "reflection patches," and use reflection-conditioned teacher scores on student on-policy rollouts as dense token-level training signals. This process effectively transforms sparse terminal supervision into dense, token-level learning signals without requiring external critics, separate reward models, or larger teacher models. We demonstrate that SRPO achieves state-of-the-art performance across mathematical reasoning and long-horizon agentic benchmarks with exceptional data efficiency. Using a Qwen3-8B base model, SRPO attains 73.3% on AIME'24 using only 8% (0.08x) of the training FLOPs required by scaled supervised fine-tuning, while significantly improving success rates on WebShop (64.7%), ALFWorld (76.8%), and SWE-Bench-Lite (31.2%). Code is available at https://github.com/Galleons2029/SRPO

AI.tldr: SRPO is a self-reflection-based framework that enables LLMs to analyze their own trajectories, generate reflection patches, and use reflection-conditioned teacher scores as dense token-level training signals, achieving state-of-the-art performance on math and agentic benchmarks with significantly reduced training FLOPs (8% of SFT) and no external reward models or larger teachers.
AI.motivation: Self-reflection is a powerful credit-assignment mechanism in human learning, yet its potential for post-training LLMs is underexplored. The authors aim to harness this capability to convert sparse terminal feedback into dense, token-level learning signals without relying on external critics, reward models, or larger teacher models.
AI.method: SRPO enables LLMs to analyze their own completed trajectories, synthesize errors into concise reflection patches, and use reflection-conditioned teacher scores on student on-policy rollouts as dense token-level training signals. This converts sparse terminal supervision into dense learning signals internally, requiring no external critics or larger teachers.
AI.result: Using Qwen3-8B, SRPO achieves 73.3% on AIME'24 with only 8% (0.08x) of the training FLOPs required by scaled SFT, and achieves strong success rates on WebShop (64.7%), ALFWorld (76.8%), and SWE-Bench-Lite (31.2%), demonstrating state-of-the-art performance with exceptional data efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Self-reflection can be internalized as an effective post-training mechanism for LLMs, enabling dense credit assignment from sparse rewards with high data and compute efficiency, outperforming scaled SFT baselines on both mathematical reasoning and long-horizon agentic tasks.

title: Spatiotemporally Decoupled Autoregressive Diffusion Model for Human Motion Generation
summary: Text-driven human motion synthesis has made substantial development with two core modules of motion representation and generative architecture. For representation, Vector Quantization (VQ)-based methods compress motion data into discrete tokens while latent-based models operate directly in continuous space. However, both of these representations exhibit significant limitations.
