VQ-based methods suffer from inherent information loss, which compromises the quality, diversity, and generalization of generated motions, while continuous representation on holistic whole-body motion hinders part-level flexibility. For architecture, diffusion and autoregressive diffusion models have demonstrated their superiority, yet the fine-grained controllability over individual body parts is also limited. Thus, we propose a unified spatiotemporally decoupled framework named DeMoDiff, which jointly redesigns representation and architecture. To enhance representation extraction capabilities and offer greater part-level controllability, we present a spatial-temporal VAE that encodes each body joint rather than compressing the whole-body motion into a single latent space. Then, we incorporate spatial-temporal masking and attention mechanisms into an autoregressive diffusion generator, achieving both generative capability and controllable editability. Extensive experiments on the HumanML3D and KIT-ML datasets demonstrate that our model achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction performance and compelling motion generation results. Moreover, our framework demonstrates strong temporal and spatial editing capabilities, further validating its effectiveness. Our project page: https://rex0191.github.io/DeMoDiff/

AI.tldr: DeMoDiff is a unified spatiotemporally decoupled framework for text-driven human motion synthesis that jointly redesigns motion representation and generative architecture. It introduces a spatial-temporal VAE that encodes each body joint independently for better representation extraction and part-level controllability, combined with an autoregressive diffusion generator incorporating spatial-temporal masking and attention mechanisms for both generation and controllable editing.
AI.motivation: Existing motion representations have fundamental limitations: VQ-based methods suffer from information loss compromising quality and generalization, while continuous whole-body representations prevent part-level flexibility. Additionally, current generative architectures (diffusion and autoregressive diffusion) lack fine-grained controllability over individual body parts, motivating the need for a framework that jointly addresses both representation and architecture shortcomings.
AI.method: DeMoDiff introduces a spatial-temporal VAE that encodes each body joint individually rather than compressing whole-body motion into a single latent space, enabling better representation extraction and part-level controllability. This is paired with an autoregressive diffusion generator that incorporates spatial-temporal masking and attention mechanisms to achieve both strong generative capability and controllable editability.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on HumanML3D and KIT-ML datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art reconstruction performance and compelling motion generation results. The framework also demonstrates strong temporal and spatial editing capabilities, validating its effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: The unified spatiotemporally decoupled design of DeMoDiff successfully overcomes the limitations of existing representations and generative architectures, achieving superior performance in reconstruction, generation, and fine-grained controllable editing of human motions.

title: Mitigating Reasoning-Induced Misalignment via Safety-Direction Penalty
summary: Reasoning-Induced Misalignment, where fine-tuning on reasoning data containing no harmful content, including mathematics, code, and problem-solving with chain-of-thought traces can induce harmful behaviors of LLM, posing a serious challenge to the safety of LLM reasoning. Cross-architecture, cross-scale, and cross-dataset checks show that RIM does not always emerge. Previous work attributed RIM to neuron-level entanglement, but did not identify the geometry of the representation space underlying this entanglement or propose a training-time fix. We provide both: a representation-space analysis of RIM and the Safety-Direction Penalty (SDP), which penalizes movement along a learned safety direction during reasoning fine-tuning. The analysis extracts two activation-space directions, one encoding reasoning ability and the other safety behavior. These directions are coupled: fine-tuning that improves reasoning shifts safety representations, and prompts with larger shifts show larger safety degradation. CKA distance ratios and probes locate the safety-decision layers where this shift is most relevant. These findings guide the design of SDP: the coupling motivates penalizing displacement along the safety direction, and the layer localization sets the initial scope. When the initial scope leaves compensatory shifts beyond the penalized layers, the same diagnostics guide iterative expansion. On Qwen2.5-3B and 7B, SDP restores safety while preserving benchmark reasoning performance.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies Reasoning-Induced Misalignment (RIM) in LLMs where fine-tuning on benign reasoning data (math, code, problem-solving) induces harmful behaviors. The authors provide a representation-space analysis showing coupling between reasoning and safety activation directions, and propose Safety-Direction Penalty (SDP), a training-time fix that penalizes movement along a learned safety direction, restoring safety while preserving reasoning performance on Qwen2.5-3B/7B.
AI.motivation: RIM poses a serious safety challenge: fine-tuning on reasoning data containing no harmful content can induce harmful LLM behaviors. Prior work attributed this to neuron-level entanglement but failed to identify the representation-space geometry underlying it or propose a training-time fix.
AI.method: The method involves: (1) extracting two activation-space directions encoding reasoning ability and safety behavior and analyzing their coupling; (2) using CKA distance ratios and probes to localize safety-decision layers where shift matters; (3) designing Safety-Direction Penalty (SDP) which penalizes displacement along the learned safety direction during reasoning fine-tuning, with iterative expansion guided by diagnostics when compensatory shifts occur beyond penalized layers.
AI.result: Cross-architecture, cross-scale, and cross-dataset checks show RIM does not always emerge. On Qwen2.5-3B and 7B, SDP restores safety while preserving benchmark reasoning performance. The analysis confirms that fine-tuning improving reasoning shifts safety representations, with prompts showing larger shifts exhibiting larger safety degradation.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides both a geometric understanding of RIM at the representation-space level and a practical training-time fix (SDP) that mitigates safety degradation without sacrificing reasoning capability, with diagnostics guiding iterative refinement of the penalty scope.

title: Spotter: Efficient Urban Visual Localization via Geo-Referenced Facade Landmarks in GPS-Degraded Environments
summary: Accurate visual localization on robotic and wearable platforms remains challenging in dense urban environments. Existing methodologies typically rely on GPS for absolute positioning, yet GPS signals frequently degrade in urban canyons due to multipath propagation. Consequently, standard solutions like visual odometry suffer from unmitigated drift over time, while map-matching techniques struggle to acquire the reliable GPS priors they need, on top of being too computationally heavy for real-time edge execution. To address these limitations, we propose Spotter, a robuts and real-time visual localization framework that uses building facades as a reliable source of global geo-reference, while retaining the capability to integrate GPS signals when available. In an offline stage, Spotter processes Google Street View panoramas by semantically segmenting facades and pairing multi-view stereo depth with cartographic data to build a compact metric database. At runtime, query images are matched via a cascaded retrieval and geometric verification pipeline to recover fine-grained global camera localization. We benchmark Spotter on a newly collected dataset of pedestrian sequences acquired with wearable smart glasses across several districts of Barcelona. Experimental results show that Spotter outperforms odometry-based baselines and achieves localization accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art map-based methods while operating at significantly higher frame rates.

AI.tldr: Spotter is a real-time visual localization framework that uses building facades as global geo-references, built from offline Google Street View processing and matched via cascaded retrieval and geometric verification, achieving accuracy comparable to map-based methods at higher frame rates in dense urban environments.
AI.motivation: GPS signals degrade in urban canyons due to multipath propagation, causing visual odometry to drift over time and map-matching techniques to lack reliable GPS priors while being computationally too heavy for real-time edge execution on robotic and wearable platforms.
AI.method: Spotter consists of an offline stage that processes Google Street View panoramas by semantically segmenting building facades and pairing multi-view stereo depth with cartographic data to build a compact metric database. At runtime, a cascaded retrieval and geometric verification pipeline matches query images to recover fine-grained global camera localization, while retaining the ability to integrate GPS signals when available.
AI.result: Spotter outperforms odometry-based baselines and achieves localization accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art map-based methods while operating at significantly higher frame rates, as demonstrated on a newly collected dataset of pedestrian sequences acquired with wearable smart glasses across several districts of Barcelona.
AI.conclusion: Building facade-based geo-referencing provides a robust and real-time alternative to GPS-dependent approaches for visual localization in dense urban environments, suitable for edge deployment on robotic and wearable platforms.

title: EarthVerse: Benchmarking Scientific Agents Across Dynamic Earth Systems and Natural Hazards
summary: Earth-system analysis reconstructs changing physical processes from observations that differ in source, scale, timing, and modality. Natural hazards make this work consequential because incomplete evidence can change estimates of severity, exposure, and mechanism. We introduce EarthVerse, a benchmark that evaluates scientific agents through package-scoped investigations. Its 405 reproducible tasks are grounded in 199 documented events and 19 hazard families. Agents inspect heterogeneous event packages, choose compatible evidence, execute transparent calculations, reconcile source differences, and preserve provenance in the final answer. We provide executable ground truth that decomposes each task into fine-grained answer units, together with task-specific rubrics that assess the supporting research process while allowing multiple valid paths. We evaluate 25 model and agent systems under a controlled tool-using protocol, then use controlled studies to locate failures in evidence access, tool selection, memory, reasoning, interaction, and scientific execution. Across systems, the best mean answer-unit accuracy is 84.65%, while the highest Strict@95 is only 34.81%. The gap shows that current agents often complete individual steps without maintaining a consistent chain across evidence, scales, units, calculations, and physical interpretation. EarthVerse provides a reproducible basis for measuring end-to-end scientific reliability in dynamic Earth systems.

AI.tldr: EarthVerse is a benchmark for evaluating scientific agents through 405 reproducible tasks across 199 documented natural hazard events and 19 hazard families, requiring agents to inspect heterogeneous data packages, select evidence, perform calculations, reconcile sources, and preserve provenance. Best mean answer-unit accuracy is 84.65% but Strict@95 is only 34.81%, revealing that current agents struggle to maintain consistent chains across evidence, scales, units, calculations, and physical interpretation.
AI.motivation: Earth-system analysis reconstructs physical processes from heterogeneous observations, and incomplete evidence can change estimates of severity, exposure, and mechanism in natural hazard contexts. Existing evaluation approaches don't adequately measure end-to-end scientific reliability of agents working with diverse, package-scoped evidence.
AI.method: The authors construct EarthVerse with 405 reproducible tasks grounded in 199 documented events and 19 hazard families. Tasks use heterogeneous event packages requiring agents to choose compatible evidence, execute transparent calculations, reconcile source differences, and preserve provenance. They provide executable ground truth decomposed into fine-grained answer units with task-specific rubrics, and evaluate 25 model/agent systems under a controlled tool-using protocol plus controlled studies to isolate failures across evidence access, tool selection, memory, reasoning, interaction, and scientific execution.
AI.result: Best mean answer-unit accuracy is 84.65% while highest Strict@95 is only 34.81%. This substantial gap indicates current agents complete individual steps but fail to maintain a consistent chain across evidence, scales, units, calculations, and physical interpretation. Controlled studies localize failures to specific aspects such as evidence access, tool selection, memory, reasoning, interaction, and scientific execution.
AI.conclusion: EarthVerse provides a reproducible basis for measuring end-to-end scientific reliability in dynamic Earth systems, and the performance gap highlights a critical shortcoming in current scientific agents: consistent end-to-end chains across evidence, scales, units, calculations, and physical interpretation remain an open challenge.

title: What Memory Composition Does Not Tell Us About Anomaly Detection
summary: Memory-based anomaly detectors store nominal training patches and score test patches against this memory. A patch selected for coverage therefore becomes a nor- mal reference without a separate check that geometric rarity makes it safe to trust. We probe this coupling with sparse training contamination. Under fixed representa- tions and memory budgets, we compare random, medoid, local, and global coverage selectors. We then use CLEANCON, an out-of-bag cross-image support gate that changes candidate-image eligibility while fixing the representation, absolute mem- ory size, builder, and inference rule. Global coverage strongly over-represents sparse contamination. CLEANCON reduces final-memory contamination to approx- imately zero and increases category-macro P-AP in all 12 matched comparisons. Yet along a retention sweep, the lowest-contamination memory does not attain the highest P-AP; performance continues to improve while contamination rises. Mem- ory contamination therefore does not order the resulting memories by P-AP

AI.tldr: This paper investigates memory-based anomaly detectors under sparse training contamination, showing that memory contamination does not determine final detection performance (P-AP). A proposed cross-image support gate (CLEANCON) reduces contamination to near zero and improves P-AP in all 12 matched comparisons, yet optimal P-AP is achieved at intermediate (non-zero) contamination levels.
AI.motivation: Memory-based anomaly detectors select nominal patches as normal references without verifying that geometric rarity guarantees trustworthiness. The paper probes this unchecked coupling by examining how different coverage selectors behave under sparse training contamination.
AI.method: Fixed representations and memory budgets are used to compare random, medoid, local, and global coverage selectors. CLEANCON is introduced as an out-of-bag cross-image support gate that changes candidate-image eligibility while holding representation, absolute memory size, builder, and inference rule constant.
AI.result: Global coverage strongly over-represents sparse contamination. CLEANCON reduces final-memory contamination to approximately zero and improves category-macro P-AP in all 12 matched comparisons. However, along a retention sweep, the lowest-contamination memory does not yield the highest P-AP; performance continues to improve as contamination rises, indicating memory contamination does not order memories by P-AP.
AI.conclusion: Minimizing memory contamination is not sufficient for (or necessarily aligned with) maximizing anomaly detection performance. The relationship between memory purity and P-AP is non-monotonic, suggesting that other factors alongside contamination influence the quality of the final memory representation.

title: Correcting a learned physical invariant improves world-model rollouts
summary: World models can predict video without learning dynamics that they reliably preserve. We test whether a frozen DreamerV3 trained only on pendulum video learns a scalar that its own latent transition treats as approximately conserved. A label-free search recovers the same energy-like invariant across independently trained conservative models, while the same procedure finds no comparable invariant in matched damped models. During autonomous rollouts, this quantity drifts. Projecting the latent state back toward its initial level set reduces rollout error in all three conservative models, whereas matched random constraints usually increase it. These results distinguish a dynamically meaningful invariant from a merely decodable correlate and reveal a concrete failure mode: a world model can learn a physical constraint from pixels yet violate that constraint when it imagines forward.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates whether a frozen DreamerV3 world model trained solely on pendulum video learns a scalar quantity that its own latent dynamics treat as approximately conserved. Using a label-free search, they recover the same energy-like invariant across independent conservative models but not in damped models. During rollouts, this quantity drifts; projecting latent states back toward their initial level set reduces rollout error in conservative models, revealing that world models can learn a physical constraint from pixels but fail to preserve it during imagined rollouts.
AI.motivation: To determine whether world models trained solely on video can discover and internally preserve physically meaningful invariants (specifically conserved quantities like energy), rather than merely predicting plausible video frames without learning true dynamics.
AI.method: Train DreamerV3 on pendulum videos (both conservative and damped variants), freeze the model, use a label-free search to find a scalar function in latent space that the model's own latent transition approximately conserves. Then evaluate the recovered invariant through autonomous rollouts, measuring drift and testing whether projecting latent states back to their initial level set improves or degrades rollout error, with random constraints as controls.
AI.result: The label-free search recovers the same energy-like invariant across independently trained conservative models but finds no comparable invariant in damped models. The discovered quantity drifts during autonomous rollouts. Projecting the latent state back toward its initial level set reduces rollout error in all three conservative models, while matched random constraints usually increase it.
AI.conclusion: The recovered invariant is a dynamically meaningful quantity (not merely a decodable correlate), yet world models exhibit a concrete failure mode: they can learn a physical constraint from pixels but violate that constraint when predicting forward. This suggests that even successful world models do not reliably internalize conservation laws in their latent dynamics.

title: What Remains Normal? Clean Images Miss Useful Near-Defect Normal Patches for Anomaly Detection
summary: Memory-based anomaly detectors store nominal training patches and score test patches against this memory. A patch selected for coverage therefore becomes a nor- mal reference without a separate check that geometric rarity makes it safe to trust. We probe this coupling with sparse training contamination. Under fixed representa- tions and memory budgets, we compare random, medoid, local, and global coverage selectors. We then use CLEANCON, an out-of-bag cross-image support gate that changes candidate-image eligibility while fixing the representation, absolute mem- ory size, builder, and inference rule. Global coverage strongly over-represents sparse contamination. CLEANCON reduces final-memory contamination to approx- imately zero and increases category-macro P-AP in all 12 matched comparisons. Yet along a retention sweep, the lowest-contamination memory does not attain the highest P-AP; performance continues to improve while contamination rises. Mem- ory contamination therefore does not order the resulting memories by P-AP.Code is publicly available at https://github.com/jw-chae/cleancon.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates memory-based anomaly detectors under sparse training contamination, showing that global coverage selectors heavily over-represent contamination. The authors propose CLEANCON, an out-of-bag cross-image support gate that filters candidate images, reducing final-memory contamination to near zero and improving P-AP in all 12 matched comparisons. However, a retention sweep reveals that the lowest-contamination memory does not achieve the highest P-AP, indicating that memory contamination does not directly order memories by P-AP.
AI.motivation: Memory-based anomaly detectors store normal training patches and score test patches against them, assuming selected patches are trustworthy normal references. However, under sparse training contamination, the coverage selection process may inadvertently include contaminated patches as normal references without verifying geometric rarity, potentially degrading detection performance.
AI.method: The authors compare random, medoid, local, and global coverage selectors under fixed representations and memory budgets with sparse training contamination. They introduce CLEANCON, an out-of-bag cross-image support gate that filters candidate-image eligibility while keeping the representation, absolute memory size, builder, and inference rule fixed. They also perform a retention sweep to study the relationship between memory contamination and P-AP.
AI.result: Global coverage strongly over-represents sparse contamination. CLEANCON reduces final-memory contamination to approximately zero and increases category-macro P-AP in all 12 matched comparisons. However, along a retention sweep, the lowest-contamination memory does not attain the highest P-AP; performance continues to improve while contamination rises.
AI.conclusion: CLEANCON effectively filters contaminated patches from the memory, improving anomaly detection performance. However, the finding that contamination does not monotonically relate to P-AP suggests that a memory with zero contamination is not necessarily optimal for anomaly detection, challenging the assumption that minimizing contamination should be the sole objective.

title: How AI Assistance Affects Human Skill Development: A Study of Learning with Logic Puzzles
comment: Accepted at Human-AI Complementarity and Alignment (HCOMP) 2026
summary: While AI assistance can improve human task performance in the short term, it may also undermine the development of skills in the longer term. We examine this tension in a controlled logic-puzzle experiment involving on-demand AI assistance, where participants complete tasks before, during, and after AI is available. By experimentally varying AI request costs, we find that lower-cost assistance induces more frequent AI use. We also find that participants who request AI assistance during the AI-access phase perform worse at the task after assistance is removed, and their subsequent unassisted performance is overestimated when predicted from earlier AI-assisted performance. We use a Bayesian latent ability model to separate initial ability, post-AI ability, and participant-specific skill change, while estimating how independent reasoning during the AI-access phase relates to skill development. The results show that greater independent problem-solving effort is associated with larger gains in latent ability, consistent with the interpretation that skill development is weaker when AI assistance substitutes for independent reasoning.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the tension between short-term performance gains from AI assistance and long-term skill development through a controlled logic-puzzle experiment with on-demand AI assistance. It finds that lower-cost AI access increases usage frequency, that AI-assisted participants perform worse after assistance is removed, and that their unassisted performance is overestimated when predicted from AI-assisted performance. A Bayesian latent ability model reveals that greater independent problem-solving effort during the AI phase is associated with larger gains in latent ability, indicating that AI substitution for independent reasoning weakens skill development.
AI.motivation: While AI tools can boost immediate task performance, there is concern that reliance on AI may degrade long-term skill acquisition. The paper aims to empirically examine this trade-off between short-term assistance benefits and long-term skill development in a controlled experimental setting.
AI.method: A controlled logic-puzzle experiment was conducted where participants complete tasks before, during, and after AI availability. AI request costs were experimentally varied to manipulate usage frequency. A Bayesian latent ability model was used to separate initial ability, post-AI ability, and participant-specific skill change, while estimating how independent reasoning during the AI-access phase relates to skill development.
AI.result: Lower-cost AI assistance led to more frequent AI use. Participants who requested AI assistance during the AI-access phase performed worse after assistance was removed. Their subsequent unassisted performance was overestimated when predicted from earlier AI-assisted performance. Greater independent problem-solving effort during the AI phase was associated with larger gains in latent ability.
AI.conclusion: The findings are consistent with the interpretation that skill development is weakened when AI assistance substitutes for independent reasoning, highlighting a potential long-term cost of low-friction AI assistance despite short-term performance benefits.

title: Grounding Free-Form Instructions for Fashion Complementary Image Generation
summary: Fashion complementary image generation (CIG) aims to create garments that stylistically match a seed item based on user intent, making it a natural multimodal grounding problem where models must interpret language in visual context. Existing CIG benchmarks rely on rigid template prompts (e.g., "a photo of a skirt"), failing to reflect natural user queries and obscuring model behavior across levels of linguistic specificity. We introduce fashion complementary image generation with free-form instructions, a multimodal language-grounding setting where a model generates a compatible garment from a seed image and a natural-language instruction. To this end, we enrich three CIG benchmarks with low-, medium-, and high-specificity instructions generated by a vision-language model and validated by human annotators. We instantiate the task with StyleFlow, a Rectified Flow Matching model that jointly conditions on the seed image and instruction within a single multimodal transformer. Across image quality metrics, catalog-alignment analysis, ablations, and human evaluation, StyleFlow consistently produces instruction-aligned and stylistically coherent garments while reducing architectural complexity and inference cost relative to auxiliary-module approaches.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a new multimodal language-grounding task for fashion complementary image generation using free-form, natural-language instructions rather than rigid templates. Three existing CIG benchmarks are enriched with instructions at three specificity levels. The proposed StyleFlow model, based on Rectified Flow Matching with a single multimodal transformer jointly conditioning on seed image and text, outperforms prior approaches in alignment, coherence, and efficiency.
AI.motivation: Existing CIG benchmarks rely on rigid template prompts (e.g., "a photo of a skirt") that fail to reflect natural user queries and obscure model behavior across linguistic specificity levels. There is a need for free-form instruction settings that better capture real-world multimodal language grounding.
AI.method: Three CIG benchmarks are enriched with low-, medium-, and high-specificity instructions generated by a vision-language model and validated by human annotators. The task is instantiated with StyleFlow, a Rectified Flow Matching model that jointly conditions on the seed image and instruction within a single multimodal transformer.
AI.result: Across image quality metrics, catalog-alignment analysis, ablations, and human evaluation, StyleFlow consistently produces instruction-aligned and stylistically coherent garments while reducing architectural complexity and inference cost relative to auxiliary-module approaches.
AI.conclusion: Free-form instructions offer a more realistic and informative benchmark for CIG, and StyleFlow demonstrates that a unified multimodal transformer with Rectified Flow Matching can effectively handle this task with better performance and efficiency than auxiliary-module-based baselines.

title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
summary: Language models are sequential processors, but long-horizon agency requires external information and computation beyond model weights and active context. Prime Agent is an open-source harness for long-horizon evaluation and coding-agent workflows. A persistent IPython REPL follows the Recursive Language Model abstraction for programmatic context processing and test-time compute, while Continual Harness preserves histories, memories, skills, prompts, and subagent specifications across trajectories. Recursive subagents coordinate through direct agent-to-agent communication, and the Agents View lets humans inspect and manage daemon-backed sessions. Prime Agent standardizes execution, recovery, verification, and resource accounting while leaving strategy construction to the model. This low-friction, expressive membrane prevents harness failures from becoming model failures and pushes measurement toward the model's true maximal underlying capability. Prime Agent raises ARC-AGI-3 RHAE Best@1 from 30% to 95.5% and matches or exceeds native and popular harnesses across long-context coding, GPU-kernel generation, emulator construction, and autonomous nanoGPT speedruns. On Factorio, we find refinement allows for continuous technology progression and dedicated subagents enable parallelized work. Code is available at https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent.

AI.tldr: Prime Agent is an open-source long-horizon evaluation harness featuring a persistent IPython REPL, continual state preservation, and recursive subagents, achieving 95.5% on ARC-AGI-3 RHAE Best@1 (up from 30%) and matching/exceeding other harnesses across coding, GPU-kernel, emulator, and nanoGPT tasks.
AI.motivation: Language models are sequential processors but long-horizon agency requires external information and computation beyond model weights and active context. Existing harnesses fail to decouple harness robustness from model capability, causing harness failures to be conflated with model failures.
AI.method: Prime Agent introduces: (1) a persistent IPython REPL following the Recursive Language Model abstraction for programmatic context processing and test-time compute; (2) a Continual Harness preserving histories, memories, skills, prompts, and subagent specs across trajectories; (3) recursive subagents with direct agent-to-agent communication; (4) an Agents View for human inspection and daemon-based session management; (5) standardized execution, recovery, verification, and resource accounting.
AI.result: Raises ARC-AGI-3 RHAE Best@1 from 30% to 95.5%, matches or exceeds native and popular harnesses on long-context coding, GPU-kernel generation, emulator construction, and autonomous nanoGPT speedruns. On Factorio, refinement enables continuous technology progression and dedicated subagents enable parallelized work.
AI.conclusion: A low-friction, expressive harness membrane prevents harness failures from becoming model failures, pushing measurement toward the model's true maximal underlying capability for long-horizon tasks.

title: Thinking Beyond Videos: Unifying Video Reasoning and Deep Research for Open-World Video Agents
summary: Open-world video understanding often requires a model to locate sparse visual evidence and acquire external knowledge that is absent from the video and its parametric memory. While Thinking-with-Videos enables active temporal perception and Deep Research supports multi-step information seeking, the two capabilities are typically developed in isolation. We introduce VideoRover, a unified Video Deep Research framework that iteratively coordinates video cropping, multimodal search, and webpage browsing. Given a video-question pair, VideoRover uses each tool result to select the next action, so localized video clips guide external retrieval and retrieved evidence triggers further video inspection and verification. To develop this capability, we construct an automated data curation pipeline, producing 26K verified SFT trajectories and 3K challenging RL instances. We also introduce VideoRover-Bench, a benchmark stratified by video duration and research difficulty. Experiments on VideoDR and VideoRover-Bench show that our VideoRover-8B-RL achieves performance comparable to proprietary models in the direct-answer setting without tool use while outperforming larger open-source models equipped with the same tool suite. Ablation studies and training dynamics further validate the complementary roles of active video grounding, external retrieval, and long-horizon reinforcement learning.

AI.tldr: VideoRover is a unified Video Deep Research framework that iteratively coordinates video cropping, multimodal search, and webpage browsing to solve open-world video understanding tasks requiring both sparse visual evidence localization and external knowledge acquisition.
AI.motivation: Open-world video understanding requires both active temporal perception (locating sparse visual evidence) and multi-step information seeking (acquiring external knowledge), but these two capabilities are typically developed in isolation rather than being unified into a single framework.
AI.method: VideoRover iteratively coordinates three tools—video cropping, multimodal search, and webpage browsing—where each tool result informs the next action selection. The authors construct an automated data curation pipeline producing 26K verified SFT trajectories and 3K RL instances, and introduce VideoRover-Bench, a benchmark stratified by video duration and research difficulty.
AI.result: The VideoRover-8B-RL model achieves performance comparable to proprietary models in the direct-answer setting without tool use, while outperforming larger open-source models equipped with the same tool suite on VideoDR and VideoRover-Bench benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Ablation studies and training dynamics validate the complementary roles of active video grounding, external retrieval, and long-horizon reinforcement learning, demonstrating that unified video deep research capability can be effectively developed in a compact model.

title: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
summary: An interactive world model must follow the user's actions, remember the places it has shown, and stream in real time. The tension is structural: control wants a short horizon, memory wants an unbounded one. ReWorld separates the two during training and bounds them at inference. Mixed per-head attention windows confine most heads to the recent past while a small set of global heads attends over the entire history, and random head routing keeps either capability from binding to particular heads; random chunk dropping makes sparse histories in-distribution. At inference the whole past lives under a fixed budget: a bounded KV cache backed by a pose-indexed landmark bank, from which the model retrieves the landmarks nearest the current pose. A metric-scale-aligned data engine places eight sources -- Unreal-rendered fly-throughs, game roaming, and real-world footage -- on one physical action scale, so the same key press moves the camera the same distance in every source, and palindrome trajectories supply the revisit evidence that memory training needs. Distribution-matching distillation confined to a LoRA adapter then compresses sampling to four steps: one backbone serves both a high-fidelity multi-step mode and a real-time interactive one, streaming 704x1280 video across photorealistic, game-style, and stylized worlds. Under a three-axis protocol covering action following, long-horizon recall, and video quality, against six recent interactive world models it attains the best control fidelity ($11.95^\circ$ rotation error and the best camera-motion consistency) and the best generation quality; and on minute-long out-and-back rollouts ($64$\,s, $384$ latents), its fixed 12-chunk cache still regenerates the starting view -- at rollout lengths where a sliding window has long evicted the evidence and full-KV attention runs out of memory.

AI.tldr: ReWorld separates control and memory during training using mixed per-head attention windows, and bounds them at inference with a pose-indexed landmark bank and fixed-budget KV cache. A metric-scale-aligned data engine and LoRA distillation enable real-time interactive video generation that outperforms six recent models in control fidelity, recall, and quality.
AI.motivation: Interactive world models face a structural tension: control requires short-horizon attention for responsiveness, while memory requires unbounded history for long-horizon recall. Existing approaches cannot simultaneously satisfy both, leading to either poor action following or failure to remember previously shown places over long rollouts.
AI.method: ReWorld uses mixed per-head attention windows (local heads for recent past, global heads for full history) with random head routing and random chunk dropping to make the architecture robust and sparse histories in-distribution. At inference, it employs a bounded KV cache backed by a pose-indexed landmark bank that retrieves landmarks nearest the current pose. A metric-scale-aligned data engine unifies eight sources on one physical action scale, with palindrome trajectories providing revisit evidence for memory training. Distribution-matching distillation confined to a LoRA adapter compresses sampling to four steps, sharing one backbone for both multi-step and real-time modes.
AI.result: Against six recent interactive world models, ReWorld achieves the best control fidelity (11.95° rotation error, best camera-motion consistency) and best generation quality. On minute-long out-and-back rollouts (64s, 384 latents), its fixed 12-chunk cache regenerates the starting view, whereas sliding windows have evicted the evidence and full-KV attention runs out of memory.
AI.conclusion: ReWorld demonstrates that decoupling control and memory during training while bounding both at inference enables both real-time interactivity and long-horizon recall in a single backbone, producing 704x1280 photorealistic, game-style, and stylized videos that faithfully follow user actions and remember revisited locations.

title: IntentQA: Intent Question Answering in Videos by Cognitive Context Reasoning
comment: 18 pages, 7 figures. Accepted manuscript of an article published in IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
summary: Video understanding requires intelligent agents to transcend mere recognition of visual facts and comprehend the underlying intents behind human actions (often termed the "dark matter" of social intelligence). To bridge the gap between visual observation and intent reasoning, we introduce a novel task, IntentQA, and contribute a large-scale VideoQA dataset specifically tailored for this purpose. However, recognizing that standard metrics may overestimate capabilities due to dataset biases, we go beyond simple accuracy to rigorously evaluate model robustness. We augment the benchmark by generating five distinct contrast sets via Large Language Models (LLMs) and introducing a "Contrast Performance Decline" metric. We propose the X-CaVIR (eXplainable Context-aware Video Intent Reasoning) framework, which leverages three types of "Cognitive Context" to enhance video analysis: i) Situational Context via a cross-modal Video Query Language (VQL) module, ii) Contrastive Context via a Contrastive Learning module, and iii) Commonsense Context via a Commonsense Reasoning module. Crucially, to overcome the opacity of traditional black-box models, we refine the integration of LLMs within X-CaVIR by employing a transparent pipeline that synergizes video captions with VQA model outputs. This approach not only improves performance by effectively utilizing rich commonsense knowledge but also renders the reasoning process explicitly interpretable. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our components, the superiority of X-CaVIR over state-of-the-art baselines, and its stability against perturbations on the contrast sets.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces IntentQA, a large-scale VideoQA dataset for video intent understanding, along with five LLM-generated contrast sets and a "Contrast Performance Decline" metric for robustness evaluation. It proposes X-CaVIR, an explainable framework integrating three cognitive context modules (Situational, Contrastive, Commonsense) with a transparent LLM pipeline, demonstrating superiority over SOTA baselines and stability against perturbations.
AI.motivation: Standard video understanding focuses on visual fact recognition, overlooking the underlying intents behind human actions—the "dark matter" of social intelligence. Additionally, standard metrics may overestimate model capabilities due to dataset biases, necessitating more rigorous robustness evaluation.
AI.method: The paper contributes IntentQA, a large-scale VideoQA dataset; augments it with five contrast sets generated via LLMs and a "Contrast Performance Decline" metric; and proposes X-CaVIR, which integrates three cognitive context modules: Situational Context via a cross-modal Video Query Language (VQL) module, Contrastive Context via Contrastive Learning, and Commonsense Context via Commonsense Reasoning, combined with a transparent LLM pipeline that synergizes video captions with VQA model outputs for interpretability.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the individual components, the superiority of X-CaVIR over state-of-the-art baselines, and its stability against perturbations on the newly introduced contrast sets.
AI.conclusion: Leveraging cognitive contexts (situational, contrastive, commonsense) with a transparent, explainable LLM-integrated pipeline significantly advances video intent reasoning, both in performance and robustness against dataset biases, while rendering the reasoning process explicitly interpretable.

title: Can Coding Agents Build Robust Baselines? A Skill-Based Approach for Automating the Medical Imaging Model-Development Pipeline
summary: Developing competitive deep learning baselines for medical imaging remains a highly iterative process requiring literature review, implementation, experimentation, and expert refinement. Existing automation approaches typically optimize isolated components, such as architecture search or hyperparameter tuning, rather than the complete baseline development process. We present an agentic AI Scientist workflow that combines literature-guided reasoning, automated code generation, and hypothesis-driven experimentation to generate competitive baseline models for medical imaging challenges. The framework is evaluated on four public benchmarks spanning segmentation, classification, and detection. Across all tasks, the Experimentation Pipeline consistently improves validation performance, achieving competitive leaderboard results, including 6th place on both PUMA tracks (15 teams) and 31st place on MILK10k (125 teams). On MIDOG25, the resulting model also demonstrates strong domain generalization across scanners, tumor types, and species. Using the same workflow across all challenges without task-specific redesign, we demonstrate that skill-based, literature-guided agentic workflows can substantially reduce the engineering effort required to develop competitive medical imaging baselines.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an agentic AI Scientist workflow that combines literature-guided reasoning, automated code generation, and hypothesis-driven experimentation to autonomously develop competitive deep learning baselines for medical imaging. Evaluated on four public benchmarks (PUMA, MILK10k, MIDOG25), the framework achieves competitive leaderboard results across segmentation, classification, and detection tasks without task-specific redesign.
AI.motivation: Developing competitive deep learning baselines for medical imaging is highly iterative and labor-intensive, requiring literature review, implementation, experimentation, and expert refinement. Existing automation approaches only optimize isolated components (e.g., architecture search, hyperparameter tuning) rather than the complete baseline development pipeline, leaving a gap for end-to-end automation.
AI.method: The framework is an agentic AI Scientist workflow integrating three capabilities: (1) literature-guided reasoning to inform model design, (2) automated code generation for implementation, and (3) hypothesis-driven experimentation for iterative refinement. The same workflow is applied uniformly across all tasks without task-specific redesign.
AI.result: The Experimentation Pipeline consistently improved validation performance across all four benchmarks. It achieved 6th place on both PUMA tracks (15 teams), 31st place on MILK10k (125 teams), and strong domain generalization on MIDOG25 across scanners, tumor types, and species.
AI.conclusion: Skill-based, literature-guided agentic workflows can substantially reduce the engineering effort required to develop competitive medical imaging baselines, demonstrating that end-to-end automated baseline development is feasible.

title: Controllable blind deblurring with diffusion models
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Accepted to IEEE ICIP 2026
summary: Image acquisition with a camera involves several degradations due to the optical system, sensor, or low-level processing steps. We address blind deblurring in professional photography: we aim to invert unknown isotropic blur without knowledge of the degradation kernel. For such inverse problems,where some high-frequency information is lost, it is challenging to use generative models to produce details that are both photo-realistic and faithful to the input. We propose SuperSharpen, a diffusion-based blind deblurring method offering explicit control over restoration strength through a blur measure. We compare two conditioning strategies: a ControlNet-style adapter on a frozen backbone, and full finetuning of the diffusion prior. Our experiments show that finetuning achieves better fidelity with fewer hallucinated details. We validate our approach on synthetic and real-world blur, demonstrating improved perceptual quality and controllable restoration strength.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes SuperSharpen, a diffusion-based blind deblurring method for professional photography that inverts unknown isotropic blur without kernel knowledge, offering explicit control over restoration strength via a blur measure. It compares ControlNet-style adapter conditioning vs. full finetuning of a frozen diffusion backbone, finding finetuning yields better fidelity with fewer hallucinations, validated on synthetic and real-world blur.
AI.motivation: Camera image acquisition introduces multiple degradations (optical, sensor, processing). Blind deblurring in professional photography aims to invert unknown isotropic blur without knowing the degradation kernel. Generative models struggle to produce photo-realistic details that remain faithful to input when high-frequency information is lost, motivating a method that balances fidelity and perceptual quality with controllable restoration.
AI.method: SuperSharpen uses a diffusion-based blind deblurring framework with explicit restoration-strength control through a blur measure. Two conditioning strategies are compared: (1) a ControlNet-style adapter on a frozen diffusion backbone, and (2) full finetuning of the diffusion prior.
AI.result: Finetuning outperforms the ControlNet-style adapter in fidelity with fewer hallucinated details. The method demonstrates improved perceptual quality and controllable restoration strength on both synthetic and real-world blur.
AI.conclusion: SuperSharpen provides a diffusion-based blind deblurring solution with controllable restoration strength, showing that full finetuning of the diffusion prior yields better faithfulness than adapter-based conditioning for deblurring in professional photography.

title: DF-MoE: Generalizable Deepfake Detection via Multimodal Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
summary: Audio-visual deepfake detection is an actively studied topic, where one of the main challenges is to develop detectors able to generalize across deepfake generation methods. We conjecture that overfitting can be mitigated by extracting multiple high-level cues from the available audio and visual modalities via pre-trained models. We therefore assemble a wide variety of pre-trained models to extract features that encode mouth movements, face parsing, facial expressions, head pose, gaze tracking, heart rate, audio emotion and speech activity. We further integrate both unimodal and multimodal cues via a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) backbone to detect deepfakes. We perform in-domain and cross-domain experiments on five benchmarks for deepfake detection (MAVOS-DD, AVLips, PolyGlotFake, BioDeepAV, FakeAVCeleb) to compare our framework (DF-MoE) with state-of-the-art methods. Our results indicate that DF-MoE obtains superior deepfake detection results, surpassing all competing methods. We release our code at https://github.com/vladhondru25/DF-MoE.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces DF-MoE, an audio-visual deepfake detection framework that extracts multiple high-level cues from both modalities using a wide array of pre-trained models and integrates them via a Mixture-of-Experts backbone. DF-MoE achieves superior in-domain and cross-domain detection performance across five deepfake detection benchmarks.
AI.motivation: A key challenge in audio-visual deepfake detection is generalizing across different deepfake generation methods, as detectors tend to overfit. The authors conjecture that extracting multiple high-level cues from audio and visual modalities via pre-trained models can mitigate this overfitting.
AI.method: The framework assembles a variety of pre-trained models to extract diverse high-level features including mouth movements, face parsing, facial expressions, head pose, gaze tracking, heart rate, audio emotion, and speech activity. These unimodal and multimodal cues are integrated through a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) backbone for deepfake detection.
AI.result: DF-MoE was evaluated on both in-domain and cross-domain settings across five benchmarks: MAVOS-DD, AVLips, PolyGlotFake, BioDeepAV, and FakeAVCeleb. The framework outperformed all competing state-of-the-art deepfake detection methods.
AI.conclusion: The proposed DF-MoE framework demonstrates superior audio-visual deepfake detection performance and generalization ability, surpassing state-of-the-art methods across multiple benchmarks. The code is publicly released.

title: Long-Horizon Audio-Visual Generation for Persistent Stories and Interactive Worlds
summary: Video generation is progressing beyond isolated clips toward long-form narratives and interactive worlds, requiring models to preserve identities, follow user controls, and remain stable over extended rollouts. We present JoyAI-Echo-1.5, a unified audio-visual generation system with two purpose-built variants. The long-video variant introduces composable cross-shot memory that aggregates visual evidence across multiple prior shots and speaker cues derived from speech-filtered full-shot audio, enabling persistent character appearance and voice identity across flexible combinations of text, image, and memory conditioning. The world-model variant converts heterogeneous navigation inputs into calibrated metric 6-DoF camera trajectories and injects them through a geometry-aware conditioning pathway, enabling controller-agnostic interaction across flexible viewpoints. To support efficient long-horizon generation, we transform a bidirectional audio-visual backbone into a causal few-step generator using progressive teacher forcing and short- and long-horizon Self-Gradient Forcing on self-generated rollouts. Experiments demonstrate strong performance in both settings. JoyAI-Echo-1.5 achieves improvements over existing long-video baselines in cross-shot consistency, visual quality, text alignment, and speech fidelity. Its world-model variant ranks first on WBench, with an average score of 81.7, and achieves leading visual quality and long-horizon persistence on SANA-WM-Bench. Together, these results indicate that memory, geometric control, and rollout-aware training provide a practical foundation for generating coherent stories and continuously evolving interactive worlds. Project page: https://echo-team-joy-future-academy-jd.github.io/Echo-1.5-Page/.

AI.tldr: JoyAI-Echo-1.5 is a unified audio-visual generation system with two variants: a long-video variant using composable cross-shot memory and speaker cues for persistent character identity, and a world-model variant using calibrated metric 6-DoF camera trajectories for interactive navigation. Both variants leverage a causal few-step generator with Self-Gradient Forcing for efficient long-horizon generation, achieving state-of-the-art results including ranking first on WBench with an average score of 81.7.
AI.motivation: Video generation is advancing from isolated clips toward long-form narratives and interactive worlds, which requires models to preserve character/voice identities, follow user controls, and maintain stability over extended rollouts—capabilities that current models lack.
AI.method: The system introduces two purpose-built variants: (1) a long-video variant with composable cross-shot memory that aggregates visual evidence across prior shots plus speech-filtered speaker cues for persistent identity across flexible text/image/memory conditioning; (2) a world-model variant that converts heterogeneous navigation inputs into calibrated metric 6-DoF camera trajectories via a geometry-aware conditioning pathway. Training transforms a bidirectional audio-visual backbone into a causal few-step generator using progressive teacher forcing and short/long-horizon Self-Gradient Forcing on self-generated rollouts.
AI.result: The long-video variant achieves improvements over baselines in cross-shot consistency, visual quality, text alignment, and speech fidelity. The world-model variant ranks first on WBench with an average score of 81.7 and achieves leading visual quality and long-horizon persistence on SANA-WM-Bench.
AI.conclusion: Memory, geometric control, and rollout-aware training provide a practical foundation for generating coherent stories and continuously evolving interactive worlds.

title: Photorealistic Novel View Synthesis of Human Faces using Next-Scale Transformers
summary: Photorealistic novel view synthesis of people remains challenging at high spatial resolutions and across multiple target cameras, where preserving identity, fine appearance details, and geometric coherence is critical. We build on the next-scale autoregressive paradigm and adapt it for human-centric view synthesis by enabling higher image resolutions, multi-view outputs and stronger cross-view consistency in a single forward pass. We train on a synthetic dataset of human faces spanning diverse identities and apparel. Contrary to diffusion models, this paradigm does not need 2D pre-training and, thanks to its next-scale architecture, it benefits from lower-resolution, general-purpose pre-trainings, with the full-sized purpose-specific images being used only in the last training stages. This enables our architecture to converge with a smaller amount of purpose-specific training data, allowing us to use a smaller but more realistic training dataset. The resulting model produces sharp and realistic views, with the option to synthesize multiple novel viewpoints simultaneously for improved agreement across views. Empirically, we observe gains in perceptual fidelity and cross-view coherence on human subjects, demonstrating that next-scale autoregression is an effective backbone for scalable, multi-output human view synthesis. We also couple our pipeline with an existing transformer-based model for pixel-aligned 3D gaussian lifting from multi-view facial inputs, resulting in accurate and photorealistic 3D models of human faces.

AI.tldr: This paper adapts the next-scale autoregressive paradigm for photorealistic human-centric novel view synthesis, enabling high-resolution, multi-view outputs with strong cross-view consistency in a single forward pass. Trained on synthetic human face data, the model leverages lower-resolution pre-training for efficient convergence with limited purpose-specific data, integrates with a transformer-based 3D Gaussian lifting model, and demonstrates gains in perceptual fidelity and cross-view coherence.
AI.motivation: Photorealistic novel view synthesis of people at high spatial resolutions and across multiple target cameras remains challenging due to the need to preserve identity, fine appearance details, and geometric coherence. Existing approaches, particularly diffusion models, require 2D pre-training and large amounts of purpose-specific data, which limits scalability and realism of training data.
AI.method: The authors build on the next-scale autoregressive paradigm, extending it to support higher image resolutions, multi-view outputs, and stronger cross-view consistency in a single forward pass. The model is trained on a synthetic dataset of human faces with diverse identities and apparel. It leverages lower-resolution general-purpose pre-training, using full-resolution purpose-specific images only in final training stages, requiring less purpose-specific data. The pipeline is also coupled with a transformer-based model for pixel-aligned 3D Gaussian lifting from multi-view facial inputs.
AI.result: The resulting model produces sharp and realistic views, with an option to synthesize multiple novel viewpoints simultaneously to improve cross-view agreement. Empirical evaluation shows gains in perceptual fidelity and cross-view coherence on human subjects, and coupling with the 3D Gaussian lifting model yields accurate and photorealistic 3D models of human faces.
AI.conclusion: Next-scale autoregression proves to be an effective backbone for scalable, multi-output human view synthesis, offering advantages over diffusion-based methods in terms of training efficiency, data requirements, and the ability to use smaller but more realistic datasets while maintaining high perceptual quality and cross-view consistency.

title: Image-Conditioned Diffusion Models for Quality Assurance of Organ-at-Risk Segmentations in Radiotherapy
comment: Submitted to the MICCAI 2026 UNSURE Workshop
summary: Accurate organ-at-risk segmentation is essential for radiotherapy planning, but reviewing segmentations is time-consuming and subjective. We investigate normative modelling for segmentation error detection in head-and-neck CT, comparing a VAE framework with an image-conditioned segmentation diffusion model. Models were evaluated on RADCURE brainstem and spinal cord segmentations using simulated boundary and width perturbations. Error detection was assessed using the Dice similarity coefficient and the Distance to Agreement (DTA) between the input and reconstructed segmentations. While both models detected some simulated errors, regional DTA showed that the diffusion model localised subtle boundary errors more consistently. These results support image-conditioned diffusion reconstruction as a promising framework for localised, anatomy-aware segmentation QA.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates normative modelling for automated segmentation error detection in head-and-neck CT, comparing a VAE framework with an image-conditioned segmentation diffusion model. The diffusion model showed more consistent localization of subtle boundary errors via regional Distance to Agreement, supporting it as a promising framework for anatomy-aware segmentation QA.
AI.motivation: Manual review of organ-at-risk segmentations in radiotherapy is time-consuming and subjective, creating a need for automated methods to detect segmentation errors reliably and consistently.
AI.method: Compared a VAE-based normative modelling framework with an image-conditioned segmentation diffusion model on RADCURE brainstem and spinal cord segmentations. Simulated boundary and width perturbations were introduced, and error detection was evaluated using Dice similarity coefficient and Distance to Agreement (DTA) between input and reconstructed segmentations.
AI.result: Both models detected some simulated errors, but regional DTA analysis showed the diffusion model localized subtle boundary errors more consistently than the VAE framework.
AI.conclusion: Image-conditioned diffusion reconstruction is a promising framework for localized, anatomy-aware segmentation quality assurance in radiotherapy.

title: Towards Comprehensive Basketball Understanding
summary: Understanding a basketball game requires recognizing events, localizing actions, identifying players, and relating these to structured game knowledge. Existing benchmarks primarily evaluate these abilities one at a time, leaving the interactions among these abilities under-explored. We introduce BasketballBench, a multimodal benchmark comprising 7,980 questions across ten tasks in text, image, and video. It is built from the 2025-2026 NBA season and includes official playby-play, rosters and profiles for 530 active players, and 2,501 possession-level broadcast clips. We further propose BasketballSkills, an agent that composes eight basketball-specific perception and retrieval tools under four reusable skills that specify tool order, evidence bindings, and stopping conditions. Experiments show that current MLLMs struggle particularly on questions requiring the integration of multiple capabilities, whereas BasketballSkills outperforms them, highlighting the effectiveness of explicitly composing domain-specific capabilities for comprehensive basketball understanding.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces BasketballBench, a multimodal benchmark with 7,980 questions across ten tasks (text, image, video) built from the 2025-2026 NBA season, along with BasketballSkills, an agent that composes eight domain-specific tools under four reusable skills. Results show current MLLMs struggle on multi-capability integration tasks, while BasketballSkills outperforms them by explicitly composing domain-specific capabilities.
AI.motivation: Existing basketball understanding benchmarks evaluate individual abilities (event recognition, action localization, player identification, game knowledge grounding) in isolation, leaving the interactions among these abilities under-explored.
AI.method: Constructs BasketballBench from 2025-2026 NBA season data including play-by-play, rosters/profiles of 530 players, and 2,501 possession-level broadcast clips, comprising 7,980 questions over ten tasks. Proposes BasketballSkills, an agent composing eight perception and retrieval tools under four reusable skills that specify tool order, evidence bindings, and stopping conditions.
AI.result: Current MLLMs struggle particularly on questions requiring integration of multiple capabilities. BasketballSkills outperforms them, demonstrating the effectiveness of explicitly composing domain-specific capabilities.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly composing domain-specific perception and retrieval capabilities yields superior comprehensive basketball understanding compared to monolithic MLLM approaches.

title: Geometry-Driven Opti-Acoustic Co-Registration and View-Invariant Reflectivity Mapping for Side-Scan Sonar
summary: Side-Scan Sonar (SSS) is a primary modality for large-scale underwater mapping, yet automated perception and cross-modal alignment are severely bottlenecked by acoustic complexities such as speckle noise, shadows, and extreme viewpoint dependencies. Traditional handcrafted descriptors and modern deep learning matchers fail to bridge the physical domain gap between optical and acoustic imagery without 3D geometric constraints. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel geometry-driven framework for pixel-level opti-acoustic co-registration and view-invariant reflectivity mapping. Our method utilizes Structure-from-Motion (SfM) to reconstruct a dense 3D seafloor mesh, acting as a geometric anchor between the visual and acoustic domains. We introduce a First Bottom Return (FBR) extraction algorithm to dynamically correct non-linear altitude drift caused by uncalibrated SfM reconstruction. Furthermore, we apply an inverse Lambertian model and a dual-Gaussian weighting function to isolate the intrinsic seabed reflectivity, effectively neutralizing slant-range propagation loss and geometric view-dependence. By deterministically associating these isolated acoustic properties with optical pixels, our pipeline generates highly accurate, strictly co-registered multi-modal datasets. This automated, physics-guided approach eliminates the need for manual annotation and paves the way for advanced self-supervised learning in benthic habitat mapping.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a geometry-driven framework that uses SfM-reconstructed 3D seafloor meshes as geometric anchors to enable pixel-level co-registration between optical and acoustic (Side-Scan Sonar) imagery, incorporating FBR-based altitude correction and inverse Lambertian modeling for view-invariant reflectivity mapping.
AI.motivation: Automated underwater mapping with Side-Scan Sonar is bottlenecked by acoustic complexities (speckle noise, shadows, extreme viewpoint dependence). Existing handcrafted descriptors and deep learning matchers fail to bridge the optical-acoustic domain gap without 3D geometric constraints, and manual annotation remains a bottleneck.
AI.method: The pipeline uses Structure-from-Motion (SfM) to reconstruct a dense 3D seafloor mesh as a geometric anchor. A First Bottom Return (FBR) extraction algorithm dynamically corrects non-linear altitude drift from uncalibrated SfM. An inverse Lambertian model and dual-Gaussian weighting function isolate intrinsic seabed reflectivity by neutralizing slant-range propagation loss and geometric view dependence. Acoustic properties are then deterministically associated with optical pixels.
AI.result: The pipeline generates highly accurate, strictly co-registered multi-modal datasets automatically, eliminating the need for manual annotation and enabling advanced self-supervised learning for benthic habitat mapping.
AI.conclusion: This automated, physics-guided approach bridges the optical-acoustic domain gap without manual intervention, paving the way for self-supervised learning in benthic habitat mapping at scale.

title: SVD-Based Typicality Maps for Out-of-Distribution Detection in Vision Transformers
summary: We present a method for analyzing the internal representations of Vision Transformers (ViTs) exploiting the geometry of their learned parameters. Each affine layer's weight matrix is factored via Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), and activations are projected onto the leading right singular vectors to obtain compact, layer-intrinsic representations. A class-conditional density model is then fitted at each layer, producing per-class \emph{typicality scores} that are stacked across depth into \emph{typicality maps}: two-dimensional summaries of how class-specific evidence evolves through the network. From these maps, we derive two post-hoc scores for Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) detection: a \emph{Prototype Alignment Score} (PAS), measuring agreement with class reference prototype patterns, and a \emph{Multi-Layer Soft Voting} (MLSV) score, capturing cross-layer consensus without stored prototypes. On ViT-B/16 fine-tuned on CIFAR-100, the proposed scores achieve competitive detection performance without retraining or OOD exposure.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a post-hoc method for OOD detection in Vision Transformers without retraining or OOD exposure, based on SVD-based layer factorization, class-conditional density modeling, and two scoring schemes (PAS and MLSV) derived from typicality maps.
AI.motivation: To analyze ViT internal representations through geometric lens of learned parameters, and leverage this understanding to build post-hoc OOD detection scores that require no retraining or exposure to OOD data.
AI.method: Factor each affine layer's weight matrix via SVD, project activations onto leading right singular vectors to get compact layer-intrinsic representations, fit class-conditional density models per layer to produce typicality scores, stack these across depth into typicality maps, and derive two OOD detection scores: Prototype Alignment Score (PAS) and Multi-Layer Soft Voting (MLSV).
AI.result: On ViT-B/16 fine-tuned on CIFAR-100, the proposed scores achieve competitive OOD detection performance without retraining or OOD exposure.
AI.conclusion: Exploiting the geometry of learned parameters in ViTs enables interpretable, layer-wise typicality maps and effective post-hoc OOD detection, achieving competitive performance without additional training or OOD data.

title: Action-Aligned Retrieval with Pairwise Multimodal Reranking for Text-Based Person Anomaly Search
comment: Accepted to the AI City workshop @ ECCV 2026
summary: Text-based person anomaly search requires distinguishing individuals based on fine-grained, context-dependent behaviors rather than mere appearance. Existing methods struggle to capture these context-conditioned actions, frequently relying on isolated skeletal geometry, discarding raw query details during reformulation, or utilizing absolute pointwise scoring for multimodal verification. To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{ActPair}, a unified three-stage coarse-to-fine framework that combines action-aligned retrieval with pairwise multimodal reranking to bridge the pose-semantic gap. First, we fine-tune a vision-language model (VLM) with an action-aligned multi-task objective that encourages the representations to encode action-discriminative semantics. Second, we perform parallel late-fusion retrieval using the original query and a large language model (LLM)-generated context-grounded rewrite, retaining complementary details from both semantic views. Finally, we propose an efficient off-the-shelf reranking module that leverages a pivot-promote algorithm to perform direct pairwise visual comparisons, mitigating residual spatial and compositional ambiguities without the prohibitive inference costs of exhaustive evaluation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework achieves the best results among the compared methods on the Pedestrian Anomaly Behavior (PAB) public test and transfers effectively to an unseen, non-anomaly-specific dataset.

AI.tldr: ActPair is a unified three-stage coarse-to-fine framework for text-based person anomaly search that combines action-aligned retrieval with pairwise multimodal reranking, achieving state-of-the-art results on the PAB dataset and transferring effectively to unseen datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing methods for text-based person anomaly search fail to capture fine-grained, context-dependent behaviors because they rely on isolated skeletal geometry, discard raw query details during reformulation, or use absolute pointwise scoring for multimodal verification.
AI.method: ActPair consists of three stages: (1) fine-tuning a vision-language model (VLM) with an action-aligned multi-task objective to encode action-discriminative semantics; (2) parallel late-fusion retrieval using both the original query and an LLM-generated context-grounded rewrite to retain complementary semantic details; (3) an efficient off-the-shelf reranking module using a pivot-promote algorithm for direct pairwise visual comparisons, avoiding exhaustive evaluation costs.
AI.result: The framework achieves the best results among compared methods on the Pedestrian Anomaly Behavior (PAB) public test set and demonstrates effective transfer to an unseen, non-anomaly-specific dataset.
AI.conclusion: By addressing the pose-semantic gap through action-aligned representation learning, dual-view query fusion, and efficient pairwise reranking, ActPair provides a robust solution for context-dependent person anomaly search with strong generalization.

title: Investigating Relational Reasoning in VLMs
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) achieve strong performance in visual reasoning tasks, but it remains unclear whether they understand visual relations, or simply employ shortcuts such as language cues or priors. To investigate this, we use the Qwen3-VL-4B (Bai et al., 2025), a modern VLM, to decode how visual information is encoded across depths. For this, we propose a synthetic dataset of simple geometric shapes for controlled analysis, along with queries crafted to precisely test language cues. Furthermore, the dataset is modified to test causal reliance on visual evidence. Our results show that current VLMs combine genuine visual reasoning with shortcut strategies primarily rooted in language cues.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether Vision-Language Models (VLMs) truly understand visual relations or rely on shortcuts such as language cues. Using the Qwen3-VL-4B model, a synthetic dataset of geometric shapes, and carefully crafted queries, the authors decode how visual information is encoded across model depths. Results show that current VLMs combine genuine visual reasoning with shortcut strategies primarily rooted in language cues.
AI.motivation: VLMs perform well on visual reasoning tasks, but it is unclear whether they genuinely understand visual relations or exploit shortcuts such as language cues and priors. This ambiguity motivates a controlled investigation into how visual information is actually processed within these models.
AI.method: The authors use the Qwen3-VL-4B VLM and decode how visual information is encoded across different model depths. They construct a synthetic dataset of simple geometric shapes for controlled analysis, craft queries to precisely test language cues, and modify the dataset to test causal reliance on visual evidence.
AI.result: Current VLMs combine genuine visual reasoning with shortcut strategies primarily rooted in language cues, indicating a hybrid behavior rather than pure visual understanding or pure shortcut reliance.
AI.conclusion: VLMs do not fully rely on visual evidence alone; they integrate genuine visual reasoning with language-based shortcuts. This suggests that more robust evaluation and training methods are needed to reduce shortcut reliance in VLMs.

title: Predicting Multiple Clinical Outcomes Related to Functional Recovery and Social Isolation Among Older Adults After Lower-Limb Fracture or Hip Replacement
summary: Older adults recovering after lower-limb fracture or hip replacement may experience complex recovery trajectories. Most of the time, these clinical aspects are studied in isolation, masking their joint impact on recovery. This study used the MAISON-LLF dataset, which contains multimodal sensor and clinical assessment data from 18 older adults recovering in the community after lower-limb fracture or hip replacement. Participants were monitored for up to eight weeks, corresponding to a maximum of 1,008 participant-days of sensor monitoring. Forty-six daily features were extracted from indoor motion, acceleration, step count, heart rate, out-of-home mobility, and sleep data. Five clinical outcomes were assessed every two weeks: the Social Isolation Scale, Oxford Hip Score, Oxford Knee Score, Timed Up and Go test, and 30-second Chair Stand test. We utilize an inherent relationship between multi-modal sensor data and different clinical scores and formulate it as a multi-output regression problem. We tested various machine learning and deep learning single- and multi-output regression algorithms to predict these scores simultaneously. The results showed that predicting clinical scores jointly was better than separately. The tabular DL multi-output regressor, NODE, gave a remarkable performance of MSE=3.96 and MAE=1.02 in comparison to other multi- and single-output regressors. The SHAP feature analysis further showed the importance of including multimodal sensors to provide a good estimate of patients' recovery trajectory. This work may support the simultaneous assessment of functional recovery and social engagement among community-dwelling older adults and ultimately help improve their care and quality of life.

AI.tldr: This study predicts five clinical recovery outcomes simultaneously from 46 daily multimodal sensor features using multi-output regression on the MAISON-LLF dataset (18 older adults, up to 1,008 participant-days). Joint prediction outperformed single-output approaches, with the tabular deep learning regressor NODE achieving best performance (MSE=3.96, MAE=1.02), and SHAP analysis confirmed the value of multimodal sensing for assessing recovery trajectories.
AI.motivation: Older adults recovering after lower-limb fracture or hip replacement experience complex recovery trajectories, yet clinical aspects are typically studied in isolation, masking their joint impact on recovery. The authors aim to model the inherent relationship between multimodal sensor data and multiple clinical outcomes simultaneously.
AI.method: Using the MAISON-LLF dataset with sensor and clinical data from 18 older adults monitored up to eight weeks (1,008 participant-days), 46 daily features were extracted from indoor motion, acceleration, step count, heart rate, out-of-home mobility, and sleep. Five clinical scores (Social Isolation Scale, Oxford Hip/Knee Score, Timed Up and Go, 30-second Chair Stand) were assessed biweekly. The task was formulated as multi-output regression, comparing various machine learning and deep learning single- and multi-output regression algorithms, including the tabular deep learning model NODE, with SHAP used for feature importance analysis.
AI.result: Joint (multi-output) prediction of clinical scores outperformed separate (single-output) prediction.
