The tabular DL multi-output regressor NODE achieved the best performance with MSE=3.96 and MAE=1.02 compared to other regressors. SHAP analysis demonstrated the importance of including multimodal sensors for accurate recovery trajectory estimation.
AI.conclusion: Multi-output regression with multimodal sensor data can simultaneously assess functional recovery and social engagement in community-dwelling older adults post lower-limb fracture or hip replacement, potentially supporting improved care and quality of life.

title: FixAnything: 3D-Consistent Rendering Refinement via Video Generative Priors
comment: Appearing in ECCV 2026. Project page: https://fix-anything.github.io
summary: Rendering views using 3D scene representations such as Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF), meshes, or even point clouds produces artifacts when input views are sparse or target views lie far from the input. Recent work mitigates these artifacts using diffusion-based generative priors, but is specialized to individual representations and require custom architectures or extensive retraining. We present FixAnything, a single model for fixing a wide range of rendering artifacts. It does so by repurposing a pretrained video generative model, leveraging its implicit multi-view priors with only minimal modification and lightweight finetuning. Our key insight is that even noisily-rendered sequences preserve camera motion and coarse scene structure, allowing cleanup to be formulated as video-to-video translation. To control what scene structure should be preserved, we introduce a binary mask denoting the clean pixels, enabling the model to anchor its output to high-quality inputs (e.g. training views) while refining the rest. To encourage FixAnything to produce 3D-consistent renderings that support downstream reconstruction, we use camera pose accuracy (recovered via structure-from-motion) as a reward signal for direct preference optimization (DPO). Across four distinct 3D representations, FixAnything consistently improves rendering quality with lightweight finetuning, demonstrating that a single generalist video prior can replace multiple specialist refinement pipelines. The simplicity of the framework enables immediate adoption of stronger future video models without architectural redesign.

AI.tldr: FixAnything is a single model that repurposes a pretrained video generative model via lightweight finetuning to fix rendering artifacts across diverse 3D representations (Gaussian Splatting, NeRF, meshes, point clouds), using binary masks to anchor clean pixels and DPO with camera pose accuracy as a reward to ensure 3D consistency.
AI.motivation: Rendering artifacts arise across various 3D representations when input views are sparse or target views are far from inputs. Existing diffusion-based priors are specialized to individual representations, requiring custom architectures and extensive retraining. A single generalist solution is needed.
AI.method: FixAnything formulates artifact cleanup as video-to-video translation using a pretrained video generative model with minimal modification and lightweight finetuning. It introduces a binary mask to flag clean pixels, anchoring outputs to high-quality inputs while refining the rest. It employs direct preference optimization (DPO) with camera pose accuracy (from structure-from-motion) as a reward signal to enforce 3D consistency.
AI.result: FixAnything consistently improves rendering quality across four distinct 3D representations (3DGS, NeRF, meshes, point clouds) with lightweight finetuning, demonstrating that a single generalist video prior can replace multiple specialist refinement pipelines.
AI.conclusion: A single generalist video generative prior can serve as a universal artifact-fixing model across multiple 3D representations, and the framework's simplicity enables immediate adoption of stronger future video models without architectural redesign.

title: EG-ARSA: An Expert-Grounded Open Model for Visual Road Safety Auditing in Low-Resource Settings
summary: Road traffic injuries remain a major challenge in low- and middle-income countries, where proactive road safety auditing is limited by incomplete crash records, shortages of qualified auditors, and the high cost of large-scale field inspections. To address this problem, we propose Expert-Grounded Distillation (EGD), a novel artificial intelligence framework that transfers institutional road safety expertise into a compact vision-language model for scalable visual road safety auditing. The key innovation is a quantified expert-grounding stage in which the teacher vision-language model is calibrated against authoritative field audits. Large-scale annotation is permitted only after the teacher reaches substantial agreement with expert risk assessments (Cohen's kappa = 0.74). The calibrated teacher then generates structured supervision that is distilled into an 8-billion-parameter student vision-language model using Low-Rank Adaptation and a single leakage-free prompt. We also introduce Bangladesh Road Safety Audit (BD-ARSA), the first open, expert-grounded Bangladeshi visual road safety audit dataset containing 21,947 image-audit records with near-national coverage, and Expert-Grounded Road Safety Auditor (EG-ARSA), the first vision-language model developed specifically for this task. Experimental results show that grounded fine-tuning substantially improves ordinal risk assessment over the zero-shot baseline, while blind expert evaluation demonstrates that the compact student outperforms both its 31 billion-parameter teacher and Gemini-2.5-Flash. These findings demonstrate that EGD provides an effective and scalable engineering solution for proactive road safety auditing in resource-constrained environments.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Expert-Grounded Distillation (EGD), an AI framework that transfers institutional road safety expertise into a compact 8B-parameter vision-language model for scalable visual road safety auditing. It also introduces BD-ARSA, the first open expert-grounded Bangladeshi visual road safety audit dataset (21,947 records), and EG-ARSA, the first vision-language model for this task. Results show the compact student outperforms its 31B teacher and Gemini-2.5-Flash in blind expert evaluation.
AI.motivation: Road traffic injuries are a major challenge in low- and middle-income countries, where proactive road safety auditing is limited by incomplete crash records, shortages of qualified auditors, and high costs of large-scale field inspections. An scalable AI-based solution is needed to address these resource constraints.
AI.method: The EGD framework uses a two-stage approach: (1) a quantified expert-grounding stage where a teacher vision-language model is calibrated against authoritative field audits (Cohen's kappa = 0.74) to only allow large-scale annotation after substantial agreement; (2) a distillation stage where the calibrated teacher generates structured supervision, distilled into an 8B-parameter student model using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) and a single leakage-free prompt. A new dataset (BD-ARSA) with 21,947 image-audit records was constructed.
AI.result: Grounded fine-tuning substantially improves ordinal risk assessment over the zero-shot baseline. Blind expert evaluation shows the compact 8B student outperforms both the 31B teacher model and Gemini-2.5-Flash. The framework demonstrates effectiveness and scalability for road safety auditing in resource-constrained environments.
AI.conclusion: EGD provides an effective and scalable engineering solution for proactive road safety auditing in low- and middle-income countries, enabling compact models to surpass much larger counterparts through expert-grounded knowledge distillation.

title: Reproducible Vision-Guided 6-DoF Robotic Manipulator with a Mixed Stepper-Driver Architecture and Browser-Native Control
comment: 13 pages, 16 figures, 7 tables. Design files and firmware: https://github.com/Lasan-Perera/6-dof-arm-neuralnexus
summary: We present the NeuralNexus Arm, an open, low-cost 6-DOF robotic manipulator built by an undergraduate engineering team, together with the design decisions and debugging experience needed to reproduce it. The arm is driven by a single STM32H743 microcontroller on a custom printed circuit board (PCB) and combines two stepper-driver strategies on one controller: push-pull 3.3 V step/direction outputs for onboard TMC2209 drivers on the three wrist joints, and open-drain outputs for external CL57T and DM542 drivers on the three high-torque proximal joints. We describe the mechanical design, mixed-driver electronics, interrupt-driven firmware, a MATLAB/Simscape-based inverse-kinematics pipeline, a browser-native control interface using the Web Serial API, and a lightweight vision pipeline for object localisation and autonomous pick-and-place tasks. We also document non-obvious hardware and firmware failure modes encountered during the transition from a development board to the custom PCB as reproducibility guidance. All design files and firmware are released openly. The platform actuates all six axes under coordinated control at a 2 kHz update rate and executes both manual and pre-recorded motions from the browser interface.

AI.tldr: This paper presents NeuralNexus Arm, an open-source, low-cost 6-DOF robotic manipulator built by an undergraduate engineering team. It combines a custom STM32H743-based PCB with mixed stepper-driver strategies (onboard TMC2209 for wrist joints, external CL57T/DM542 for proximal joints), including mechanical design, firmware, inverse-kinematics, web-based control, and vision-based pick-and-place. Failure modes from the dev-board-to-PCB transition are documented as reproducibility guidance; all design files are openly released.
AI.motivation: To provide an open, affordable, and reproducible 6-DOF robotic manipulator platform with detailed design rationale and debugging guidance, lowering the barrier for educational and research use of articulated robotic arms.
AI.method: The system uses a single STM32H743 microcontroller on a custom PCB with two stepper-driver strategies: push-pull 3.3V step/direction outputs for onboard TMC2209 drivers (three wrist joints) and open-drain outputs for external CL57T/DM542 drivers (three proximal joints). The pipeline includes interrupt-driven firmware, a MATLAB/Simscape inverse-kinematics pipeline, a browser-native control interface via the Web Serial API, and a lightweight vision pipeline for pick-and-place. Non-obvious failure modes from the development-board-to-custom-PCB transition are documented.
AI.result: The platform actuates all six axes under coordinated control at a 2 kHz update rate and executes both manual and pre-recorded motion sequences from the browser interface.
AI.conclusion: The NeuralNexus Arm demonstrates a viable, low-cost, fully open 6-DOF manipulator built by an undergraduate team, with reproducible design files and practical debugging guidance for the broader robotics community.

title: Pointing-VLA: Typed Spatial Grounding Interfaces for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models often expose spatial grounding through autoregressive text coordinates or opaque action tokens, creating brittle interfaces between multimodal reasoning and robot execution. We present Pointing-VLA, a typed hidden-state spatial readout built on Embodied-R1. Geometry-specific heads predict normalized points, object-functional grounding (OFG) heatmaps, and visual trajectories without serializing geometry as text. For the evaluated Bridge/WidowX and physical pick-place deployments, an explicit execution contract assigns PICK to source-conditioned OFG and PLACE to Pointing, providing direct stage-aligned spatial targets. Pointing-VLA achieves SOTA performance on Bridge/WidowX, averaging 72.9\% across the evaluated four-task set without Bridge-specific finetuning under collision-enabled CuRobo execution. Pointing and OFG show complementary strengths across native and cross-dataset evaluations. The OFG/contact readout transfers to NORA-1.5, preserving or improving success while reducing recorded controller time by more than 20$\times$; typed heads are also 6.68--6.90$\times$ faster than Embodied-R1 text decoding on a shared external suite. When integrated as spatial guidance for a $π_{0.5}$ action policy, Pointing-VLA raises autonomous real-robot success from 52.7\% to 80.7\% across three visual contexts. These results establish typed spatial readouts as an efficient, inspectable interface between embodied reasoning and robot execution.

AI.tldr: Pointing-VLA proposes typed hidden-state spatial readouts (pointing, object-functional grounding heatmaps, and visual trajectories) as an alternative to text-based coordinate or opaque action token interfaces in VLA models. Built on Embodied-R1, it achieves SOTA performance on Bridge/WidowX and improves real-robot success from 52.7% to 80.7% when guiding a π0.5 policy.
AI.motivation: Existing VLA models expose spatial grounding through brittle interfaces—either autoregressive text coordinates or opaque action tokens—creating a mismatch between multimodal reasoning and robot execution. These serialized or opaque formats are inefficient, non-inspectable, and poorly aligned with stage-level task semantics.
AI.method: Pointing-VLA introduces typed hidden-state spatial readout heads on Embodied-R1: (1) geometry-specific heads predict normalized points, (2) object-functional grounding (OFG) heatmaps, and (3) visual trajectories, avoiding text serialization of geometry. An explicit execution contract assigns PICK to source-conditioned OFG and PLACE to Pointing, enabling stage-aligned spatial targets. The approach is evaluated on Bridge/WidowX and physical pick-place tasks, with readouts also transferred to NORA-1.5 and integrated as spatial guidance for a π0.5 action policy.
AI.result: Pointing-VLA achieves SOTA on Bridge/WidowX with 72.9% average across four tasks without Bridge-specific finetuning under collision-enabled CuRobo execution. OFG/contact readouts transfer to NORA-1.5 preserving/improving success while reducing controller time over 20×; typed heads are 6.68–6.90× faster than text decoding. As spatial guidance for π0.5, real-robot success improves from 52.7% to 80.7% across three visual contexts.
AI.conclusion: Typed spatial readouts serve as an efficient, inspectable, and complementary interface between embodied reasoning and robot execution, outperforming both text-coordinate interfaces and unguided action policies while transferring across different robot platforms.

title: Think Only When Needed: Prompt-Authority Control for Selective Slow-Path Intervention in Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
summary: Retrieval can efficiently and effectively augment a frozen vision--language--action (VLA) policy without retraining, yet retrieved text becomes a control intervention once it enters the executed prompt. In a matched audit, raw appended text reduces mean success from 92.47\% to 3.00\%, while meaningful and length-matched meaningless appends both fail on all 500 states. This result identifies \emph{prompt-form collapse}: changing the instruction form, rather than adding useful semantics, can dominate execution. We introduce TOWN-VLA (Think Only When Needed), a prompt-authority interface that separates candidate generation from permission to alter the policy input. A fixed compatibility rule authorizes a canonical compact instruction; otherwise, the interface restores the original Base prompt exactly. Across 900 audited routes, every route follows this contract: 525 routes recover Base with matching hashes, and all 375 authorized prompts preserve the task signature. On a matched $4\times7$ LIBERO-Plus evaluation with 10{,}030 episodes per method, success rises from 69.5\% to 73.1\% ($+362$ episodes; 95\% CI 1.89--5.45 points), improving on six perturbation axes and all four suites. On a physical PiPER arm with a frozen \pizerofive{} checkpoint, success rises from 52.7\% to 78.7\% over 150 trials per method ($p=3.16\times10^{-6}$). Prompt authority is enforceable for a frozen controller; oracle-free admission calibration is the next deployment target.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces TOWN-VLA (Think Only When Needed), a prompt-authority interface for frozen vision-language-action (VLA) policies. It identifies "prompt-form collapse"—where changing the instruction form rather than adding semantics can dominate execution, dropping success from 92.47% to 3.00% in a matched audit. TOWN-VLA separates candidate generation from permission to alter policy input via a fixed compatibility rule, improving success from 69.5% to 73.1% on LIBERO-Plus and from 52.7% to 78.7% on a physical PiPER arm while ensuring every route follows the authorization contract.
AI.motivation: Retrieval-augmented frozen VLA policies can suffer from prompt-form collapse, where merely changing the instruction format—not the content—catastrophically degrades performance. This creates an urgent need for a mechanism that controls when and how retrieved text may alter the executed prompt.
AI.method: The authors audit retrieval effects on a frozen VLA policy, demonstrating prompt-form collapse via matched comparisons. They then design TOWN-VLA, a prompt-authority interface that separates candidate generation from permission to alter the policy input. A fixed compatibility rule authorizes a canonical compact instruction; otherwise, the original Base prompt is restored exactly.
AI.result: Across 900 audited routes, all follow the contract (525 recover Base with matching hashes; 375 authorized prompts preserve task signatures). On a matched 4x7 LIBERO-Plus evaluation with 10,030 episodes per method, success rises from 69.5% to 73.1% (+362 episodes; 95% CI 1.89–5.45 points). On a physical PiPER arm with frozen PiZeroFive, success rises from 52.7% to 78.7% over 150 trials (p=3.16e-6).
AI.conclusion: Prompt authority is enforceable for frozen controllers, making retrieved text safe for use in VLA policies. Oracle-free admission calibration is identified as the next deployment target.

title: OptiSight: Bridging Semantic Reasoning and Geometric Control for Embodied Navigation
summary: Autonomous indoor navigation requires both semantic understanding and precise geometric control. We propose OptiSight, a hybrid framework that combines Vision-Language Model reasoning with deterministic visual servoing through a finite-state Chain-of-Thought architecture. Grounded-SAM localizes open-vocabulary targets, while camera projection geometry converts visual observations into navigation commands without requiring dense mapping. The VLM is queried only at key decision points, reducing computational overhead while geometric control handles continuous navigation. Experiments in AI Habitat demonstrate reliable zero-shot navigation across diverse indoor scenarios, including obstacle avoidance and semantic ambiguity, while operating within an 8~GB VRAM budget. The source code is available at https://github.com/avanalperen/OptiSight-Python-Multimodal-CoT-for-Visual-Reasoning.

AI.tldr: OptiSight is a hybrid autonomous indoor navigation framework combining Vision-Language Model reasoning with deterministic visual servoing via a finite-state Chain-of-Thought architecture, achieving zero-shot navigation in AI Habitat within an 8 GB VRAM budget.
AI.motivation: Autonomous indoor navigation requires both semantic understanding and precise geometric control, which pure VLM approaches or traditional geometric methods individually fail to provide efficiently.
AI.method: Ground-SAM localizes open-vocabulary targets and camera projection geometry converts visual observations into navigation commands without dense mapping. The VLM is queried only at key decision points through a finite-state Chain-of-Thought architecture, while geometric control handles continuous navigation.
AI.result: Reliable zero-shot navigation across diverse indoor scenarios including obstacle avoidance and semantic ambiguity, operating within an 8 GB VRAM budget in AI Habitat experiments.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid approach demonstrates that combining VLM reasoning with deterministic geometric control provides an efficient and robust solution for autonomous indoor navigation, balancing semantic flexibility with precise control while keeping computational overhead low.

title: Training-Free VLM Personalization via Calibrated Residual Decoding
summary:
Vision-language models can be personalized in a training-free manner by directly providing user profiles, preferences, or visual references at inference time, without updating model parameters. However, direct personalized prompting does not guarantee that the model will reliably exploit such evidence. The predictive distribution under the positive user profile often mixes two sources: personalized signals genuinely supported by the current profile, and the model's generic visual or linguistic priors. As a result, from the positive-profile response alone, it is difficult to determine whether a high-confidence answer is supported by the user profile or merely reflects the model's default preference. To address this problem, we propose a training-free calibrated residual decoding framework. Given the same image and question, we construct three evidence conditions: a positive profile , a counterfactual profile , and an empty profile . Our method keeps the prediction under
  as the anchored base, and explicitly estimates the marginal contribution of personalization from score differences across the three conditions. We further introduce normalized-entropy-based uncertainty calibration, allowing the strength of personalized enhancement to adapt to the reliability of the residual signal. Experiments on MMPB, YoLLaVA, and MyVLM show that the proposed method improves personalized multimodal understanding without fine-tuning, with consistent gains on identity-sensitive visual personalization tasks. Additional analysis shows that entropy calibration stabilizes residual decoding when the contrastive personalization signal is uncertain.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a training-free calibrated residual decoding framework for reliable personalization of vision-language models. By contrasting predictions under positive, counterfactual, and empty user profiles, it isolates the marginal contribution of personalization and applies normalized-entropy-based uncertainty calibration to adaptively control personalized enhancement strength, improving performance on identity-sensitive multimodal tasks without fine-tuning.
AI.motivation: Direct personalized prompting in vision-language models does not guarantee reliable exploitation of user profile evidence, because high-confidence predictions under positive profiles may mix genuine personalized signals with the model's generic visual/linguistic priors, making it difficult to determine whether an answer is truly supported by the user profile or merely reflects default preferences.
AI.method: The proposed training-free calibrated residual decoding framework constructs three evidence conditions—positive profile, counterfactual profile, and empty profile—for the same image and question. It anchors prediction on the positive profile while explicitly estimating the marginal contribution of personalization from score differences across all three conditions. Additionally, normalized-entropy-based uncertainty calibration adaptively adjusts the strength of personalized enhancement based on the reliability of the residual signal.
AI.result: Experiments on MMPB, YoLLaVA, and MyVLM benchmarks demonstrate consistent performance improvements in personalized multimodal understanding without fine-tuning, with particular gains on identity-sensitive visual personalization tasks. Additional analysis shows that entropy calibration stabilizes residual decoding when the contrastive personalization signal is uncertain.
AI.conclusion: The calibrated residual decoding framework effectively disentangles genuine personalization from generic model priors and provides robust, training-free personalization capability for vision-language models, validated across multiple benchmarks and tasks.

title: GAN-Diff : Coupling Pretrained WGAN-GP Features with Conditional Diffusion U-Nets
summary: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) can provide efficient image generation, while diffusion models offer high-quality image restoration but require iterative sampling. This paper presents a hybrid GAN-guided diffusion framework that uses a pretrained Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) as a feature prior for conditional diffusion-based image restoration. Intermediate features from the frozen WGAN-GP generator are incorporated into a diffusion U-Net through cross-attention and remain fixed during the DDIM sampling process. The framework is evaluated on two restoration tasks, Gaussian denoising and 2Xsuper-resolution, using CelebA face images. During development, several sources of instability were identified and addressed, including adversarial learning-rate imbalance, inappropriate diffusion initialization, excessive corruption, and insufficient parameter averaging. The resulting framework consistently improves the quality of both degraded and low-resolution images. In particular, it improves denoising performance by 4.40 dB in PSNR and super-resolution performance by 3.70 dB over their respective input baselines. These results demonstrate the potential of a frozen GAN feature prior to guide diffusion models toward stable and effective image restoration.

AI.tldr: A hybrid GAN-guided diffusion framework uses a frozen WGAN-GP generator as a feature prior for conditional diffusion-based image restoration, improving denoising by 4.40 dB PSNR and 2× super-resolution by 3.70 dB over input baselines on CelebA images.
AI.motivation: GANs offer efficient image generation but lack high-quality restoration fidelity, while diffusion models produce excellent restoration but require iterative sampling. The paper seeks a hybrid approach that leverages the strengths of both—using a GAN as a stable feature prior to guide diffusion-based restoration.
AI.method: A pretrained WGAN-GP is frozen and used as a feature extractor. Intermediate features from its generator are injected into a diffusion U-Net via cross-attention, with these features kept fixed throughout DDIM sampling. The framework addresses identified instabilities including adversarial learning-rate imbalance, improper diffusion initialization, excessive corruption, and insufficient parameter averaging.
AI.result: On CelebA face images, the framework achieves 4.40 dB PSNR improvement for Gaussian denoising and 3.70 dB improvement for 2× super-resolution over their respective input baselines, consistently improving the quality of both degraded and low-resolution images.
AI.conclusion: A frozen GAN feature prior can effectively guide diffusion models toward stable and effective image restoration, demonstrating that hybrid GAN-diffusion designs are a viable strategy for balancing efficiency and restoration quality.

title: OVIBench: Benchmarking Online Video Question Answering under Interruption
summary: Recent vision language models (VLMs) have achieved strong progress in video understanding. However, most existing video QA research and benchmarks still follow an offline, single-round paradigm, overlooking realistic interactions where users may interrupt the model during answer generation. To address this gap, we formulate the task of Online Video Question Answering under Interruption and introduce OVIBench, the first standardized benchmark for evaluating VLMs in this setting. OVIBench categorizes interruptions into three types: Cancellation, False Trigger, Correction and supports both open-ended and multiple-choice evaluations. To enable large-scale and reproducible testing, we develop an offline simulation protocol that reproduces interruption during generation under a unified temporal setup, together with a multi-dimensional metric suite for assessing interruption understanding and response generation. Experiments demonstrate that OVIBench effectively distinguishes models' interruption-handling abilities, especially in following correction requests. Finally, we construct a train set OVI-Train for interruption-aware fine-tuning. Models fine-tuned on this dataset achieve significant gains on OVIBench, validating the effectiveness of our benchmark and data design. OVIBench, OVI-Train, and the evaluation code will be released.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces OVIBench, the first standardized benchmark for evaluating vision language models on the task of Online Video Question Answering under Interruption, where users may interrupt models mid-generation. It categorizes interruptions into Cancellation, False Trigger, and Correction, and provides an offline simulation protocol with a multi-dimensional metric suite. The authors also construct OVI-Train for interruption-aware fine-tuning and demonstrate significant gains on OVIBench.
AI.motivation: Existing video QA research and benchmarks follow an offline, single-round paradigm that overlooks realistic interactions where users may interrupt the model during answer generation. This gap prevents VLMs from being evaluated in practical, interactive video understanding scenarios.
AI.method: The authors formulate the task of Online Video Question Answering under Interruption, categorize interruptions into three types (Cancellation, False Trigger, Correction), and build OVIBench as a benchmark supporting both open-ended and multiple-choice evaluations. They develop an offline simulation protocol reproducing interruptions during generation under a unified temporal setup, along with a multi-dimensional metric suite. They also construct OVI-Train for interruption-aware fine-tuning.
AI.result: Experiments show that OVIBench effectively distinguishes models' interruption-handling abilities, particularly in following correction requests. Models fine-tuned on OVI-Train achieve significant gains on OVIBench, validating the benchmark and data design.
AI.conclusion: The proposed OVIBench benchmark and OVI-Train dataset enable evaluation and improvement of VLMs' interruption-handling capabilities in online video QA, and will be released to the community.

title: Hybrid Panels: Toward Human-AI Collaboration in Survey Research
summary: Large-scale population surveys are essential for generating robust social and scientific insights, yet they face significant challenges, including declining response rates, increasing data collection costs, long delays between data collection and data provision, and the risk of nonresponse bias. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have opened up new opportunities for AI-supported survey infrastructures where the goal is to overcome these challenges without limiting the data quality. A promising AI-enabled survey infrastructure for which we build a first pilot is a hybrid panel. A hybrid panel is a longitudinal AI-enabled survey which allows to iteratively improve the alignment between large language models (LLMs) and the population they aim to simulate and use the errors to inform the design and implementation of the next survey wave (e.g., inform the participant recruitment, assignment of questions to participants). It incorporates both human participants and LLMs as fundamental elements of its design. In this research note, we introduce the concept of a hybrid panel by providing a definition and outlining an overarching framework, spanning data collection to data validation. We detail results from a first pilot study to illustrate (open) challenges that we identify for hybrid panels.

AI.tldr: This research note introduces the concept of a "hybrid panel"—a longitudinal AI-enabled survey infrastructure that integrates both human participants and large language models (LLMs) to address challenges in large-scale population surveys such as declining response rates, high costs, data delays, and nonresponse bias. The authors provide a definition, an overarching framework spanning data collection to validation, and results from a first pilot study that illustrates open challenges for hybrid panels.
AI.motivation: Large-scale population surveys face significant challenges including declining response rates, rising data collection costs, long delays between data collection and provision, and nonresponse bias. The authors aim to leverage advances in AI to build survey infrastructures that overcome these challenges without compromising data quality.
AI.method: The paper introduces the concept of a hybrid panel—a longitudinal AI-enabled survey that iteratively improves alignment between LLMs and the target population, using errors to inform subsequent survey wave design (e.g., participant recruitment, question assignment). The framework integrates human participants and LLMs as fundamental design elements, spanning data collection to data validation. A first pilot study was conducted to test the concept.
AI.result: The authors detail results from a first pilot study that illustrates open challenges for hybrid panels, though specific quantitative results are not detailed in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: Hybrid panels represent a promising AI-enabled survey infrastructure that can potentially address current survey challenges; however, open challenges remain and are illustrated through the pilot study, requiring further development and validation.

title: Teaching LLMs How ICU Physicians Approach Clinical Reasoning Through OMOP-Aligned Retrieval Improves Reasoning Across Clinical Domains
summary: Clinical decision-making relies on identifying relevant patient information to guide diagnosis and treatment, a challenge that is especially difficult in the data-dense and rapidly changing intensive care unit (ICU). Large language models (LLMs) could support this task. However, existing applications and datasets mostly emphasize surface-level retrieval or factual recall rather than the inductive and deductive reasoning clinicians practice to select and reason over decision-relevant evidence. We hypothesized that training LLMs on expert ICU reasoning could yield clinical reasoning skills that generalize beyond critical care. Here we introduce ICU-REACT, a reasoning dataset developed with 19 clinicians through a clinician-in-the-loop framework to teach LLMs to perform information retrieval and context-aware clinical reasoning in the ICU. Using ICU-REACT, we fine-tuned Clin-REACT models spanning 8B-70B parameters and three model families. Across five clinical reasoning benchmarks, Clin-REACT consistently outperformed its backbone models and open-source general-purpose and medical LLMs. Gains extended to different tasks including script concordance tests, and downstream diagnosis and treatment tasks. These findings suggest that expert reasoning supervision in critical care can improve broader clinical reasoning, although prospective evaluation is needed before real-world clinical use.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces ICU-REACT, a clinician-in-the-loop reasoning dataset for training LLMs on ICU clinical reasoning, and Clin-REACT models (8B-70B parameters) that outperform baseline and medical LLMs across five clinical reasoning benchmarks, demonstrating that expert ICU reasoning supervision can generalize to broader clinical reasoning tasks.
AI.motivation: Clinical decision-making in the ICU is challenging due to data density and rapid change. While LLMs could support this task, existing applications and datasets emphasize surface-level retrieval or factual recall rather than the inductive and deductive reasoning that clinicians actually practice. The authors hypothesized that training LLMs on expert ICU reasoning could produce reasoning skills that generalize beyond critical care.
AI.method: The authors developed ICU-REACT, a reasoning dataset created with 19 clinicians through a clinician-in-the-loop framework, designed to teach LLMs information retrieval and context-aware clinical reasoning in the ICU. Using this dataset, they fine-tuned Clin-REACT models spanning 8B-70B parameters across three model families.
AI.result: Across five clinical reasoning benchmarks, Clin-REACT consistently outperformed its backbone models as well as open-source general-purpose and medical LLMs. The gains extended to different tasks including script concordance tests, and downstream diagnosis and treatment tasks.
AI.conclusion: Expert reasoning supervision in critical care can improve broader clinical reasoning in LLMs, although prospective evaluation is needed before real-world clinical use.

title: GeoRisk-RAG: A Hierarchy-Aware Risk Framework for Improving RAG Reliability through Selective Answering
summary: Current work on improving reliability in large language model (LLM)- generated answers has primarily leveraged Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), knowledge-graph augmentation, and reinforcement learning. While these methods are adept at enhancing and measuring reliability through semantic similarity and faithfulness, they often struggle to distinguish semantic similarity from geographic validity. This is especially critical in natural hazard management domains where geographic granularity (i.e., town vs. city vs. state) is significant for decision-making, as responses valid in one municipality may not transfer to another. In such domains, a confidently wrong answer carries greater risk than abstaining. We present GeoRisk-RAG, a novel hierarchy-aware framework that addresses this geographic-validity gap through selective answering. This framework explicitly estimates geographic applicability using a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)-based distance for context retrieval before response generation. Experiments on a novel held-out wildfire-related question-answering (QA) dataset show that GeoRisk-RAG significantly reduces false confidence rates for location-dependent questions, lowering the rate to 0.009 compared with ~0.090 for standard semantic similarity and reranking baselines, while consistently achieving higher human preference alignment. This work provides a more comprehensive assessment of end-to-end RAG pipelines by integrating geographic validity and selective-answering behavior for safer decision-making in geospatial domains.

AI.tldr: GeoRisk-RAG is a hierarchy-aware framework that uses a DAG-based geographic distance for context retrieval to address the gap between semantic similarity and geographic validity in LLM-generated answers, reducing false confidence rates from ~0.090 to 0.009 for location-dependent questions in natural hazard management.
AI.motivation: Existing methods for improving LLM reliability (RAG, knowledge-graph augmentation, reinforcement learning) measure reliability via semantic similarity and faithfulness but fail to distinguish semantic similarity from geographic validity. This is critical in natural hazard management, where geographic granularity (town vs. city vs. state) matters for decision-making, and a confidently wrong answer is more dangerous than abstaining.
AI.method: GeoRisk-RAG employs a selective-answering framework that explicitly estimates geographic applicability using a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)-based distance during context retrieval before response generation. This allows the system to determine whether a retrieved context is geographically relevant to the query before producing an answer.
AI.result: On a novel held-out wildfire-related QA dataset, GeoRisk-RAG reduced false confidence rates for location-dependent questions to 0.009 compared to ~0.090 for standard semantic similarity and reranking baselines, while consistently achieving higher human preference alignment.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a more comprehensive assessment of end-to-end RAG pipelines by integrating geographic validity and selective-answering behavior, enabling safer decision-making in geospatial domains.

title: Enrich-Retrieve-Rank: Scaling Capability Discovery Beyond In-Context Routing
summary: Agent ecosystems now include thousands of MATS components (Models, Agents, Tools, and Skills), yet their discovery still relies on in-context routing. These systems read a registry (names, hints, or descriptions, as context budget permits), pick a candidate, invoke it, and retry on failure. This pattern degrades with scale, and registries are growing fast. We recast capability discovery as search over a registry by defining an offline enrichment step that turns sparse metadata into searchable profiles, and an online retrieve-then-rank pipeline that returns a ranked shortlist without invoking any candidates online. We show that from N=10 to 7,278 capabilities, in-context routing's top-1 accuracy (Match@1) collapses (0.85 to 0.12), while retrieve-then-rank degrades more gently (0.81 to 0.39) because its reranker still ranks the right capability first 0.70-0.87 of the time once retrieval finds it. In the Nova Micro sweep, the crossover is around N=500. We compare against two in-context baselines. Full-Ctx puts the whole registry in the prompt and asks the LLM to pick. Search&Pick gives the LLM a search tool to narrow candidates before it picks. At full scale the pipeline leads Search&Pick by 6.5 percentage points (pp) on Match@1 at about half the cost. It reduces cost 70x versus Full-Ctx. We use a fixed configuration (same enrichment, retriever, and scorer weights) across agent, tool, and skill registries. The pipeline runs in production as the default capability-discovery layer of a large-scale multi-agent platform.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the scalability problem of capability discovery in agent ecosystems by proposing a retrieve-then-rank pipeline that outperforms in-context routing. It shows that while in-context routing's top-1 accuracy collapses from 0.85 to 0.12 as the registry grows from N=10 to 7,278 capabilities, the proposed retrieve-then-rank approach degrades more gracefully (0.81 to 0.39), crosses over around N=500, and beats the Search&Pick baseline by 6.5pp at full scale while reducing cost 70x versus Full-Ctx.
AI.motivation: Agent ecosystems now contain thousands of MATS components, but capability discovery still relies on in-context routing where the LLM reads a registry and picks candidates. This pattern degrades significantly with scale as registries grow, requiring a more scalable approach to capability discovery.
AI.method: The paper defines an offline enrichment step that converts sparse metadata into searchable profiles, plus an online retrieve-then-rank pipeline that returns a ranked shortlist of candidates without invoking any candidates online. The pipeline uses a fixed configuration (same enrichment, retriever, and scorer weights) across agent, tool, and skill registries.
AI.result: From N=10 to 7,278 capabilities, in-context routing's Match@1 collapses (0.85 to 0.12), while retrieve-then-rank degrades more gently (0.81 to 0.39) because its reranker ranks the right capability first 0.70-0.87 of the time once retrieval finds it. The crossover is around N=500. At full scale the pipeline leads Search&Pick by 6.5pp on Match@1 at about half the cost, and reduces cost 70x versus Full-Ctx.
AI.conclusion: Retrieve-then-rank is a scalable and cost-effective alternative to in-context routing for capability discovery. The pipeline has been deployed in production as the default capability-discovery layer of a large-scale multi-agent platform, demonstrating its practical viability.

title: Shaping the Evolutionary Dynamics of Robot Morphology via Adaptive Control Learning
summary: Robot co-design via bi-level optimization couples within-lifetime controller learning for fitness evaluation with cross-generational morphological evolution. Prior work has established that well-adapted morphology facilitates faster control learning, a property termed morphological intelligence. Yet how control learning reciprocally shapes morphological evolution remains unexplored. This paper examines both directions for a holistic account of brain-body interplay. We first show that morphological contributions to control learning decouple into two orthogonal dimensions. We formalize the convergence speed as morphological intelligence and identify the performance ceiling as a complementary quantity termed true potential. A concise functional relation is then established to jointly characterize both quantities from individual learning curves, which, when aggregated at the population level, capture evolutionary profiles. Through extensive experiments on simulated voxel-based soft robots, we reveal that premature fitness evaluation systematically underestimates true potential and biases selection towards fast learners. This restricts design space exploration, compromising both optimization efficiency and morphological diversity. Notably, the widely recognized morphological Baldwin effect emerges as an artifact of this bias rather than a general evolutionary tendency. We therefore propose AdaControl, which monitors disproportionate selection for morphological intelligence during evolution and allocates minimally sufficient control learning for unbiased fitness evaluation. With AdaControl, a simple genetic algorithm rivals state-of-the-art generative-model-based co-design methods in discovering diverse high-performing designs while cutting computation by up to 80% versus exhaustive control.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates brain-body co-design in robots via bi-level optimization, decomposing morphological contributions to control learning into two orthogonal dimensions: morphological intelligence (convergence speed) and true potential (performance ceiling). It shows that premature fitness evaluation biases selection toward fast learners, underestimates true potential, and restricts design space exploration. The paper proposes AdaControl, which adaptively allocates minimal control learning for unbiased fitness evaluation, enabling a simple genetic algorithm to rival state-of-the-art generative co-design methods while cutting computation by up to 80%.
AI.motivation: While prior work established that well-adapted morphology facilitates faster control learning (morphological intelligence), the reciprocal question—how control learning shapes morphological evolution—remains unexplored. This paper aims to provide a holistic account of brain-body interplay by examining both directions.
AI.method: The authors formalize two orthogonal dimensions (morphological intelligence for convergence speed and true potential for performance ceiling), establish a functional relation characterizing both from individual learning curves, and aggregate these at the population level. They then propose AdaControl, which monitors disproportionate selection for morphological intelligence and allocates minimally sufficient control learning for unbiased fitness evaluation during evolution.
AI.result: Experiments on simulated voxel-based soft robots show that premature fitness evaluation systematically underestimates true potential and biases selection toward fast learners, restricting design space exploration. The morphological Baldwin effect is revealed to be an artifact of this bias. AdaControl enables a simple genetic algorithm to match state-of-the-art generative-model-based co-design methods in discovering diverse high-performing designs, cutting computation by up to 80% versus exhaustive control.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a holistic understanding of brain-body co-design by showing that premature fitness evaluation introduces systematic bias favoring fast learners over high-potential designs. AdaControl offers a computationally efficient mechanism for unbiased fitness evaluation, demonstrating that careful control allocation can match or exceed more complex generative approaches.
